11.1.title: Vectors - The Basics
11.1.unitTitle: Onboarding + Calc I/II Review + Intro to Vectors

problems.problem: Describe the difference between \(\left( {4, - 1} \right)\) and \(\left\langle {4, - 1} \right\rangle \). Illustrate the difference with a sketch.
problems.answer: \((4,-1)\) is a point; \(\langle 4,-1\rangle\) is a vector.
problems.solution: The notation \((4,-1)\) denotes a fixed point in the plane. The notation \(\langle 4,-1\rangle\) denotes a vector: a directed displacement with components \(4\) in \(x\) and \(-1\) in \(y\). The vector has no fixed location: drawn from the origin it ends at \((4,-1)\), but drawn from \((1,1)\) it ends at \((5,0)\). A sketch shows the point as a single dot at \((4,-1)\) and the vector as an arrow with those components drawn from any chosen tail.

problems.problem: The line segment from \(\left( { - 9,2} \right)\) to \(\left( {4, - 1} \right)\).
problems.solution: The vector from \(P=(-9,2)\) to \(Q=(4,-1)\) is head minus tail: \[ \vec{PQ}=\langle 4-(-9),\,-1-2\rangle=\langle 13,-3\rangle. \]

problems.problem: The line segment from \(\left( {4,5,6} \right)\) to \(\left( {4,6,6} \right)\).
problems.solution: Subtract tail from head: \[ \langle 4-4,\,6-5,\,6-6\rangle=\langle 0,1,0\rangle. \]

problems.problem: The position vector for \(\left( { - 3,2,10} \right)\).
problems.solution: The position vector for \(P\) is the vector from the origin to \(P\), with components equal to the coordinates of \(P\): \[ \vec r=\langle -3,2,10\rangle. \]

problems.problem: The position vector for \(\displaystyle \left( {\frac{1}{2}, - \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{2}} \right)\).
problems.solution: The position vector has components equal to the point's coordinates: \[ \vec r=\left\langle \tfrac{1}{2},-\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right\rangle. \] Note this is already a unit vector since \((1/2)^2+(\sqrt{3}/2)^2=1\).

problems.problem: The vector \(\vec v = \left\langle {6, - 4,0} \right\rangle \) starts at the point \(P = \left( { - 2,5, - 1} \right)\). At what point does the vector end?
Given \(\vec a = 3\vec i - 9\vec j\) and \(\vec b = - 6\vec i + \vec j\) compute each of the following. \(10\vec b\) \(14\vec a + 20\vec b\) \(\left\| {8\vec b - \frac{1}{3}\vec a} \right\|\)
problems.solution: \[ 10\vec b=10\langle -6,1\rangle=\langle -60,10\rangle. \] \[ 14\vec a+20\vec b=\langle 42,-126\rangle+\langle -120,20\rangle=\langle -78,-106\rangle. \] \[ 8\vec b-\tfrac{1}{3}\vec a=\langle -48,8\rangle-\langle 1,-3\rangle=\langle -49,11\rangle, \] so \(\|8\vec b-\tfrac{1}{3}\vec a\|=\sqrt{49^2+11^2}=\sqrt{2522}\).

problems.problem: Given \(\vec u = \left\langle {0,4, - 1} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec v = \left\langle {6, - 2, - 7} \right\rangle \) compute each of the following. \(\frac{3}{4}\vec u\) \( - 3\vec u - 7\vec v\) \(\left\| {\vec v + 10\vec u} \right\|\)
problems.solution: \[ \tfrac{3}{4}\vec u=\left\langle 0,3,-\tfrac{3}{4}\right\rangle. \] \[ -3\vec u-7\vec v=\langle 0,-12,3\rangle+\langle -42,14,49\rangle=\langle -42,2,52\rangle. \] \[ \vec v+10\vec u=\langle 6,-2,-7\rangle+\langle 0,40,-10\rangle=\langle 6,38,-17\rangle, \] \(\|\cdot\|=\sqrt{36+1444+289}=\sqrt{1769}\).

problems.problem: Given \(\vec p = \left\langle {3, - 1, - 2} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec q = - \frac{1}{3}\vec i - \frac{1}{2}\vec k\) compute each of the following. \(2\vec p\) \(9\vec q - 2\vec p\) \(\left\| {8\vec p - 12\vec q} \right\|\)
problems.solution: With \(\vec q=\langle -\tfrac{1}{3},0,-\tfrac{1}{2}\rangle\): \[ 2\vec p=\langle 6,-2,-4\rangle. \] \[ 9\vec q-2\vec p=\langle -3,0,-\tfrac{9}{2}\rangle-\langle 6,-2,-4\rangle=\langle -9,2,-\tfrac{1}{2}\rangle. \] \[ 8\vec p-12\vec q=\langle 24,-8,-16\rangle-\langle -4,0,-6\rangle=\langle 28,-8,-10\rangle, \] \(\|\cdot\|=\sqrt{784+64+100}=\sqrt{948}=2\sqrt{237}\).

problems.problem: Find a unit vector that points in the same direction as \(\vec a = \left\langle {10, - 3,8, - 2} \right\rangle \).
problems.solution: \[ \|\vec a\|=\sqrt{100+9+64+4}=\sqrt{177},\qquad \hat u=\frac{\vec a}{\|\vec a\|}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{177}}\langle 10,-3,8,-2\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Find a unit vector that points in the same direction as \(\vec w = - \vec i - 6\vec j\).
problems.solution: \[ \|\vec w\|=\sqrt{1+36}=\sqrt{37},\qquad \hat u=\frac{\vec w}{\|\vec w\|}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{37}}\langle -1,-6\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Find a unit vector that points in the opposite direction as \(\vec c = 2\vec i + 7\vec j - 5\vec k\).
problems.solution: For the opposite direction, negate the unit vector. \[ \|\vec c\|=\sqrt{4+49+25}=\sqrt{78}, \] \[ \hat u=-\frac{\vec c}{\|\vec c\|}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{78}}\langle -2,-7,5\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Find a unit vector that points in the opposite direction as \(\vec b = \left\langle {0, - 3, - 11} \right\rangle \).
problems.solution: \[ \|\vec b\|=\sqrt{0+9+121}=\sqrt{130}, \] \[ \hat u=-\frac{\vec b}{\|\vec b\|}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{130}}\langle 0,3,11\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Find a vector that points in the same direction as \(\vec p = 2\vec i - 3\vec j + \vec k\) with a magnitude of \(\frac{1}{2}\).
problems.solution: \[ \|\vec p\|=\sqrt{4+9+1}=\sqrt{14}, \] then scale the unit vector by \(\tfrac{1}{2}\): \[ \tfrac{1}{2}\,\frac{\vec p}{\|\vec p\|}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{14}}\langle 2,-3,1\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Find a vector that points in the opposite direction as \(\vec a = \left\langle { - 3, - 14,2} \right\rangle \) with a magnitude of 32.
problems.solution: \[ \|\vec a\|=\sqrt{9+196+4}=\sqrt{209}, \] then negate and scale to magnitude \(32\): \[ -32\,\frac{\vec a}{\|\vec a\|}=\frac{32}{\sqrt{209}}\langle 3,14,-2\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Find a vector that points in the same direction as \(\vec b = - 3\vec i + 2\vec k\) with a magnitude that is \(\frac{1}{{10}}\) the magnitude of \(\vec b\).
problems.solution: A vector in the same direction with \(\tfrac{1}{10}\) the magnitude is just \(\tfrac{1}{10}\vec b\): \[ \tfrac{1}{10}\langle -3,0,2\rangle=\left\langle -\tfrac{3}{10},0,\tfrac{1}{5}\right\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Determine if \(\vec p = 8\vec i - 3\vec j\) and \(\vec q = 16\vec i - 6\vec j\) are parallel vectors.
problems.solution: Two vectors are parallel iff one is a scalar multiple of the other. Here \(\vec q=\langle 16,-6\rangle=2\langle 8,-3\rangle=2\vec p\), so they are parallel.

problems.problem: Determine if \(\vec v = \left\langle {1,0, - 4} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec w = \left\langle {9,3,1} \right\rangle \) are parallel vectors.
problems.solution: For \(\vec w=k\vec v\) we would need \(9=k\), \(3=0\cdot k\), and \(1=-4k\). The middle equation forces \(3=0\), which is impossible.

problems.problem: Determine if \(\vec a = 10\vec i + 8\vec j + 20\vec k\) and \(b = \left\langle { - 35, - 28,70} \right\rangle \) are parallel vectors.
problems.solution: Check ratios: \(-35/10=-7/2\) and \(-28/8=-7/2\), but \(70/20=7/2\). The third ratio has the opposite sign, so \(\vec b\) is not a scalar multiple of \(\vec a\).

problems.problem: Prove the property : \(\vec u + \left( {\vec v + \vec w} \right) = \left( {\vec u + \vec v} \right) + \vec w\).
problems.solution: Componentwise, by associativity of real-number addition: \[ [\vec u+(\vec v+\vec w)]_i=u_i+(v_i+w_i)=(u_i+v_i)+w_i=[(\vec u+\vec v)+\vec w]_i. \] Equality of all components gives \(\vec u+(\vec v+\vec w)=(\vec u+\vec v)+\vec w\).

problems.problem: Prove the property : \(\vec v + \vec 0 = \vec v\).
problems.solution: With \(\vec 0\) the zero vector, componentwise addition gives \((\vec v+\vec 0)_i=v_i+0=v_i\), so \(\vec v+\vec 0=\vec v\).

problems.problem: Prove the property : \(1\vec v = \vec v\).
problems.solution: Scalar multiplication multiplies each component, so \((1\vec v)_i=1\cdot v_i=v_i\); hence \(1\vec v=\vec v\).

problems.problem: Prove the property : \(\left( {a + b} \right)\vec v = a\vec v + b\vec v\).
problems.solution: By distributivity of real numbers, applied componentwise: \[ ((a+b)\vec v)_i=(a+b)v_i=av_i+bv_i=(a\vec v+b\vec v)_i, \] so \((a+b)\vec v=a\vec v+b\vec v\).

problems.problem: Given \(\vec a = \left\langle {8,5} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec b = \left\langle { - 3,6} \right\rangle \) compute each of the following. \(6\vec a\) \(7\vec b - 2\vec a\) \(\left\| {10\vec a + 3\vec b} \right\|\)
problems.solution: \[ 6\vec a=\langle 48,30\rangle. \] \[ 7\vec b-2\vec a=\langle -21,42\rangle-\langle 16,10\rangle=\langle -37,32\rangle. \] \[ 10\vec a+3\vec b=\langle 80,50\rangle+\langle -9,18\rangle=\langle 71,68\rangle, \] \(\|\cdot\|=\sqrt{5041+4624}=\sqrt{9665}\).

problems.problem: Given \(\vec u = 8\vec i - \vec j + 3\vec k\) and \(\vec v = 7\vec j - 4\vec k\) compute each of the following. \( - 3\vec v\) \(12\vec u + \vec v\) \(\left\| { - 9\vec v - 2\vec u} \right\|\)
problems.solution: With \(\vec u=\langle 8,-1,3\rangle\), \(\vec v=\langle 0,7,-4\rangle\): \[ -3\vec v=\langle 0,-21,12\rangle. \] \[ 12\vec u+\vec v=\langle 96,-12,36\rangle+\langle 0,7,-4\rangle=\langle 96,-5,32\rangle. \] \[ -9\vec v-2\vec u=\langle 0,-63,36\rangle-\langle 16,-2,6\rangle=\langle -16,-61,30\rangle, \] \(\|\cdot\|=\sqrt{256+3721+900}=\sqrt{4877}\).

problems.problem: Find a unit vector that points in the same direction as \(\vec q = \vec i + 3\vec j + 9\vec k\).
problems.solution: \[ \|\vec q\|=\sqrt{1+9+81}=\sqrt{91},\qquad \hat u=\frac{1}{\sqrt{91}}\langle 1,3,9\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Find a vector that points in the same direction as \(\vec c = \left\langle { - 1,4} \right\rangle \) with a magnitude of 10.
problems.solution: \[ \|\vec c\|=\sqrt{1+16}=\sqrt{17},\qquad 10\,\frac{\vec c}{\|\vec c\|}=\frac{10}{\sqrt{17}}\langle -1,4\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Determine if \(\vec a = \left\langle {3, - 5,1} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec b = \left\langle {6, - 2,2} \right\rangle \) are parallel vectors.
problems.solution: If \(\vec b=k\vec a\) then \(6=3k\) gives \(k=2\), but then the second component would be \(-10\), not \(-2\).

problems.problem: Determine if \(\vec v = 9\vec i - 6\vec j - 24\vec k\) and \(\vec w = \left\langle { - 15,10,40} \right\rangle \) are parallel vectors.
Prove the property : \(\vec v + \vec w = \vec w + \vec v\).
problems.solution: Componentwise, \((\vec v+\vec w)_i=v_i+w_i=w_i+v_i=(\vec w+\vec v)_i\) by commutativity of real addition.

problems.problem: \(\vec a = 9\vec i - 8\vec k\), \(\vec b = \left\langle {3, - 2,1} \right\rangle \)
\(\vec a = \left\langle {4, - 1,0,5} \right\rangle \) , \(\vec b = \left\langle {3,0, - 10,6} \right\rangle \)
\(\vec a = \vec i - 5\vec j - 2\vec k\) , \(\vec b = - 4\vec i + 2\vec j + 8\vec k\)
\(\displaystyle \left\| {\vec a} \right\| = \frac{1}{4}\), \(\displaystyle \left\| {\vec b} \right\| = \frac{9}{4}\) and the angle between the two vectors is \(\theta = \pi \).
problems.solution: Use \(\vec a\cdot\vec b=\|\vec a\|\|\vec b\|\cos\theta\): \[ \vec a\cdot\vec b=\tfrac{1}{4}\cdot\tfrac{9}{4}\cos\pi=\tfrac{9}{16}\cdot(-1)=-\tfrac{9}{16}. \]

problems.problem: \(\displaystyle \left\| {\vec a} \right\| = 24\), \(\left\| {\vec b} \right\| = 9\) and the angle between the two vectors is \(\displaystyle \theta = \frac{{2\pi }}{7}\).
problems.solution: \[ \vec a\cdot\vec b=(24)(9)\cos(2\pi/7)=216\cos(2\pi/7) \] (numerically about \(134.6\)).

problems.problem: \(\vec a = \left\langle {9,5, - 4,2} \right\rangle \), \(\vec b = \left\langle { - 3, - 2,7, - 1} \right\rangle \)
\(\vec a = \left\langle {0,4, - 2} \right\rangle \) , \(\vec b = 2\vec i - \vec j + 7\vec k\)
\(\left\| {\vec a} \right\| = 5\), \(\displaystyle \left\| {\vec b} \right\| = \frac{3}{7}\) and the angle between the two vectors is \(\displaystyle \theta = \frac{\pi }{{12}}\).
problems.solution: \[ \vec a\cdot\vec b=(5)\!\left(\tfrac{3}{7}\right)\cos(\pi/12)=\tfrac{15}{7}\cos(\pi/12). \]

problems.problem: If \(\vec w = \left\langle {1,0, - 3} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec v = \left\langle {6, - 3, - 4} \right\rangle \) compute \(\vec v \times \vec w\).
problems.solution: Using the determinant formula with \(\vec v=\langle 6,-3,-4\rangle\), \(\vec w=\langle 1,0,-3\rangle\): \[ \vec v\times\vec w=\begin{vmatrix}\vec i&\vec j&\vec k\\6&-3&-4\\1&0&-3\end{vmatrix} =\langle (-3)(-3)-(-4)(0),\,-(6(-3)-(-4)(1)),\,6(0)-(-3)(1)\rangle=\langle 9,14,3\rangle. \] (Check: \(\vec v\cdot(\vec v\times\vec w)=54-42-12=0\). ✓)

problems.problem: If \(\vec w = \left\langle {1,0, - 3} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec v = \left\langle {6, - 3, - 4} \right\rangle \) compute \(\vec w \times \vec v\).
problems.solution: By antisymmetry, \(\vec w\times\vec v=-(\vec v\times\vec w)=\langle -9,-14,-3\rangle\) using the previous result.

problems.problem: If \(\vec a = 3\vec i - 2\vec j + 6\vec k\) and \(\vec b = \left\langle {4, - 1, - 6} \right\rangle \) compute \(\vec a \times \vec b\).
problems.solution: With \(\vec a=\langle 3,-2,6\rangle\), \(\vec b=\langle 4,-1,-6\rangle\): \[ \vec a\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\vec i&\vec j&\vec k\\3&-2&6\\4&-1&-6\end{vmatrix} =\langle (-2)(-6)-6(-1),\,-(3(-6)-6(4)),\,3(-1)-(-2)(4)\rangle=\langle 18,42,5\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Find a vector that is orthogonal to the plane containing the points \(P = \left( { - 4,2,6} \right)\), \(Q = \left( { - 3,2,1} \right)\) and \(R = \left( {2, - 1,1} \right)\).
problems.solution: Form two edge vectors and take their cross product. \[ \vec{PQ}=\langle 1,0,-5\rangle,\quad \vec{PR}=\langle 6,-3,-5\rangle. \] \[ \vec{PQ}\times\vec{PR}=\langle 0(-5)-(-5)(-3),\,-(1(-5)-(-5)(6)),\,1(-3)-0(6)\rangle=\langle -15,-25,-3\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Find a vector that is orthogonal to the plane containing the points \(P = \left( { - 1,1,6} \right)\), \(Q = \left( { - 2,3,2} \right)\) and \(R = \left( { - 2,4,5} \right)\).
problems.solution: \[ \vec{PQ}=\langle -1,2,-4\rangle,\quad \vec{PR}=\langle -1,3,-1\rangle. \] \[ \vec{PQ}\times\vec{PR}=\langle 2(-1)-(-4)(3),\,-((-1)(-1)-(-4)(-1)),\,(-1)(3)-2(-1)\rangle=\langle 10,3,-1\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Are the vectors \(\vec u = \left\langle { - 2,4, - 1} \right\rangle \), \(\vec v = \left\langle {5, - 2, - 1} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec w = \left\langle {3,4, - 3} \right\rangle \) are in the same plane?
problems.solution: Three vectors are coplanar iff their scalar triple product is zero. \[ \vec v\times\vec w=\langle (-2)(-3)-(-1)(4),\,(-1)(3)-5(-3),\,5(4)-(-2)(3)\rangle=\langle 10,12,26\rangle. \] \[ \vec u\cdot(\vec v\times\vec w)=(-2)(10)+(4)(12)+(-1)(26)=-20+48-26=2\neq 0. \] So the vectors are not coplanar.

problems.problem: Are the vectors \(\vec u = \left\langle {1, - 1,4} \right\rangle \), \(\vec v = \left\langle {4,2, - 2} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec w = \left\langle { - 5,4, - 17} \right\rangle \) are in the same plane?
problems.solution: Compute the scalar triple product. \[ \vec v\times\vec w=\langle 2(-17)-(-2)(4),\,(-2)(-5)-4(-17),\,4(4)-2(-5)\rangle=\langle -26,78,26\rangle. \] \[ \vec u\cdot(\vec v\times\vec w)=(1)(-26)+(-1)(78)+(4)(26)=-26-78+104=0. \] So the vectors are coplanar.

problems.problem: Determine the value of b so that the vectors \(\vec u = \left\langle {4, - 5,3} \right\rangle \), \(\vec v = \left\langle { - 2,0, - 5} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec w = \left\langle {b, - 1,6} \right\rangle \) are in the same plane.
problems.solution: The vectors are coplanar iff \(\vec u\cdot(\vec v\times\vec w)=0\). \[ \vec v\times\vec w=\langle 0(6)-(-5)(-1),\,-((-2)(6)-(-5)(b)),\,(-2)(-1)-0\cdot b\rangle=\langle -5,\,12-5b,\,2\rangle. \] \[ \vec u\cdot(\vec v\times\vec w)=4(-5)+(-5)(12-5b)+3(2)=-20-60+25b+6=25b-74. \] Setting this equal to zero gives \(b=\tfrac{74}{25}\).

problems.problem: If \(\vec w = \left\langle {3, - 1,5} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec v = \left\langle {0,4, - 2} \right\rangle \) compute \(\vec v \times \vec w\).
problems.solution: With \(\vec v=\langle 0,4,-2\rangle\), \(\vec w=\langle 3,-1,5\rangle\): \[ \vec v\times\vec w=\langle (4)(5)-(-2)(-1),\,-((0)(5)-(-2)(3)),\,(0)(-1)-(4)(3)\rangle=\langle 18,-6,-12\rangle. \]

problems.problem: If \(\vec w = \left\langle {1,6, - 8} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec v = \left\langle {4, - 2, - 1} \right\rangle \) compute \(\vec w \times \vec v\).
Find a vector that is orthogonal to the plane containing the points \(P = \left( {3,0,1} \right)\), \(Q = \left( {4, - 2,1} \right)\) and \(R = \left( {5,3, - 1} \right)\).
problems.solution: \[ \vec{PQ}=\langle 1,-2,0\rangle,\quad \vec{PR}=\langle 2,3,-2\rangle. \] \[ \vec{PQ}\times\vec{PR}=\langle (-2)(-2)-0(3),\,-((1)(-2)-0(2)),\,(1)(3)-(-2)(2)\rangle=\langle 4,2,7\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Are the vectors \(\vec u = \left\langle {1,2, - 4} \right\rangle \), \(\vec v = \left\langle { - 5,3, - 7} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec w = \left\langle { - 1,4,2} \right\rangle \) in the same plane?
Give the projection of \(P = \left( { - 9,1,5} \right)\) onto the three coordinate planes.
problems.solution: To project a point onto a coordinate plane, set the coordinate perpendicular to that plane to \(0\). For \(P=(-9,1,5)\): drop \(z\) for the \(xy\)-plane, drop \(y\) for \(xz\), drop \(x\) for \(yz\). \[ \text{xy: }(-9,1,0),\quad \text{xz: }(-9,0,5),\quad \text{yz: }(0,1,5). \]

problems.problem: Give the projection of \(P = \left( {3, - 2, - 5} \right)\) onto the three coordinate planes.
problems.solution: Set the relevant coordinate to zero: \[ \text{xy: }(3,-2,0),\quad \text{xz: }(3,0,-5),\quad \text{yz: }(0,-2,-5). \]

problems.problem: Which of the points \(P = \left( {8, - 9,3} \right)\) and \(Q = \left( { - 6,4, - 5} \right)\) is closest to the \(xz\)-plane?
problems.solution: Distance from a point \((x,y,z)\) to the \(xz\)-plane is \(|y|\). For \(P\), \(|y|=9\); for \(Q\), \(|y|=4\). \(Q\) is closer.

problems.problem: Which of the points \(P = \left( {8, - 9,3} \right)\) and \(Q = \left( { - 6,4, - 5} \right)\) is closest to the \(xy\)-plane?
problems.solution: Distance to the \(xy\)-plane is \(|z|\). For \(P\), \(|z|=3\); for \(Q\), \(|z|=5\). \(P\) is closer.

problems.problem: Which of the points \(P = \left( {5, - 4,3} \right)\) and \(Q = \left( { - 6,3,9} \right)\) is closest to the \(x\)-axis?
problems.solution: Distance from \((x,y,z)\) to the \(x\)-axis is \(\sqrt{y^2+z^2}\). \[ P:\sqrt{16+9}=5,\qquad Q:\sqrt{9+81}=\sqrt{90}\approx 9.49. \] \(P\) is closer.

problems.problem: Which of the points \(P = \left( {5, - 4,3} \right)\) and \(Q = \left( { - 6,3,9} \right)\) is closest to the \(y\)-axis?
problems.solution: Distance from \((x,y,z)\) to the \(y\)-axis is \(\sqrt{x^2+z^2}\). \[ P:\sqrt{25+9}=\sqrt{34}\approx 5.83,\qquad Q:\sqrt{36+81}=\sqrt{117}\approx 10.82. \] \(P\) is closer.

problems.problem: Give the projection of \(P = \left( {3, - 4,6} \right)\) onto the three coordinate planes.
problems.solution: Set the relevant coordinate to zero: \[ \text{xy: }(3,-4,0),\quad \text{xz: }(3,0,6),\quad \text{yz: }(0,-4,6). \]

problems.problem: Which of the points \(P = \left( {4, - 2,6} \right)\) and \(Q = \left( { - 6, - 3,2} \right)\) is closest to the \(yz\)-plane?
problems.solution: Distance to the \(yz\)-plane is \(|x|\). For \(P\), \(|x|=4\); for \(Q\), \(|x|=6\). \(P\) is closer.

problems.problem: Which of the points \(P = \left( { - 1,4, - 7} \right)\) and \(Q = \left( {6, - 1,5} \right)\) is closest to the \(z\)-axis?
problems.solution: Distance to the \(z\)-axis is \(\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\). \[ P=(-1,4,-7):\;\sqrt{1+16}=\sqrt{17}\approx 4.12,\quad Q=(6,-1,5):\;\sqrt{36+1}=\sqrt{37}\approx 6.08. \] \(P\) is closer.

problems.problem: The line through the points \(\left( {7, - 3,1} \right)\) and \(\left( { - 2,1,4} \right)\).
problems.solution: A line through point \(P_0\) with direction \(\vec d\) is \(\vec r(t)=\vec{r_0}+t\vec d\). Take \(P_0=(7,-3,1)\) and direction \[ \vec d=\langle -2-7,\,1-(-3),\,4-1\rangle=\langle -9,4,3\rangle. \] \[ \vec r(t)=\langle 7,-3,1\rangle+t\langle -9,4,3\rangle=\langle 7-9t,\,-3+4t,\,1+3t\rangle. \]

problems.problem: The line through the point \(\left( {1, - 5,0} \right)\) and parallel to the line given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {8 - 3t, - 10 + 9t, - 1 - t} \right\rangle \).
problems.solution: Use the same direction \(\vec d=\langle -3,9,-1\rangle\) since the lines are parallel. \[ \vec r(t)=\langle 1,-5,0\rangle+t\langle -3,9,-1\rangle=\langle 1-3t,\,-5+9t,\,-t\rangle. \]

problems.problem: The line through the point \(\left( {1, - 7,14} \right)\) and parallel to the line given by \(x = 6t\), \(y = 9\), \(z = 8 - 16t\).
problems.solution: Read direction from the parametric form: \(\vec d=\langle 6,0,-16\rangle\). \[ \vec r(t)=\langle 1,-7,14\rangle+t\langle 6,0,-16\rangle=\langle 1+6t,\,-7,\,14-16t\rangle. \]

problems.problem: The line through the point \(\left( { - 7,2,4} \right)\) and orthogonal to both \(\vec v = \left\langle {0, - 9,1} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec w = 3\vec i + \vec j - 4\vec k\).
problems.solution: A vector orthogonal to both \(\vec v\) and \(\vec w\) is \(\vec v\times\vec w\). With \(\vec v=\langle 0,-9,1\rangle\), \(\vec w=\langle 3,1,-4\rangle\): \[ \vec v\times\vec w=\langle (-9)(-4)-(1)(1),\,(1)(3)-(0)(-4),\,(0)(1)-(-9)(3)\rangle=\langle 35,3,27\rangle. \] \[ \vec r(t)=\langle -7,2,4\rangle+t\langle 35,3,27\rangle. \]

problems.problem: The line through the points \(\left( {2, - 4,1} \right)\) and \(\left( {0,4, - 10} \right)\).
problems.solution: \[ \vec d=\langle 0-2,\,4-(-4),\,-10-1\rangle=\langle -2,8,-11\rangle, \] \[ \vec r(t)=\langle 2,-4,1\rangle+t\langle -2,8,-11\rangle. \]

problems.problem: The line through the point \(\left( { - 7,2,4} \right)\) and parallel to the line given by \(x = 5 - 8t\), \(y = 6 + t\), \(z = - 12t\).
problems.solution: Direction from the parametric form is \(\vec d=\langle -8,1,-12\rangle\). \[ \vec r(t)=\langle -7,2,4\rangle+t\langle -8,1,-12\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Is the line through the points \(\left( {2,0,9} \right)\) and \(\left( { - 4,1, - 5} \right)\) parallel, orthogonal or neither to the line given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {5,1 - 9t, - 8 - 4t} \right\rangle \)?
problems.solution: The first line has direction \(\vec d_1=\langle -4-2,\,1-0,\,-5-9\rangle=\langle -6,1,-14\rangle\); the second has direction \(\vec d_2=\langle 0,-9,-4\rangle\). They are not scalar multiples (the first component would force the scalar to be \(0\)), so not parallel. The dot product is \(0+(-9)+56=47\neq 0\), so not orthogonal.

problems.problem: The plane containing the points \(\left( {6, - 3,1} \right)\), \(\left( {5, - 4,1} \right)\) and \(\left( {3, - 4,0} \right)\).
problems.solution: Use two edge vectors and take their cross product for the normal. With \(A=(6,-3,1)\), \(B=(5,-4,1)\), \(C=(3,-4,0)\): \[ \vec{AB}=\langle -1,-1,0\rangle,\quad \vec{AC}=\langle -3,-1,-1\rangle, \] \[ \vec n=\vec{AB}\times\vec{AC}=\langle 1,-1,-2\rangle. \] Plane: \(1(x-6)-1(y+3)-2(z-1)=0\), so \(x-y-2z=7\).

problems.problem: The plane containing the point \(\left( {1, - 5,8} \right)\) and orthogonal to the line given by \(x = - 3 + 15t\), \(y = 14 - t\), \(z = 9 - 3t\).
problems.solution: The line direction \(\langle 15,-1,-3\rangle\) serves as the plane's normal. \[ 15(x-1)-1(y+5)-3(z-8)=0\;\Rightarrow\;15x-y-3z=-4. \]

problems.problem: The plane containing the point \(\left( { - 8,3,7} \right)\) and parallel to the plane given by \(4x + 8y - 2z = 45\).
problems.solution: Parallel planes share a normal. Use \(\vec n=\langle 4,8,-2\rangle\) (or its scaled form \(\langle 2,4,-1\rangle\)) and the point \((-8,3,7)\): \[ 4(x+8)+8(y-3)-2(z-7)=0\;\Rightarrow\;4x+8y-2z=-22\;\Rightarrow\;2x+4y-z=-11. \]

problems.problem: The plane containing the point \(\left( {2,0, - 8} \right)\) and containing the line given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {8t, - 1 - 5t,4 - t} \right\rangle \).
problems.solution: The line lives in the plane, so its direction \(\vec d=\langle 8,-5,-1\rangle\) lies in the plane. Pick the line's basepoint \((0,-1,4)\) (at \(t=0\)); the vector from there to \((2,0,-8)\) is \(\langle 2,1,-12\rangle\), also in the plane. The normal is the cross product: \[ \vec n=\langle 8,-5,-1\rangle\times\langle 2,1,-12\rangle=\langle 61,94,18\rangle. \] \(61(x-2)+94(y-0)+18(z+8)=0\Rightarrow 61x+94y+18z=-22\).

problems.problem: The plane containing the two lines given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {7 + 5t,2 + t,6t} \right\rangle \) and \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {7 - 6t,2 - 2t,10t} \right\rangle \).
problems.solution: Both lines pass through \((7,2,0)\) (at \(t=0\)), so they intersect there and lie in a common plane. Use their direction vectors: \[ \vec d_1=\langle 5,1,6\rangle,\quad \vec d_2=\langle -6,-2,10\rangle, \] \[ \vec n=\vec d_1\times\vec d_2=\langle 22,-86,-4\rangle = 2\langle 11,-43,-2\rangle. \] Plane: \(11(x-7)-43(y-2)-2z=0\Rightarrow 11x-43y-2z=-9\).

problems.problem: The plane containing the points \(\left( {4, - 3,1} \right)\), \(\left( { - 3, - 1,1} \right)\) and \(\left( {4, - 2,8} \right)\).
problems.solution: With \(A=(4,-3,1)\), \(B=(-3,-1,1)\), \(C=(4,-2,8)\): \[ \vec{AB}=\langle -7,2,0\rangle,\;\vec{AC}=\langle 0,1,7\rangle,\;\vec n=\vec{AB}\times\vec{AC}=\langle 14,49,-7\rangle=7\langle 2,7,-1\rangle. \] \(2(x-4)+7(y+3)-1(z-1)=0\Rightarrow 2x+7y-z=-14\).

problems.problem: The plane containing the point \(\left( {3,0, - 4} \right)\) and orthogonal to the line given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {12 - t,1 + 8t,4 + 6t} \right\rangle \).
problems.solution: The line direction is the plane's normal: \(\vec n=\langle -1,8,6\rangle\). \[ -1(x-3)+8(y-0)+6(z+4)=0\;\Rightarrow\;-x+8y+6z=-27. \]

problems.problem: The plane containing the point \(\left( { - 8,3,7} \right)\) and parallel to the plane given by \(4x + 8y - 2z = 45\).
problems.solution: Same setup as before: parallel planes share a normal. Using \(\vec n=\langle 2,4,-1\rangle\) and \((-8,3,7)\): \[ 2(x+8)+4(y-3)-(z-7)=0\;\Rightarrow\;2x+4y-z=-11. \]

problems.problem: Find the domain of the given vector function. \(\displaystyle \vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {\frac{1}{{{t^2} - 1}},\frac{1}{{t + 3}},\frac{1}{{t - 6}}} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution:
Each component is a rational function, so we just need each denominator to be nonzero. The first denominator \( t^2-1=(t-1)(t+1) \) is zero at \( t=\pm 1 \); the second is zero at \( t=-3 \); the third at \( t=6 \). Intersecting these constraints gives the domain \[ \{t\in\mathbb{R} : t
eq -3,\ t
eq -1,\ t
eq 1,\ t
eq 6\}. \]

problems.problem: Find the domain of the given vector function. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {\sqrt t ,\sqrt {t + 1} ,\sqrt {t + 2} } \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Each square root requires its radicand to be nonnegative: \( t\ge 0 \), \( t\ge -1 \), and \( t\ge -2 \). The most restrictive condition is \( t\ge 0 \), so the domain is \[ \{t\in\mathbb{R} : t\ge 0\}. \]

problems.problem: Find the domain of the given vector function. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {\ln \left( {t + 7} \right),\ln \left( {t - 3} \right)} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Each logarithm requires a positive argument: \( t+7>0 \) gives \( t>-7 \), and \( t-3>0 \) gives \( t>3 \). The intersection is \[ \{t\in\mathbb{R} : t>3\}. \]

problems.problem: Find the domain of the given vector function. \(\displaystyle \vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {{t^2} + 1,\frac{1}{{t + 2}},\sqrt {t + 4} } \right\rangle \)
problems.solution:
The polynomial \( t^2+1 \) is defined everywhere. The rational component requires \( t+2
eq 0 \), i.e. \( t
eq -2 \). The square root requires \( t+4\ge 0 \), i.e. \( t\ge -4 \). Intersecting gives \[ \{t\in\mathbb{R} : t\ge -4 	ext{ and } t
eq -2\}. \]

problems.problem: Find the domain of the given vector function. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {\ln \left( {4 - {t^2}} \right),\sqrt {t + 1} } \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: The logarithm requires \( 4-t^2>0 \), i.e. \( -2<t<2 \). The square root requires \( t+1\ge 0 \), i.e. \( t\ge -1 \). Intersecting these intervals gives \[ \{t\in\mathbb{R} : -1 \le t < 2\}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\mathop {\lim }\limits_{t \to 0} \left( {\cos \left( {2t} \right)\,\vec i - {{\bf{e}}^{4 - t}}\vec j + \left( {{t^2} + 3t - 9} \right)\vec k} \right)\)
problems.solution: Each component is continuous at \( t=0 \), so we just plug in. \[ \cos(0)=1,\qquad e^{4-0}=e^{4},\qquad 0^2+3(0)-9=-9. \] The limit is \( \langle 1,\ -e^{4},\ -9 \rangle \).

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{t \to 4} \left\langle {\frac{{t - 4}}{{{t^2} - 3t - 4}},\frac{{{t^2} - 4t}}{{16 - {t^2}}}} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Both components are \( \tfrac{0}{0} \) at \( t=4 \), so factor and cancel. \[ \frac{t-4}{t^2-3t-4} = \frac{t-4}{(t-4)(t+1)} = \frac{1}{t+1} \to \frac{1}{5}. \] For the second, \( 16-t^2 = -(t-4)(t+4) \), so \[ \frac{t^2-4t}{16-t^2} = \frac{t(t-4)}{-(t-4)(t+4)} = -\frac{t}{t+4} \to -\frac{4}{8} = -\frac{1}{2}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{t \to 0} \left\langle {\frac{{\sin \left( t \right)}}{{2t}},\frac{{1 - \cos \left( t \right)}}{t}, - 3} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Use the standard limits \( \frac{\sin t}{t}\to 1 \) and \( \frac{1-\cos t}{t}\to 0 \) as \( t\to 0 \). \[ \frac{\sin t}{2t} = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\sin t}{t} \to \frac{1}{2}, \qquad \frac{1-\cos t}{t}\to 0. \] The third component is the constant \( -3 \), so the limit is \( \langle \tfrac{1}{2},\ 0,\ -3\rangle \).

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{t \to - 8} \left( {\frac{{{{\bf{e}}^{t{\,^2} - \,64}} - 1}}{{t + 8}}\,\vec i + \frac{{\sin \left( {t + 8} \right)}}{{t + 8}}\vec j - \vec k} \right)\)
problems.solution: For the \( \vec i \) component, write \( t^2-64=(t-8)(t+8) \) and let \( u=t^2-64\to 0 \): \[ \frac{e^{t^2-64}-1}{t+8} = \frac{e^{u}-1}{u}\cdot\frac{u}{t+8} = \frac{e^{u}-1}{u}\cdot(t-8) \to 1\cdot(-16) = -16. \] For the \( \vec j \) component, \( \frac{\sin(t+8)}{t+8}\to 1 \) by the standard sine limit. The \( \vec k \) component is the constant \( -1 \).

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{t \to - \infty } \left\langle {\frac{{5{t^2} - 8t + 1}}{{12 + 5{t^2}}},\frac{{2 + {t^3}}}{{1 + {t^2} + {t^4}}}} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Both components are rational, so compare the highest powers of \( t \). \[ \frac{5t^2-8t+1}{12+5t^2} \to \frac{5}{5} = 1, \qquad \frac{2+t^3}{1+t^2+t^4} \to 0, \] since the numerator of the second component has degree \( 3 \) and the denominator has degree \( 4 \).

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{t \to \infty } \left\langle {\ln \left( {1 - \frac{4}{t}} \right),{{\bf{e}}^{\frac{1}{{t{\,^2}}}}},2} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: As \( t\to\infty \), \( \tfrac{4}{t}\to 0 \) so \( \ln(1-\tfrac{4}{t})\to \ln 1 = 0 \). Likewise \( \tfrac{1}{t^2}\to 0 \), so \( e^{1/t^2}\to e^{0}=1 \). The third component is constant. \[ \lim_{t\to\infty}\left\langle \ln(1-\tfrac{4}{t}),\ e^{1/t^2},\ 2 \right\rangle = \langle 0,\ 1,\ 2\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{t \to 1} \left\langle {{{\bf{e}}^{t - 1}},4t,\frac{{t - 1}}{{{t^2} - 1}}} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: The first two components are continuous at \( t=1 \): \( e^{0}=1 \) and \( 4(1)=4 \). The third is \( \tfrac{0}{0} \), so factor: \[ \frac{t-1}{t^2-1} = \frac{t-1}{(t-1)(t+1)} = \frac{1}{t+1} \to \frac{1}{2}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{t \to - 2} \left( {\frac{{1 - {{\bf{e}}^{t + 2}}}}{{{t^2} + t - 2}}\vec i + \vec j + \left( {{t^2} + 6t} \right)\vec k} \right)\)
problems.solution: Set \( u=t+2\to 0 \). Then \( t^2+t-2=(t+2)(t-1) \), and using \( \frac{e^{u}-1}{u}\to 1 \), \[ \frac{1-e^{t+2}}{t^2+t-2} = -\frac{e^{u}-1}{u}\cdot\frac{1}{t-1} \to -1\cdot\frac{1}{-3} = \frac{1}{3}. \] The \( \vec j \) component is the constant \( 1 \), and the \( \vec k \) component evaluates to \( (-2)^2+6(-2)=4-12=-8 \).

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{t \to \infty } \left\langle {\frac{1}{{{t^2}}},\frac{{2{t^2}}}{{1 - t - {t^2}}},{{\bf{e}}^{ - t}}} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: As \( t\to\infty \), \( \tfrac{1}{t^2}\to 0 \) and \( e^{-t}\to 0 \). For the middle component, divide top and bottom by \( t^2 \): \[ \frac{2t^2}{1-t-t^2} = \frac{2}{\tfrac{1}{t^2}-\tfrac{1}{t}-1} \to \frac{2}{-1} = -2. \]

12.8.title: Tangent, Normal and Binormal Vectors
12.8.unitTitle: Tangent, Normal, Arc Length, Curvature & Motion

problems.problem: Find the unit tangent vector for the given vector function. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = {t^2}\,\vec i - \cos \left( {8t} \right)\vec j + \sin \left( {8t} \right)\vec k\)
problems.solution: Differentiate component-wise: \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \langle 2t,\ 8\sin(8t),\ 8\cos(8t)\rangle \). Then \[ |\vec r\,\prime (t)|^2 = 4t^2 + 64\sin^2(8t) + 64\cos^2(8t) = 4t^2 + 64, \] so \( |\vec r\,\prime (t)| = 2\sqrt{t^2+16} \). Dividing gives \[ \vec T(t) = \frac{\langle 2t,\ 8\sin(8t),\ 8\cos(8t)\rangle}{2\sqrt{t^2+16}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{t^2+16}}\langle t,\ 4\sin(8t),\ 4\cos(8t)\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Find the unit tangent vector for the given vector function. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {8t,2 - {t^6},{t^4}} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Differentiate: \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \langle 8,\ -6t^{5},\ 4t^{3}\rangle \). Its magnitude is \[ |\vec r\,\prime (t)| = \sqrt{64+36t^{10}+16t^{6}} = 2\sqrt{16+9t^{10}+4t^{6}}. \] The unit tangent is therefore \[ \vec T(t) = \frac{\langle 8,\ -6t^{5},\ 4t^{3}\rangle}{2\sqrt{16+9t^{10}+4t^{6}}} = \frac{\langle 4,\ -3t^{5},\ 2t^{3}\rangle}{\sqrt{16+9t^{10}+4t^{6}}}. \]

problems.problem: Find the unit tangent vector for the given vector function. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {\ln \left( {6t} \right),{{\bf{e}}^{1 - t}},5t} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Differentiate: \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \left\langle \tfrac{1}{t},\ -e^{1-t},\ 5\right\rangle \). Its magnitude is \[ |\vec r\,\prime (t)| = \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{t^{2}}+e^{2-2t}+25}. \] Dividing gives \[ \vec T(t) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1/t^{2}+e^{2-2t}+25}}\left\langle \tfrac{1}{t},\ -e^{1-t},\ 5\right\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Find the unit tangent vector for the given vector function. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {{t^2} + 1,3 - t,{t^3}} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Differentiate: \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \langle 2t,\ -1,\ 3t^{2}\rangle \). Then \[ |\vec r\,\prime (t)| = \sqrt{4t^{2}+1+9t^{4}}. \] The unit tangent is \[ \vec T(t) = \frac{\langle 2t,\ -1,\ 3t^{2}\rangle}{\sqrt{9t^{4}+4t^{2}+1}}. \]

problems.problem: Find the unit tangent vector for the given vector function. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = t{{\bf{e}}^{2t}}\,\vec i + \left( {2 - {t^2}} \right)\vec j - {{\bf{e}}^{2t}}\vec k\)
problems.solution: Use the product rule on the first component: \( \tfrac{d}{dt}[t e^{2t}] = e^{2t}+2te^{2t} = e^{2t}(1+2t) \). So \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \langle e^{2t}(1+2t),\ -2t,\ -2e^{2t}\rangle \), and \[ |\vec r\,\prime (t)| = \sqrt{e^{4t}(1+2t)^{2}+4t^{2}+4e^{4t}}. \] Therefore \[ \vec T(t) = \frac{\langle e^{2t}(1+2t),\ -2t,\ -2e^{2t}\rangle}{\sqrt{e^{4t}(1+2t)^{2}+4t^{2}+4e^{4t}}}. \]

12.9.title: Arc Length with Vector Functions
12.9.unitTitle: Tangent, Normal, Arc Length, Curvature & Motion

problems.problem: Find the arc length of the given vector function on the given interval. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = 4\cos \left( {2t} \right)\vec i + 3t\,\vec j - 4\sin \left( {2t} \right)\vec k\) from \(0 \le t \le 3\pi \).
problems.solution: Differentiate: \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \langle -8\sin(2t),\ 3,\ -8\cos(2t)\rangle \). \[ |\vec r\,\prime (t)| = \sqrt{64\sin^{2}(2t)+9+64\cos^{2}(2t)} = \sqrt{64+9} = \sqrt{73}, \] a constant. Therefore \[ L = \int_{0}^{3\pi}\sqrt{73}\,dt = 3\pi\sqrt{73}. \]

problems.problem: Find the arc length of the given vector function on the given interval. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {9 - 2t,4 + 2t,\sqrt 2 \,{t^2}} \right\rangle \) from \(0 \le t \le 1\).
problems.solution: Differentiate: \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \langle -2,\ 2,\ 2\sqrt{2}\,t\rangle \), so \[ |\vec r\,\prime (t)| = \sqrt{4+4+8t^{2}} = 2\sqrt{2}\,\sqrt{1+t^{2}}. \] Using the standard antiderivative \( \int\sqrt{1+t^{2}}\,dt = \tfrac{t}{2}\sqrt{1+t^{2}} + \tfrac{1}{2}\ln(t+\sqrt{1+t^{2}}) \), \[ L = 2\sqrt{2}\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{1+t^{2}}\,dt = 2\sqrt{2}\left[\tfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} + \tfrac{1}{2}\ln(1+\sqrt{2})\right] = 2 + \sqrt{2}\,\ln(1+\sqrt{2}). \]

problems.problem: Find the arc length of the given vector function on the given interval. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = 2t\,\vec i + \frac{1}{2}{t^2}\,\vec j + \ln \left( {{t^2}} \right)\vec k\) from \(1 \le t \le 3\).
problems.solution: Note \( \ln(t^{2})=2\ln t \) for \( t>0 \). Then \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \langle 2,\ t,\ 2/t\rangle \), and \[ |\vec r\,\prime (t)|^{2} = 4 + t^{2} + \tfrac{4}{t^{2}} = \left(t+\tfrac{2}{t}\right)^{2}, \] so \( |\vec r\,\prime (t)| = t + \tfrac{2}{t} \) on \( [1,3] \). Thus \[ L = \int_{1}^{3}\left(t+\tfrac{2}{t}\right)dt = \left[\tfrac{t^{2}}{2}+2\ln t\right]_{1}^{3} = \tfrac{9}{2}+2\ln 3 - \tfrac{1}{2} = 4 + 2\ln 3. \]

problems.problem: Find the arc length of the given vector function on the given interval. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left( {3 - 4t} \right)\vec i + 6t\,\vec j - \left( {9 + 2t} \right)\vec k\) from \( - 6 \le t \le 8\).
problems.solution: The curve is a line: \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \langle -4,\ 6,\ -2\rangle \) is constant, with \[ |\vec r\,\prime (t)| = \sqrt{16+36+4} = \sqrt{56} = 2\sqrt{14}. \] The interval has length \( 8-(-6)=14 \), so \[ L = 2\sqrt{14}\cdot 14 = 28\sqrt{14}. \]

problems.problem: Find the arc length of the given vector function on the given interval. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {\frac{1}{3}{t^3},4t,\sqrt 2 {t^2}} \right\rangle \) from \(0 \le t \le 2\).
problems.solution: Differentiate: \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \langle t^{2},\ 4,\ 2\sqrt{2}\,t\rangle \). Then \[ |\vec r\,\prime (t)|^{2} = t^{4} + 16 + 8t^{2} = (t^{2}+4)^{2}, \] so \( |\vec r\,\prime (t)| = t^{2}+4 \). Therefore \[ L = \int_{0}^{2}(t^{2}+4)\,dt = \left[\tfrac{t^{3}}{3}+4t\right]_{0}^{2} = \tfrac{8}{3}+8 = \tfrac{32}{3}. \]

12.10.title: Curvature
12.10.unitTitle: Tangent, Normal, Arc Length, Curvature & Motion

problems.problem: Find the curvature of the given vector function. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {5t,1 - 2t,4{t^{\frac{3}{2}}}} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Compute \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \langle 5,\ -2,\ 6\sqrt{t}\rangle \) and \( \vec r\,\prime\prime (t) = \langle 0,\ 0,\ 3/\sqrt{t}\rangle \). The cross product is \[ \vec r\,\prime \times\vec r\,\prime\prime  = \left\langle -\tfrac{6}{\sqrt{t}},\ -\tfrac{15}{\sqrt{t}},\ 0\right\rangle, \qquad |\vec r\,\prime \times\vec r\,\prime\prime | = \sqrt{\tfrac{36+225}{t}} = \tfrac{\sqrt{261}}{\sqrt{t}}. \] Since \( |\vec r\,\prime (t)|^{2} = 25+4+36t = 29+36t \), the curvature is \[ \kappa(t) = \frac{|\vec r\,\prime \times\vec r\,\prime\prime |}{|\vec r\,\prime |^{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{261}}{\sqrt{t}\,(29+36t)^{3/2}}. \]

problems.problem: Find the curvature of the given vector function. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {6,{{\bf{e}}^{ - 5t}},3t{{\bf{e}}^{ - 5t}}} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Differentiate: \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \langle 0,\ -5e^{-5t},\ e^{-5t}(3-15t)\rangle \) and \( \vec r\,\prime\prime (t) = \langle 0,\ 25e^{-5t},\ e^{-5t}(75t-30)\rangle \). Since both first components vanish, \[ \vec r\,\prime \times\vec r\,\prime\prime  = \langle e^{-10t}\bigl[-5(75t-30) - 25(3-15t)\bigr],\ 0,\ 0\rangle = \langle 75 e^{-10t},\ 0,\ 0\rangle. \] Also \( |\vec r\,\prime (t)|^{2} = e^{-10t}\bigl[25+(3-15t)^{2}\bigr] \). Hence \[ \kappa(t) = \frac{75\,e^{-10t}}{e^{-15t}\bigl[25+(3-15t)^{2}\bigr]^{3/2}} = \frac{75\,e^{5t}}{\bigl[25+(3-15t)^{2}\bigr]^{3/2}}. \]

problems.problem: Find the curvature of the given vector function. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {\cos \left( {\omega t} \right),t,\sin \left( {\omega t} \right)} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Differentiate: \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \langle -\omega\sin(\omega t),\ 1,\ \omega\cos(\omega t)\rangle \) and \( \vec r\,\prime\prime (t) = \langle -\omega^{2}\cos(\omega t),\ 0,\ -\omega^{2}\sin(\omega t)\rangle \). The cross product is \[ \vec r\,\prime \times\vec r\,\prime\prime  = \langle -\omega^{2}\sin(\omega t),\ -\omega^{3},\ \omega^{2}\cos(\omega t)\rangle, \] with magnitude \( \sqrt{\omega^{4}+\omega^{6}}=\omega^{2}\sqrt{1+\omega^{2}} \). Since \( |\vec r\,\prime |^{2} = 1+\omega^{2} \), \[ \kappa = \frac{\omega^{2}\sqrt{1+\omega^{2}}}{(1+\omega^{2})^{3/2}} = \frac{\omega^{2}}{1+\omega^{2}}. \]

problems.problem: Find the curvature of the given vector function. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {\cos \left( {2t} \right), - \sin \left( {2t} \right),4t} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Differentiate: \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \langle -2\sin(2t),\ -2\cos(2t),\ 4\rangle \) and \( \vec r\,\prime\prime (t) = \langle -4\cos(2t),\ 4\sin(2t),\ 0\rangle \). Then \( |\vec r\,\prime |^{2} = 4+16 = 20 \), and \[ \vec r\,\prime \times\vec r\,\prime\prime  = \langle -16\sin(2t),\ -16\cos(2t),\ -8\rangle, \qquad |\vec r\,\prime \times\vec r\,\prime\prime | = \sqrt{256+64} = 8\sqrt{5}. \] So \( \kappa = \dfrac{8\sqrt{5}}{20^{3/2}} = \dfrac{8\sqrt{5}}{40\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{1}{5}. \)

problems.problem: Find the curvature of the given vector function. \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {4t, - {t^2},2{t^3}} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Differentiate: \( \vec r\,\prime (t) = \langle 4,\ -2t,\ 6t^{2}\rangle \) and \( \vec r\,\prime\prime (t) = \langle 0,\ -2,\ 12t\rangle \). The cross product is \[ \vec r\,\prime \times\vec r\,\prime\prime  = \langle -12t^{2},\ -48t,\ -8\rangle, \qquad |\vec r\,\prime \times\vec r\,\prime\prime | = \sqrt{144t^{4}+2304t^{2}+64} = 4\sqrt{9t^{4}+144t^{2}+4}. \] Since \( |\vec r\,\prime (t)|^{2} = 16+4t^{2}+36t^{4} \), \[ \kappa(t) = \frac{4\sqrt{9t^{4}+144t^{2}+4}}{(36t^{4}+4t^{2}+16)^{3/2}}. \]

12.11.title: Velocity and Acceleration
12.11.unitTitle: Tangent, Normal, Arc Length, Curvature & Motion

problems.problem: Determine the position function of the object given the acceleration and initial conditions. An objects acceleration is given by \(\vec a = \cos \left( {2t} \right)\,\vec i + 4{t^3}\,\vec j + 6\sin \left( {3t} \right)\vec k\). The objects initial velocity is \(\vec v\left( 0 \right) = 6\,\vec i + 2\vec j + 7\vec k\) and the objects initial position is \(\vec r\left( 0 \right) = \vec i - 9\vec j + 6\vec k\). Determine the objects velocity and position functions.
problems.solution: Integrate \( \vec a \) once and apply \( \vec v(0)=\langle 6,2,7\rangle \): \[ \vec v(t) = \left\langle \tfrac{1}{2}\sin(2t)+6,\ t^{4}+2,\ -2\cos(3t)+9\right\rangle, \] where the constants come from \( 0+C_{1}=6 \), \( 0+C_{2}=2 \), and \( -2+C_{3}=7 \). Integrating again and applying \( \vec r(0)=\langle 1,-9,6\rangle \) (so \( -\tfrac{1}{4}+D_{1}=1 \) gives \( D_{1}=\tfrac{5}{4} \)) yields \[ \vec r(t) = \left\langle -\tfrac{1}{4}\cos(2t)+6t+\tfrac{5}{4},\ \tfrac{t^{5}}{5}+2t-9,\ -\tfrac{2}{3}\sin(3t)+9t+6\right\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Determine the position function of the object given the acceleration and initial conditions. An objects acceleration is given by \(\vec a = 10t\,\vec i - 6\,\vec j + t\cos \left( t \right)\vec k\). The objects initial velocity is \(\vec v\left( 0 \right) = - \,\vec i + 11\vec j - \vec k\) and the objects initial position is \(\vec r\left( 0 \right) = 4\vec i + \vec j + 10\vec k\). Determine the objects velocity and position functions.
problems.answer: \( \vec v(t)=\langle 5t^{2}-1,\ -6t+11,\ t\sin t+\cos t-2\rangle,\ \ \vec r(t)=\langle \tfrac{5}{3}t^{3}-t+4,\ -3t^{2}+11t+1,\ -t\cos t+2\sin t-2t+10\rangle \)
problems.solution: Integrating \( \vec a \) and using \( \int t\cos t\,dt = t\sin t+\cos t \) by parts gives, after applying \( \vec v(0)=\langle -1,11,-1\rangle \), \[ \vec v(t) = \langle 5t^{2}-1,\ -6t+11,\ t\sin t+\cos t-2\rangle. \] Integrating again, with \( \int t\sin t\,dt = -t\cos t+\sin t \), and applying \( \vec r(0)=\langle 4,1,10\rangle \), \[ \vec r(t) = \langle \tfrac{5}{3}t^{3}-t+4,\ -3t^{2}+11t+1,\ -t\cos t+2\sin t-2t+10\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Determine the tangential and normal components of acceleration for the object whose position is given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {5t,1 - 2t,4{t^{\frac{3}{2}}}} \right\rangle \).
problems.solution: Here \( \vec v = \langle 5,\ -2,\ 6\sqrt{t}\rangle \) and \( \vec a = \langle 0,\ 0,\ 3/\sqrt{t}\rangle \), so \[ \vec v\cdot\vec a = 18,\qquad |\vec v| = \sqrt{29+36t},\qquad |\vec v\times\vec a| = \sqrt{\tfrac{261}{t}}. \] Using \( a_{T} = \dfrac{\vec v\cdot\vec a}{|\vec v|} \) and \( a_{N} = \dfrac{|\vec v\times\vec a|}{|\vec v|} \) gives \[ a_{T} = \frac{18}{\sqrt{29+36t}},\qquad a_{N} = \frac{\sqrt{261}}{\sqrt{t}\,\sqrt{29+36t}}. \]

problems.problem: Determine the tangential and normal components of acceleration for the object whose position is given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {6,{{\bf{e}}^{ - 5t}},3t{{\bf{e}}^{ - 5t}}} \right\rangle \).
problems.solution: With \( \vec v = \langle 0,\ -5e^{-5t},\ e^{-5t}(3-15t)\rangle \) and \( \vec a = \langle 0,\ 25e^{-5t},\ e^{-5t}(75t-30)\rangle \), \[ \vec v\cdot\vec a = e^{-10t}\bigl[-125+(3-15t)(75t-30)\bigr] = -5e^{-10t}\bigl(225t^{2}-135t+43\bigr), \] and \( |\vec v|=e^{-5t}\sqrt{25+(3-15t)^{2}} \). From the curvature computation, \( |\vec v\times\vec a|=75e^{-10t} \). Therefore \[ a_{T} = \frac{\vec v\cdot\vec a}{|\vec v|} = \frac{-5e^{-5t}\bigl(225t^{2}-135t+43\bigr)}{\sqrt{25+(3-15t)^{2}}},\qquad a_{N} = \frac{|\vec v\times\vec a|}{|\vec v|} = \frac{75\,e^{-5t}}{\sqrt{25+(3-15t)^{2}}}. \]

problems.problem: Determine the position function of the object given the acceleration and initial conditions. An objects acceleration is given by \(\vec a = 3t\,\vec i - 4{{\bf{e}}^{ - t}}\,\vec j + 12{t^2}\vec k\). The objects initial velocity is \(\vec v\left( 0 \right) = \vec j - 3\vec k\) and the objects initial position is \(\vec r\left( 0 \right) = - 5\vec i + 2\vec j - 3\vec k\). Determine the objects velocity and position functions.
problems.solution: Integrate \( \vec a = \langle 3t,\ -4e^{-t},\ 12t^{2}\rangle \) once. Applying \( \vec v(0)=\langle 0,1,-3\rangle \) (note \( 4+C_{2}=1 \) gives \( C_{2}=-3 \)) yields \[ \vec v(t) = \left\langle \tfrac{3}{2}t^{2},\ 4e^{-t}-3,\ 4t^{3}-3\right\rangle. \] Integrating again and applying \( \vec r(0)=\langle -5,2,-3\rangle \) (so \( -4+D_{2}=2 \) gives \( D_{2}=6 \)) gives \[ \vec r(t) = \left\langle \tfrac{t^{3}}{2}-5,\ -4e^{-t}-3t+6,\ t^{4}-3t-3\right\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Determine the tangential and normal components of acceleration for the object whose position is given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {\cos \left( {2t} \right), - \sin \left( {2t} \right),4t} \right\rangle \).
problems.solution: Compute \( \vec v=\langle -2\sin(2t),\ -2\cos(2t),\ 4\rangle \) and \( \vec a=\langle -4\cos(2t),\ 4\sin(2t),\ 0\rangle \). Then \[ \vec v\cdot\vec a = 8\sin(2t)\cos(2t) - 8\sin(2t)\cos(2t) + 0 = 0, \] so \( a_{T}=0 \). Since \( |\vec a|=4 \) and \( a_{T}^{2}+a_{N}^{2}=|\vec a|^{2} \), we get \( a_{N}=4 \). (Equivalently, \( |\vec v|=2\sqrt{5} \) and \( |\vec v\times\vec a|=8\sqrt{5} \), giving \( a_{N}=8\sqrt{5}/(2\sqrt{5})=4 \).)

problems.problem: Convert the following equation written in Cartesian coordinates into an equation in Cylindrical coordinates. \(\displaystyle \frac{{x - y}}{{{x^2} + {y^2} + 1}} = xyz\)
problems.solution: Substitute \(x=r\cos\theta\), \(y=r\sin\theta\), and \(x^2+y^2=r^2\): \[ \frac{r\cos\theta-r\sin\theta}{r^2+1}=r^2\cos\theta\sin\theta\,z. \]
\(r=\sqrt{16+1}=\sqrt{17}\); \((-4,-1)\) in quadrant III gives \(\theta=-\pi+\tan^{-1}(1/4)\approx -2.897\) (or equivalently \(\pi+\tan^{-1}(1/4)\approx 3.387\)); \(z=8\).

problems.problem: Convert the following equation written in Cartesian coordinates into an equation in Cylindrical coordinates. \({x^3} + 2{x^2} - 6z = 4 - 2{y^2}\)
problems.solution: Substitute \(x=r\cos\theta\), \(y=r\sin\theta\): \[ r^3\cos^3\theta+2r^2\cos^2\theta-6z=4-2r^2\sin^2\theta. \]

\(\rho=\sqrt{36+4+64}=\sqrt{104}=2\sqrt{26}\approx 10.198\). \(\theta=\tan^{-1}(2/6)=\tan^{-1}(1/3)\approx 0.322\) (quadrant I in \(xy\)). \(\varphi=\cos^{-1}(z/\rho)=\cos^{-1}(-8/\sqrt{104})\approx 2.473\) (the negative \(z\) places it below the \(xy\)-plane, so \(\varphi>\pi/2\)).

problems.problem: Convert the Cylindrical coordinates for the point \(\left( {5,1.294,6} \right)\) into Spherical coordinates.
problems.solution: From cylindrical \((r,\theta,z)=(5,1.294,6)\): \[ \rho=\sqrt{r^2+z^2}=\sqrt{25+36}=\sqrt{61}\approx 7.810. \] \(\theta\) is unchanged. \(\varphi=\cos^{-1}(z/\rho)=\cos^{-1}(6/\sqrt{61})\approx 0.695\).

problems.problem: Convert the following equation written in Cartesian coordinates into an equation in Spherical coordinates. \(\frac{{xz}}{y} = 2 - x\)
problems.solution: Substitute \(x=\rho\sin\varphi\cos\theta\), \(y=\rho\sin\varphi\sin\theta\), \(z=\rho\cos\varphi\): \[ \frac{(\rho\sin\varphi\cos\theta)(\rho\cos\varphi)}{\rho\sin\varphi\sin\theta}=2-\rho\sin\varphi\cos\theta. \] The \(\rho\sin\varphi\) cancels on the left, giving \[ \rho\cos\varphi\cot\theta=2-\rho\sin\varphi\cos\theta. \]
\(\rho=\sqrt{9+16+1}=\sqrt{26}\approx 5.099\). \((3,-4)\) is in quadrant IV, so \(\theta=-\tan^{-1}(4/3)\approx -0.927\). \(\varphi=\cos^{-1}(1/\sqrt{26})\approx 1.373\).

\(\rho=\sqrt{4+1+49}=\sqrt{54}=3\sqrt{6}\approx 7.348\). \((-2,-1)\) is in quadrant III: \(\theta=-\pi+\tan^{-1}(1/2)\approx -2.678\). The negative \(z\) gives \(\varphi=\cos^{-1}(-7/\sqrt{54})\approx 2.832\).

problems.problem: Convert the Cylindrical coordinates for the point \(\left( {2,0.345, - 3} \right)\) into Spherical coordinates.
problems.solution: From cylindrical \((r,\theta,z)=(2,0.345,-3)\): \[ \rho=\sqrt{4+9}=\sqrt{13}\approx 3.606,\quad \theta=0.345,\quad \varphi=\cos^{-1}(-3/\sqrt{13})\approx 2.554. \]

problems.problem: Convert the following equation written in Cartesian coordinates into an equation in Spherical coordinates. \({x^2} + {y^2} = 4x + z - 2\)
problems.solution: Use \(x^2+y^2=\rho^2\sin^2\varphi\), \(x=\rho\sin\varphi\cos\theta\), \(z=\rho\cos\varphi\): \[ \rho^2\sin^2\varphi=4\rho\sin\varphi\cos\theta+\rho\cos\varphi-2. \]

13.1.title: Limits
13.1.unitTitle: Limits, Partial Derivatives & the Chain Rule

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{\left( {x,y,z} \right) \to \left( {2,1,0} \right)} \frac{{\left( {4y - {z^3}} \right){{\bf{e}}^{3x - 6}}}}{{4z - y{x^2}}}\)
problems.solution: The denominator at \((2,1,0)\) is \(4(0) - (1)(2)^2 = -4\), which is nonzero, so the function is continuous there and we substitute directly. The numerator becomes \((4(1) - 0)e^{0} = 4\). \[\lim_{(x,y,z)\to(2,1,0)} \frac{(4y-z^3)e^{3x-6}}{4z - yx^2} = \frac{4}{-4} = -1.\]

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{\left( {x,y} \right) \to \left( {3, - 7} \right)} \frac{{6x - y + xy}}{{2{x^3} + {y^3}}}\)
problems.solution: Both numerator and denominator are polynomials, so the function is continuous at \((3,-7)\) and we evaluate directly. The numerator is \(6(3) - (-7) + (3)(-7) = 18 + 7 - 21 = 4\). The denominator is \(2(27) + (-343) = 54 - 343 = -289\). \[\lim_{(x,y)\to(3,-7)} \frac{6x - y + xy}{2x^3 + y^3} = -\frac{4}{289}.\]

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{\left( {x,y} \right) \to \left( { - 3,4} \right)} \frac{{4{x^2} - xy - 3{y^2}}}{{12{x^2} + 17xy + 6{y^2}}}\)
problems.solution: Direct substitution gives \(0/0\), so we factor. The numerator factors as \((x-y)(4x+3y)\) and the denominator factors as \((3x+2y)(4x+3y)\). The common factor \(4x+3y\) vanishes at \((-3,4)\), but it cancels off the indeterminacy. \[\lim_{(x,y)\to(-3,4)} \frac{4x^2 - xy - 3y^2}{12x^2 + 17xy + 6y^2} = \lim_{(x,y)\to(-3,4)} \frac{x-y}{3x+2y} = \frac{-3-4}{-9+8} = \frac{-7}{-1} = 7.\]

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{\left( {x,y} \right) \to \left( { - 1,10} \right)} \frac{{10{x^2} + 11xy + {y^2}}}{{10{x^2} - 39xy - 4{y^2}}}\)
problems.solution: Direct substitution gives \(0/0\). The numerator factors as \((x+y)(10x+y)\) and the denominator as \((x-4y)(10x+y)\). After cancellation we evaluate. \[\lim_{(x,y)\to(-1,10)} \frac{10x^2 + 11xy + y^2}{10x^2 - 39xy - 4y^2} = \lim_{(x,y)\to(-1,10)} \frac{x+y}{x-4y} = \frac{-1+10}{-1-40} = -\frac{9}{41}.\]

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{\left( {x,y} \right) \to \left( {0,0} \right)} \frac{{2{x^2} + 7{y^2}}}{{4{y^2} + {x^2}}}\)
problems.solution: Both numerator and denominator vanish at \((0,0)\), so we test paths. Along \(y=0\): \(\dfrac{2x^2}{x^2} = 2\). Along \(x=0\): \(\dfrac{7y^2}{4y^2} = \dfrac{7}{4}\). The two path-limits disagree, so the limit does not exist.

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{\left( {x,y} \right) \to \left( {0,0} \right)} \frac{{6\,\,\sqrt[3]{x} - 3{y^{10}}}}{{9{y^{30}} + 2x}}\)
problems.solution: We test paths through the origin. Along \(y=0\): \(\dfrac{6x^{1/3}}{2x} = 3x^{-2/3} \to +\infty\). Along \(x=0\): \(\dfrac{-3y^{10}}{9y^{30}} = -\dfrac{1}{3y^{20}} \to -\infty\). The path-limits diverge in opposite directions, so the limit does not exist.

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{\left( {x,y} \right) \to \left( {0,0} \right)} \frac{{2{x^4}y}}{{{x^8} + 6{y^2}}}\)
problems.solution: Test paths. Along \(y=0\): the expression equals \(0\). Along \(y = x^4\): \[\frac{2x^4 \cdot x^4}{x^8 + 6x^8} = \frac{2x^8}{7x^8} = \frac{2}{7}.\]The two path-limits disagree, so the limit does not exist.

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{\left( {x,y,z} \right) \to \left( { - 1,0,4} \right)} \frac{{{x^3} - z{{\bf{e}}^{2y}}}}{{6x + 2y - 3z}}\)
problems.solution: The denominator at \((-1,0,4)\) is \(-6 + 0 - 12 = -18 \neq 0\), so the function is continuous and we substitute. The numerator is \((-1)^3 - 4e^{0} = -1 - 4 = -5\). \[\lim_{(x,y,z)\to(-1,0,4)} \frac{x^3 - z e^{2y}}{6x + 2y - 3z} = \frac{-5}{-18} = \frac{5}{18}.\]

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{\left( {x,y} \right) \to \left( {2,1} \right)} \frac{{{x^2} - 2xy}}{{{x^2} - 4{y^2}}}\)
problems.solution: Direct substitution gives \(0/0\). Factor: numerator \(= x(x-2y)\), denominator \(= (x-2y)(x+2y)\). After cancelling \(x-2y\): \[\lim_{(x,y)\to(2,1)} \frac{x^2 - 2xy}{x^2 - 4y^2} = \lim_{(x,y)\to(2,1)} \frac{x}{x+2y} = \frac{2}{2+2} = \frac{1}{2}.\]

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{\left( {x,y} \right) \to \left( {0,0} \right)} \frac{{x - 4y}}{{6y + 7x}}\)
problems.solution: Test paths. Along \(y=0\): \(\dfrac{x}{7x} = \dfrac{1}{7}\). Along \(x=0\): \(\dfrac{-4y}{6y} = -\dfrac{2}{3}\). Different path-limits, so the limit does not exist.

problems.problem: Evaluate the given limit. \(\displaystyle \mathop {\lim }\limits_{\left( {x,y} \right) \to \left( {0,0} \right)} \frac{{{x^2} - {y^6}}}{{x{y^3}}}\)
problems.solution: Test paths. Along \(x=y^3\): \(\dfrac{y^6 - y^6}{y^3 \cdot y^3} = 0\). Along \(x=y\): \[\frac{y^2 - y^6}{y \cdot y^3} = \frac{1}{y^2} - y^2 \to +\infty.\]The two path-limits disagree, so the limit does not exist.

13.2.title: Partial Derivatives
13.2.unitTitle: Limits, Partial Derivatives & the Chain Rule

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = {x^3}\sqrt y + 4{z^3}{y^2} - xyz + {x^2} - \sqrt[3]{{{z^5}}}\)
problems.solution: Treat the other variables as constants and apply standard rules. Note \(\sqrt[3]{z^5} = z^{5/3}\), so its derivative in \(z\) is \(\tfrac{5}{3}z^{2/3}\). \[f_x = 3x^2\sqrt{y} - yz + 2x, \qquad f_y = \frac{x^3}{2\sqrt{y}} + 8z^3 y - xz, \qquad f_z = 12 z^2 y^2 - xy - \frac{5}{3}z^{2/3}.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(W\left( {a,b,c,d} \right) = {a^2} + {b^3} - {c^2}{d^4} - 5{a^3}c - {d^6}{b^2}a\)
problems.solution: Differentiate term-by-term, treating the other three letters as constants each time. \[W_a = 2a - 15 a^2 c - d^6 b^2, \quad W_b = 3b^2 - 2 a b d^6, \quad W_c = -2 c d^4 - 5 a^3, \quad W_d = -4 c^2 d^3 - 6 a b^2 d^5.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(\displaystyle A\left( {p,t,u} \right) = \frac{1}{{p\,{t^2}}} - \frac{{{t^3}}}{{{u^2}}} + \frac{{4u\,p}}{{{t^4}}}\)
problems.solution: Rewrite each term with negative exponents: \(A = p^{-1} t^{-2} - t^3 u^{-2} + 4 u p t^{-4}\). Then differentiate. \[A_p = -p^{-2} t^{-2} + 4u t^{-4}, \quad A_t = -2 p^{-1} t^{-3} - 3 t^2 u^{-2} - 16 u p t^{-5}, \quad A_u = 2 t^3 u^{-3} + 4 p t^{-4}.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(g\left( {x,y,z} \right) = \sqrt {{x^2} + {z^{ - 2}}} + \sin \left( {xy - {x^2}} \right)\)
problems.solution: For the radical use the chain rule with \(u = x^2 + z^{-2}\): \(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial v}\sqrt{u} = \dfrac{u_v}{2\sqrt{u}}\). For the sine use the chain rule on \(xy - x^2\). \[g_x = \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2+z^{-2}}} + (y-2x)\cos(xy-x^2),\quad g_y = x\cos(xy-x^2),\quad g_z = -\frac{1}{z^3\sqrt{x^2+z^{-2}}}.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(f\left( {s,t} \right) = \cos \left( {s{{\bf{e}}^{{t^{\,2}}}}} \right) + \cos \left( {s + {{\bf{e}}^{{t^{\,2}}}}} \right)\)
problems.solution: Apply the chain rule to each cosine. The inner function of the first cosine has \(s\)-derivative \(e^{t^2}\) and \(t\)-derivative \(2t s e^{t^2}\); the inner function of the second has \(s\)-derivative \(1\) and \(t\)-derivative \(2t e^{t^2}\). \[f_s = -e^{t^2}\sin(s e^{t^2}) - \sin(s + e^{t^2}),\] \[f_t = -2 t s e^{t^2}\sin(s e^{t^2}) - 2 t e^{t^2}\sin(s + e^{t^2}).\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(\displaystyle f\left( {x,y} \right) = \ln \left( {\frac{y}{x}} \right) + \ln \left( {\frac{1}{{x + y}}} \right) - \ln \left( {\frac{x}{6}} \right)\)
problems.solution: Use log laws to split the function: \(f = \ln y - \ln x - \ln(x+y) - \ln x + \ln 6 = \ln y - 2\ln x - \ln(x+y) + \ln 6.\) Differentiating term-by-term: \[f_x = -\frac{2}{x} - \frac{1}{x+y}, \qquad f_y = \frac{1}{y} - \frac{1}{x+y}.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(\displaystyle A\left( {y,z} \right) = \frac{1}{{y - 4{z^5}}} + \tan \left( {y{z^2} - {y^3}} \right)\)
problems.solution: Differentiate the rational term using \(\dfrac{d}{dv}\dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{u_v}{u^2}\), and the tangent term using \(\dfrac{d}{dv}\tan u = u_v \sec^2 u\). \[A_y = -\frac{1}{(y-4z^5)^2} + (z^2 - 3y^2)\sec^2(yz^2 - y^3),\] \[A_z = \frac{20 z^4}{(y-4z^5)^2} + 2 y z \sec^2(yz^2 - y^3).\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(\displaystyle g\left( {u,v} \right) = \frac{u}{v}\cos \left( {\frac{v}{u}} \right) + 4u - {v^2}u\)
problems.solution: Use the product rule on \((u/v)\cos(v/u)\). For the \(u\)-partial, \((u/v)_u = 1/v\) and the inner derivative of \(v/u\) is \(-v/u^2\). For the \(v\)-partial, \((u/v)_v = -u/v^2\) and the inner derivative of \(v/u\) is \(1/u\). \[g_u = \frac{1}{v}\cos\!\left(\frac{v}{u}\right) + \frac{u}{v}\cdot\sin\!\left(\frac{v}{u}\right)\cdot\frac{v}{u^2} + 4 - v^2 = \frac{1}{v}\cos\!\left(\frac{v}{u}\right) + \frac{1}{u}\sin\!\left(\frac{v}{u}\right) + 4 - v^2.\] \[g_v = -\frac{u}{v^2}\cos\!\left(\frac{v}{u}\right) - \frac{u}{v}\cdot\sin\!\left(\frac{v}{u}\right)\cdot\frac{1}{u} - 2 u v = -\frac{u}{v^2}\cos\!\left(\frac{v}{u}\right) - \frac{1}{v}\sin\!\left(\frac{v}{u}\right) - 2 u v.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(w = \left( {x - y} \right){{\bf{e}}^{4x + {z^{\,6}}}} - \sin \left( {2x + 7z} \right)\sec \left( {y{z^3}} \right)\)
problems.solution: Apply the product rule to each term. For the first term differentiate \((x-y)\) and \(e^{4x+z^6}\) via the chain rule. For the second, recall \(\dfrac{d}{dv}\sec u = u_v\sec u\tan u\). \[w_x = e^{4x+z^6} + 4(x-y)e^{4x+z^6} - 2\cos(2x+7z)\sec(yz^3),\] \[w_y = -e^{4x+z^6} - z^3\sec(yz^3)\tan(yz^3)\sin(2x+7z),\] \[w_z = 6 z^5(x-y)e^{4x+z^6} - 7\cos(2x+7z)\sec(yz^3) - 3 y z^2 \sec(yz^3)\tan(yz^3)\sin(2x+7z).\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(f\left( {u,v,w} \right) = \left( {uw + 4} \right){\sin ^{ - 1}}\left( {{u^2} + {v^2}} \right) - \ln \left( {\frac{{{w^2}}}{{{v^4}}}} \right)\)
problems.solution: Note \(\ln(w^2/v^4) = 2\ln w - 4\ln v\). Use the product rule on \((uw+4)\sin^{-1}(u^2+v^2)\) and the chain rule with \(\dfrac{d}{dv}\sin^{-1}(u) = \dfrac{u_v}{\sqrt{1-u^2}}\). \[f_u = w\sin^{-1}(u^2+v^2) + \frac{2u(uw+4)}{\sqrt{1-(u^2+v^2)^2}},\] \[f_v = \frac{2v(uw+4)}{\sqrt{1-(u^2+v^2)^2}} + \frac{4}{v}, \qquad f_w = u\sin^{-1}(u^2+v^2) - \frac{2}{w}.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(\displaystyle f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = \sin \left( {\frac{z}{{{z^2} + x}}} \right) - \frac{{6{x^2} + y}}{{{y^2} - {z^2}}}\)
problems.solution: For the sine use the quotient rule on the inner function: \(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}\!\left(\dfrac{z}{z^2+x}\right) = -\dfrac{z}{(z^2+x)^2}\) and \(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}\!\left(\dfrac{z}{z^2+x}\right) = \dfrac{(z^2+x) - z(2z)}{(z^2+x)^2} = \dfrac{x - z^2}{(z^2+x)^2}\). For the rational term apply the quotient rule directly. \[f_x = -\frac{z\cos\!\left(\frac{z}{z^2+x}\right)}{(z^2+x)^2} - \frac{12x}{y^2-z^2},\] \[f_y = \frac{12 x^2 y + y^2 + z^2}{(y^2-z^2)^2}, \qquad f_z = \frac{(x-z^2)\cos\!\left(\frac{z}{z^2+x}\right)}{(z^2+x)^2} - \frac{2 z(6 x^2 + y)}{(y^2-z^2)^2}.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(\displaystyle g\left( {s,t,p} \right) = \frac{{{p^3}{t^2}}}{{{s^2} + 1}} + \frac{{\left( {4s - 1} \right){t^2}}}{{6 - s}}\)
problems.solution: Use the quotient rule on each term. For the second term, the \(s\)-derivative numerator is \(4(6-s) - (4s-1)(-1) = 24 - 4s + 4s - 1 = 23\). \[g_s = -\frac{2 s p^3 t^2}{(s^2+1)^2} + \frac{23 t^2}{(6-s)^2},\] \[g_t = \frac{2 p^3 t}{s^2+1} + \frac{2 t(4s-1)}{6-s}, \qquad g_p = \frac{3 p^2 t^2}{s^2+1}.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(f\left( {x,y,z,w} \right) = {x^2}\sin \left( {4y} \right) + {z^3}\left( {6x - y} \right) + {y^4}\)
problems.solution: The function does not contain \(w\), so \(f_w = 0\). The remaining partials follow standard rules. \[f_x = 2 x \sin(4y) + 6 z^3, \quad f_y = 4 x^2 \cos(4y) - z^3 + 4 y^3, \quad f_z = 3 z^2 (6 x - y), \quad f_w = 0.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = 4{x^3}{y^2} - {{\bf{e}}^z}{y^4} + \frac{{{z^3}}}{{{x^2}}} + 4y - {x^{16}}\)
problems.solution: Rewrite \(z^3/x^2 = z^3 x^{-2}\) and differentiate term-by-term. \[f_x = 12 x^2 y^2 - 2 z^3 x^{-3} - 16 x^{15}, \quad f_y = 8 x^3 y - 4 e^z y^3 + 4, \quad f_z = -e^z y^4 + 3 z^2 x^{-2}.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(w = \cos \left( {{x^2} + 2y} \right) - {{\bf{e}}^{4x - {z^{\,4}}y}} + {y^3}\)
problems.solution: Apply the chain rule to the cosine and to the exponential. The inner function \(4x - z^4 y\) has partials \(4\), \(-z^4\), \(-4 z^3 y\). \[w_x = -2 x \sin(x^2 + 2 y) - 4 e^{4x - z^4 y},\] \[w_y = -2 \sin(x^2 + 2 y) + z^4 e^{4x - z^4 y} + 3 y^2, \qquad w_z = 4 y z^3 e^{4x - z^4 y}.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(f\left( {u,v,p,t} \right) = 8{u^2}{t^3}p - \sqrt v \,{p^2}{t^{ - 5}} + 2{u^2}t + 3{p^4} - v\)
problems.solution: Differentiate term-by-term, treating the other three letters as constants. Recall \(\dfrac{d}{dv}\sqrt{v} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{v}}\) and \(\dfrac{d}{dt} t^{-5} = -5 t^{-6}\). \[f_u = 16 u t^3 p + 4 u t, \quad f_v = -\frac{p^2}{2\sqrt{v}\,t^5} - 1,\] \[f_p = 8 u^2 t^3 - \frac{2 \sqrt{v}\, p}{t^5} + 12 p^3, \quad f_t = 24 u^2 t^2 p + \frac{5 \sqrt{v}\, p^2}{t^6} + 2 u^2.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(f\left( {u,v} \right) = {u^2}\sin \left( {u + {v^3}} \right) - \sec \left( {4u} \right){\tan ^{ - 1}}\left( {2v} \right)\)
problems.solution: Use the product rule on each term. Recall \(\dfrac{d}{dv}\sec(4u) = 4\sec(4u)\tan(4u)\) and \(\dfrac{d}{dv}\tan^{-1}(2v) = \dfrac{2}{1+4v^2}\). \[f_u = 2u\sin(u+v^3) + u^2\cos(u+v^3) - 4\sec(4u)\tan(4u)\tan^{-1}(2v),\] \[f_v = 3 u^2 v^2 \cos(u+v^3) - \frac{2\sec(4u)}{1+4v^2}.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(\displaystyle f\left( {x,z} \right) = {{\bf{e}}^{ - x}}\sqrt {{z^4} + {x^2}} - \frac{{2x + 3z}}{{4z - 7x}}\)
problems.solution: Apply the product rule to \(e^{-x}\sqrt{z^4+x^2}\) and the quotient rule to \((2x+3z)/(4z-7x)\). For the rational \(x\)-derivative, the numerator is \(2(4z-7x) - (2x+3z)(-7) = 8z - 14x + 14x + 21z = 29z\). For the \(z\)-derivative, the numerator is \(3(4z-7x) - (2x+3z)(4) = 12z - 21x - 8x - 12z = -29x\). \[f_x = -e^{-x}\sqrt{z^4+x^2} + \frac{x e^{-x}}{\sqrt{z^4+x^2}} - \frac{29 z}{(4z-7x)^2},\] \[f_z = \frac{2 z^3 e^{-x}}{\sqrt{z^4+x^2}} + \frac{29 x}{(4z-7x)^2}.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(g\left( {s,t,v} \right) = {t^2}\ln \left( {s + 2t} \right) - \ln \left( {3v} \right)\left( {{s^3} + {t^2} - 4v} \right)\)
problems.solution: Apply the product rule and chain rule to each term. For \(\ln(s+2t)\), the derivatives are \(\partial_s = 1/(s+2t)\) and \(\partial_t = 2/(s+2t)\). For \(\ln(3v)\), \(\partial_v = 1/v\). \[g_s = \frac{t^2}{s+2t} - 3 s^2 \ln(3v), \qquad g_t = 2 t \ln(s+2t) + \frac{2 t^2}{s+2t} - 2 t \ln(3v),\] \[g_v = -\frac{s^3 + t^2 - 4 v}{v} + 4 \ln(3v).\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(\displaystyle R\left( {x,y} \right) = \frac{{{x^2}}}{{{y^2} + 1}} - \frac{{{y^2}}}{{{x^2} + y}}\)
problems.solution: Apply the quotient rule to each term. For the second term and \(R_x\), the numerator derivative simplifies to \(2 x y^2\) after \(0 \cdot (x^2+y) - y^2 \cdot 2x = -2 x y^2\), giving the sign shown. For \(R_y\), \(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}\!\left(\dfrac{y^2}{x^2+y}\right) = \dfrac{2y(x^2+y) - y^2}{(x^2+y)^2} = \dfrac{2 x^2 y + y^2}{(x^2+y)^2}\). \[R_x = \frac{2x}{y^2+1} + \frac{2 x y^2}{(x^2+y)^2}, \qquad R_y = -\frac{2 x^2 y}{(y^2+1)^2} - \frac{2 x^2 y + y^2}{(x^2+y)^2}.\]

problems.problem: Find all the first-order partial derivatives of the given function. \(\displaystyle z = \frac{{{p^2}\left( {r + 1} \right)}}{{{t^3}}} + pr\,{{\bf{e}}^{2p + 3r + 4t}}\)
problems.solution: Differentiate term-by-term, using the product rule on \(p r e^{2p+3r+4t}\). \[z_p = \frac{2 p(r+1)}{t^3} + r e^{2p+3r+4t} + 2 p r e^{2p+3r+4t},\] \[z_r = \frac{p^2}{t^3} + p e^{2p+3r+4t} + 3 p r e^{2p+3r+4t}, \qquad z_t = -\frac{3 p^2(r+1)}{t^4} + 4 p r e^{2p+3r+4t}.\]

problems.problem: Find \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial x}}\) and \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial y}}\) for the following function. \({x^2}\sin \left( {{y^3}} \right) + x{{\bf{e}}^{3z}} - \cos \left( {{z^2}} \right) = 3y - 6z + 8\)
problems.answer: \(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial x} = -\dfrac{2 x \sin(y^3) + e^{3z}}{3 x e^{3z} + 2 z \sin(z^2) + 6}\), \(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial y} = \dfrac{3 - 3 x^2 y^2 \cos(y^3)}{3 x e^{3z} + 2 z \sin(z^2) + 6}\)
problems.solution: Set \(F(x,y,z) = x^2 \sin(y^3) + x e^{3z} - \cos(z^2) - 3y + 6z - 8\). Then \(\partial z/\partial x = -F_x/F_z\) and \(\partial z/\partial y = -F_y/F_z\). Computing: \(F_x = 2x\sin(y^3) + e^{3z}\), \(F_y = 3 x^2 y^2 \cos(y^3) - 3\), \(F_z = 3 x e^{3z} + 2 z \sin(z^2) + 6\). \[\frac{\partial z}{\partial x} = -\frac{2 x \sin(y^3) + e^{3z}}{3 x e^{3z} + 2 z \sin(z^2) + 6}, \qquad \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} = \frac{3 - 3 x^2 y^2 \cos(y^3)}{3 x e^{3z} + 2 z \sin(z^2) + 6}.\]

13.3.title: Interpretations of Partial Derivatives
13.3.unitTitle: Limits, Partial Derivatives & the Chain Rule

problems.problem: Determine if \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 10 - {x^2} - {y^2}\) is increasing or decreasing at \(\left( {7, - 3} \right)\) if we allow \(x\) to vary and hold \(y\) fixed. we allow \(y\) to vary and hold \(x\) fixed.
problems.solution: The first-order partials are \(f_x = -2x\) and \(f_y = -2y\). Evaluating at \((7,-3)\): \[f_x(7,-3) = -14 < 0, \qquad f_y(7,-3) = 6 > 0.\] So with \(y\) held fixed the function is decreasing, and with \(x\) held fixed it is increasing.

problems.problem: Determine if \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = x{{\bf{e}}^{x - y}} + 100y\) is increasing or decreasing at \(\left( { - 2,1} \right)\) if we allow \(x\) to vary and hold \(y\) fixed. we allow \(y\) to vary and hold \(x\) fixed.
problems.solution: Use the product rule: \(f_x = e^{x-y} + x e^{x-y} = (1 + x) e^{x-y}\) and \(f_y = -x e^{x-y} + 100\). At \((-2, 1)\), \(x-y = -3\), so \[f_x(-2,1) = (1-2)e^{-3} = -e^{-3} < 0, \qquad f_y(-2,1) = 2 e^{-3} + 100 > 0.\] \(f\) is decreasing in \(x\) and increasing in \(y\) at this point.

problems.problem: Determine if \(\displaystyle f\left( {x,y} \right) = \frac{{x + y}}{{y - x}}\) is increasing or decreasing at \(\left( {0,7} \right)\) if we allow \(x\) to vary and hold \(y\) fixed. we allow \(y\) to vary and hold \(x\) fixed.
problems.solution: Quotient rule: \(f_x = \dfrac{(1)(y-x) - (x+y)(-1)}{(y-x)^2} = \dfrac{2y}{(y-x)^2}\) and \(f_y = \dfrac{(1)(y-x) - (x+y)(1)}{(y-x)^2} = \dfrac{-2x}{(y-x)^2}\). At \((0,7)\): \[f_x(0,7) = \frac{14}{49} = \frac{2}{7} > 0, \qquad f_y(0,7) = 0.\] So \(f\) is increasing as \(x\) varies; the rate of change is zero as \(y\) varies, so neither increasing nor decreasing in \(y\).

problems.problem: Write down the vector equations of the tangent lines to the traces for \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = \sin \left( x \right)\cos \left( y \right)\) at \(\displaystyle \left( {\frac{\pi }{3}, - \frac{\pi }{4}} \right)\).
problems.answer: \(\vec r_x(t) = \left\langle \dfrac{\pi}{3} + t,\ -\dfrac{\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{4} + \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{4} t \right\rangle\), \(\vec r_y(t) = \left\langle \dfrac{\pi}{3},\ -\dfrac{\pi}{4} + t,\ \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{4} + \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{4} t \right\rangle\)
problems.solution: The point on the surface is \(z_0 = \sin(\pi/3)\cos(-\pi/4) = \tfrac{\sqrt 3}{2}\cdot\tfrac{\sqrt 2}{2} = \tfrac{\sqrt 6}{4}\). The partials are \(f_x = \cos x \cos y\) and \(f_y = -\sin x \sin y\). At the point, \(f_x = \tfrac{1}{2}\cdot\tfrac{\sqrt 2}{2} = \tfrac{\sqrt 2}{4}\) and \(f_y = -\tfrac{\sqrt 3}{2}\cdot(-\tfrac{\sqrt 2}{2}) = \tfrac{\sqrt 6}{4}\). The trace tangent lines have direction vectors \(\langle 1, 0, f_x\rangle\) and \(\langle 0, 1, f_y\rangle\). \[\vec r_x(t) = \left\langle \tfrac{\pi}{3} + t,\ -\tfrac{\pi}{4},\ \tfrac{\sqrt 6}{4} + \tfrac{\sqrt 2}{4} t \right\rangle, \quad \vec r_y(t) = \left\langle \tfrac{\pi}{3},\ -\tfrac{\pi}{4} + t,\ \tfrac{\sqrt 6}{4} + \tfrac{\sqrt 6}{4} t \right\rangle.\]

problems.problem: Write down the vector equations of the tangent lines to the traces for \(\displaystyle f\left( {x,y} \right) = \ln \left( {\frac{x}{{{y^2}}}} \right)\) at \(\left( {6,2} \right)\).
problems.answer: \(\vec r_x(t) = \left\langle 6 + t,\ 2,\ \ln(3/2) + \tfrac{1}{6} t \right\rangle\), \(\vec r_y(t) = \left\langle 6,\ 2 + t,\ \ln(3/2) - t \right\rangle\)
problems.solution: Write \(f = \ln x - 2\ln y\). Then \(f_x = 1/x\) and \(f_y = -2/y\). At \((6,2)\), \(z_0 = \ln(6/4) = \ln(3/2)\), \(f_x = 1/6\), \(f_y = -1\). The traces have direction vectors \(\langle 1, 0, f_x\rangle\) and \(\langle 0, 1, f_y\rangle\). \[\vec r_x(t) = \langle 6 + t,\ 2,\ \ln(3/2) + \tfrac{1}{6} t \rangle, \qquad \vec r_y(t) = \langle 6,\ 2 + t,\ \ln(3/2) - t \rangle.\]

problems.problem: Determine if \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = x\ln \left( {4y} \right) + \sqrt {x + y} \) is increasing or decreasing at \(\left( { - 3,6} \right)\) if we allow \(x\) to vary and hold \(y\) fixed. we allow \(y\) to vary and hold \(x\) fixed.
problems.solution: Compute \(f_x = \ln(4y) + \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x+y}}\) and \(f_y = \dfrac{x}{y} + \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x+y}}\). At \((-3,6)\), \(x+y = 3\). \[f_x(-3,6) = \ln 24 + \tfrac{1}{2\sqrt 3} \approx 3.47 > 0, \qquad f_y(-3,6) = -\tfrac{1}{2} + \tfrac{1}{2\sqrt 3} \approx -0.21 < 0.\] So \(f\) is increasing in \(x\) and decreasing in \(y\) at this point.

problems.problem: Determine if \(\displaystyle f\left( {x,y} \right) = {x^2}\sin \left( {\frac{\pi }{y}} \right)\) is increasing or decreasing at \(\displaystyle \left( { - 2,\frac{3}{4}} \right)\) if we allow \(x\) to vary and hold \(y\) fixed. we allow \(y\) to vary and hold \(x\) fixed.
problems.solution: \(f_x = 2 x \sin(\pi/y)\) and \(f_y = -\dfrac{\pi x^2}{y^2}\cos(\pi/y)\). At \((-2, 3/4)\), \(\pi/y = 4\pi/3\), so \(\sin(4\pi/3) = -\tfrac{\sqrt 3}{2}\) and \(\cos(4\pi/3) = -\tfrac{1}{2}\). \[f_x = 2(-2)(-\tfrac{\sqrt 3}{2}) = 2\sqrt 3 > 0, \qquad f_y = -\frac{\pi (4)}{9/16}\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{32 \pi}{9} > 0.\] \(f\) is increasing in both \(x\) and \(y\) at this point.

problems.problem: Write down the vector equations of the tangent lines to the traces for \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = x\,{{\bf{e}}^{2x - {y^{\,2}}}}\) at \(\left( {2,0} \right)\).
problems.answer: \(\vec r_x(t) = \langle 2 + t,\ 0,\ 2 e^4 + 5 e^4 t \rangle\), \(\vec r_y(t) = \langle 2,\ t,\ 2 e^4 \rangle\)

13.4.title: Higher Order Partial Derivatives
13.4.unitTitle: Limits, Partial Derivatives & the Chain Rule

problems.problem: Verify Clairaut's Theorem for the given function (compute the mixed second-order partials and confirm they are equal). \(Q\left( {s,t} \right) = \ln \left( {st} \right) - {s^4}\sin \left( {6t} \right) + st\)
problems.solution: Write \(Q = \ln s + \ln t - s^4 \sin(6t) + s t\). Then \(Q_s = 1/s - 4 s^3 \sin(6t) + t\) and \(Q_t = 1/t - 6 s^4 \cos(6t) + s\). Cross-differentiating: \[Q_{st} = -24 s^3 \cos(6t) + 1, \qquad Q_{ts} = -24 s^3 \cos(6t) + 1.\] They agree, confirming Clairaut\'s theorem.

problems.problem: Verify Clairaut's Theorem for the given function (compute the mixed second-order partials and confirm they are equal). \(f\left( {u,w} \right) = \sin \left( {uw} \right) + 4{u^2}{w^{ - 2}}\)
problems.answer: \(f_{uw} = f_{wu} = -u w \sin(u w) + \cos(u w) - 16 u w^{-3}\)
problems.solution: \(f_u = w \cos(u w) + 8 u w^{-2}\) and \(f_w = u \cos(u w) - 8 u^2 w^{-3}\). Then \[f_{uw} = \cos(u w) - u w \sin(u w) - 16 u w^{-3}, \qquad f_{wu} = \cos(u w) - u w \sin(u w) - 16 u w^{-3}.\] They are equal, verifying Clairaut\'s theorem.

problems.problem: Verify Clairaut's Theorem for the given function (compute the mixed second-order partials and confirm they are equal). \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = {{\bf{e}}^{x\,y}}\sin \left( y \right)\)
problems.answer: \(f_{xy} = f_{yx} = (1 + x y) e^{x y} \sin(y) + y e^{x y} \cos(y)\)
problems.solution: \(f_x = y e^{x y} \sin(y)\) and \(f_y = x e^{x y} \sin(y) + e^{x y} \cos(y)\). Differentiating each crosswise: \[f_{xy} = e^{x y}\sin(y) + x y e^{x y}\sin(y) + y e^{x y}\cos(y),\] \[f_{yx} = e^{x y}\sin(y) + x y e^{x y}\sin(y) + y e^{x y}\cos(y).\] The two mixed partials match, verifying Clairaut\'s theorem.

problems.problem: Verify Clairaut's Theorem for the given function (compute the mixed second-order partials and confirm they are equal). \(\displaystyle f\left( {x,y} \right) = {x^3}{y^2} - \frac{{4{y^6}}}{{{x^3}}}\)
problems.solution: \(f_x = 3 x^2 y^2 + 12 y^6 x^{-4}\) and \(f_y = 2 x^3 y - 24 y^5 x^{-3}\). \[f_{xy} = 6 x^2 y + 72 y^5 x^{-4}, \qquad f_{yx} = 6 x^2 y + 72 y^5 x^{-4}.\] Equal, as Clairaut\'s theorem requires.

problems.problem: Verify Clairaut's Theorem for the given function (compute the mixed second-order partials and confirm they are equal). \(\displaystyle A\left( {x,y} \right) = \cos \left( {\frac{x}{y}} \right) - {x^7}{y^4} + {y^{10}}\)
problems.solution: \(A_x = -\dfrac{1}{y}\sin(x/y) - 7 x^6 y^4\) and \(A_y = \dfrac{x}{y^2}\sin(x/y) - 4 x^7 y^3 + 10 y^9\). Cross-differentiating: \[A_{xy} = \frac{1}{y^2}\sin(x/y) + \frac{x}{y^3}\cos(x/y) - 28 x^6 y^3,\] \[A_{yx} = \frac{1}{y^2}\sin(x/y) + \frac{x}{y^3}\cos(x/y) - 28 x^6 y^3.\] They agree, verifying Clairaut\'s theorem.

13.6.title: Chain Rule
13.6.unitTitle: Limits, Partial Derivatives & the Chain Rule

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \(\displaystyle \frac{{dz}}{{dt}}\) . \(z = {{\bf{e}}^{{x^{\,2}} - y}}\,\hspace{0.5in}x = \sin \left( {4t} \right),\,\,\,\,y = {t^3} - 9\)
problems.solution: Use \(\dfrac{dz}{dt} = z_x \dfrac{dx}{dt} + z_y \dfrac{dy}{dt}\). Here \(z_x = 2 x e^{x^2 - y}\), \(z_y = -e^{x^2 - y}\), \(dx/dt = 4\cos(4t)\), \(dy/dt = 3 t^2\). \[\frac{dz}{dt} = 2 x e^{x^2 - y}\cdot 4\cos(4t) + (-e^{x^2 - y})(3 t^2) = e^{x^2 - y}\bigl(8 x \cos(4t) - 3 t^2\bigr).\]

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \(\displaystyle \frac{{dw}}{{dt}}\) . \(w = {x^4} - 4x{y^2} + {z^3}\,\hspace{0.5in}x = \sqrt t ,\,\,\,\,y = {{\bf{e}}^{2t}},\,\,\,\,z = \frac{1}{t}\)
problems.answer: \(\dfrac{dw}{dt} = \dfrac{4 x^3 - 4 y^2}{2\sqrt{t}} - 16 x y\, e^{2t} - \dfrac{3 z^2}{t^2}\)

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \(\displaystyle \frac{{dw}}{{dt}}\) . \(w = \frac{{4x}}{{y\,{z^3}}}\,\hspace{0.5in}x = 7t - 1,\,\,\,\,y = 1 - 2t,\,\,\,\,z = {t^4}\)
problems.answer: \(\dfrac{dw}{dt} = \dfrac{28}{y z^3} + \dfrac{8 x}{y^2 z^3} - \dfrac{48 x t^3}{y z^4}\)

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \(\displaystyle \frac{{dz}}{{dx}}\) . \(z = 2{x^3}{{\bf{e}}^{4y}}\,\hspace{0.5in}y = \cos \left( {6x} \right)\)
problems.solution: \(z\) depends on \(x\) directly and through \(y\). Use \(\dfrac{dz}{dx} = \dfrac{\partial z}{\partial x} + \dfrac{\partial z}{\partial y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\). Here \(\partial z/\partial x = 6 x^2 e^{4y}\), \(\partial z/\partial y = 8 x^3 e^{4y}\), \(dy/dx = -6\sin(6x)\). \[\frac{dz}{dx} = 6 x^2 e^{4y} + 8 x^3 e^{4y}\bigl(-6\sin(6x)\bigr) = 6 x^2 e^{4y} - 48 x^3 e^{4y}\sin(6x).\]

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \(\displaystyle \frac{{dz}}{{dx}}\) . \(z = \tan \left( {\frac{x}{y}} \right)\,\hspace{0.5in}y = {{\bf{e}}^{{x^{\,2}}}}\)
problems.solution: \(\dfrac{dz}{dx} = \dfrac{\partial z}{\partial x} + \dfrac{\partial z}{\partial y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\). Here \(\partial z/\partial x = \tfrac{1}{y}\sec^2(x/y)\), \(\partial z/\partial y = -\tfrac{x}{y^2}\sec^2(x/y)\), \(dy/dx = 2 x e^{x^2}\). \[\frac{dz}{dx} = \frac{\sec^2(x/y)}{y} + \left(-\frac{x \sec^2(x/y)}{y^2}\right)(2 x e^{x^2}) = \sec^2(x/y)\left(\frac{1}{y} - \frac{2 x^2 e^{x^2}}{y^2}\right).\]

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial u}}\) and \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial v}}\) . \(z = x\sin \left( {{y^2} - x} \right)\,\hspace{0.5in}x = 3u - {v^2},\,\,\,\,y = {u^6}\)
problems.answer: \(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial u} = 3\bigl(\sin(y^2 - x) - x \cos(y^2 - x)\bigr) + 12 x y u^5 \cos(y^2 - x)\), \(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial v} = -2 v\bigl(\sin(y^2 - x) - x \cos(y^2 - x)\bigr)\)
problems.solution: \(z_x = \sin(y^2 - x) - x \cos(y^2 - x)\) and \(z_y = 2 x y \cos(y^2 - x)\).
