With \(x_u = 3, x_v = -2v, y_u = 6 u^5, y_v = 0\): \[\frac{\partial z}{\partial u} = 3 z_x + 6 u^5 z_y, \qquad \frac{\partial z}{\partial v} = -2 v\, z_x.\] Substituting the expressions for \(z_x, z_y\) gives the formulas shown.

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \({w_u}\) and \({w_v}\) . \(w = {x^4}{y^{ - 3}}{z^2}\,\hspace{0.5in}x = {u^2}v,\,\,\,\,y = 3 - uv,\,\,\,\,\,\,z = 7{u^2} - 10v\)

Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial t}}\) and \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial s}}\) . \(z = 6x + {y^2}\tan \left( x \right)\,\hspace{0.5in}x = {p^2} - 3t,\,\,\,\,y = {s^2} - {t^2},\,\,\,\,p = {{\bf{e}}^{3s}}\)
problems.answer: \(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial t} = -3\bigl(6 + y^2 \sec^2 x\bigr) - 4 t y \tan x\), \(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial s} = 6 p e^{3s}\bigl(6 + y^2 \sec^2 x\bigr) + 4 s y \tan x\)
problems.solution: \(z_x = 6 + y^2 \sec^2 x\) and \(z_y = 2 y \tan x\). For \(\partial z/\partial t\): \(x_t = -3\), \(y_t = -2 t\), so \(z_t = -3 z_x - 2 t z_y\). For \(\partial z/\partial s\): \(x\) depends on \(s\) only through \(p\), with \(x_p = 2 p\) and \(p_s = 3 e^{3s}\); \(y_s = 2 s\). Thus \(z_s = z_x \cdot 2 p \cdot 3 e^{3s} + z_y \cdot 2 s\). \[\frac{\partial z}{\partial t} = -3(6 + y^2 \sec^2 x) - 4 t y \tan x,\] \[\frac{\partial z}{\partial s} = 6 p e^{3s}(6 + y^2 \sec^2 x) + 4 s y \tan x.\]

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \({w_p}\) and \({w_t}\) . \(w = {x^2}{y^4}{z^6} - 2xy\,\hspace{0.5in}x = 2p,\,\,\,\,y = 3tq,\,\,\,\,\,\,z = 3t{p^2},\,\,\,\,q = 2t\)
problems.solution: \(w_x = 2 x y^4 z^6 - 2 y\), \(w_y = 4 x^2 y^3 z^6 - 2 x\), \(w_z = 6 x^2 y^4 z^5\). With \(x = 2p\) so \(x_p = 2\); \(z = 3 t p^2\) so \(z_p = 6 t p\); for \(t\), \(y = 3 t q\) and \(q = 2 t\), giving \(dy/dt = 3 q + 3 t (2) = 3 q + 6 t\); also \(z_t = 3 p^2\). \[w_p = 2 w_x + 6 t p\, w_z, \qquad w_t = (3 q + 6 t) w_y + 3 p^2 w_z.\] Substituting gives the formulas shown.

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial w}}{{\partial u}}\) and \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial w}}{{\partial v}}\) . \(w = \frac{{\sqrt y }}{{{x^2}{z^3}}}\,\hspace{0.5in}x = uv,\,\,\,\,y = {u^2} - {p^3},\,\,\,\,\,\,z = 4qp,\,\,\,\,p = 2u - 3v,\,\,\,\,\,\,q = {v^2}\)
problems.answer: \(\dfrac{\partial w}{\partial u} = v\, w_x + (2 u - 6 p^2) w_y + 8 q\, w_z\), \(\dfrac{\partial w}{\partial v} = u\, w_x + 9 p^2 w_y + (8 p v - 12 q) w_z\), where \(w_x = -\dfrac{2\sqrt{y}}{x^3 z^3},\ w_y = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{y}\, x^2 z^3},\ w_z = -\dfrac{3\sqrt{y}}{x^2 z^4}\)
problems.solution: Here \(x(u,v), y(u,p), z(q,p), p(u,v), q(v)\). Build the chain: \(x_u = v\); \(\dfrac{dy}{du} = y_u + y_p p_u = 2u + (-3 p^2)(2) = 2 u - 6 p^2\); \(\dfrac{dz}{du} = z_p p_u = (4 q)(2) = 8 q\). For \(v\): \(x_v = u\); \(\dfrac{dy}{dv} = y_p p_v = -3 p^2 \cdot (-3) = 9 p^2\); \(\dfrac{dz}{dv} = z_q q_v + z_p p_v = (4 p)(2 v) + (4 q)(-3) = 8 p v - 12 q\). \[\frac{\partial w}{\partial u} = v\, w_x + (2 u - 6 p^2)\, w_y + 8 q\, w_z, \qquad \frac{\partial w}{\partial v} = u\, w_x + 9 p^2\, w_y + (8 p v - 12 q)\, w_z.\]

problems.problem: Determine formulas for \({w_u}\) and \({w_t}\) for the following situation. \(w = w\left( {x,y} \right)\hspace{0.5in}x = x\left( {y,z} \right),\,\,\,\,y = y\left( {u,v} \right),\,\,\,\,z = z\left( {u,t} \right),\,\,\,\,v = v\left( t \right)\)
problems.answer: \(w_u = w_x \bigl(x_y \cdot y_u\bigr) + w_y \cdot y_u\), \(w_t = w_x \bigl(x_y \cdot y_v \cdot v_t + x_z \cdot z_t\bigr) + w_y \cdot y_v \cdot v_t\)
problems.solution: Build the dependency tree. \(u\) reaches \(w\) only through \(y\), with \(y\) feeding both \(x\) and \(w\) directly. Since \(v = v(t)\), \(v\) does not depend on \(u\), so \(y_u\) is the only contribution. For \(t\), the path runs \(t \to v \to y\) and also \(t \to z\), with \(z\) and \(y\) feeding \(x\). \[w_u = \frac{\partial w}{\partial x}\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial u} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial u},\] \[w_t = \frac{\partial w}{\partial x}\!\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\frac{dv}{dt} + \frac{\partial x}{\partial z}\frac{\partial z}{\partial t}\right) + \frac{\partial w}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\frac{dv}{dt}.\]

problems.problem: Determine formulas for \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial w}}{{\partial s}}\) and \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial w}}{{\partial t}}\) for the following situation. \(w = w\left( {x,y,z} \right)\hspace{0.5in}x = x\left( {u,v,t} \right),\,\,\,\,y = y\left( p \right),\,\,\,\,z = z\left( {u,t} \right),\,\,\,\,v = v\left( {p,t} \right),\,\,\,\,p = p\left( {s,t} \right)\)
problems.answer: \(w_s = p_s\bigl(w_x x_v v_p + w_y y_p\bigr)\), \(w_t = w_x\bigl(x_t + x_v(v_t + v_p p_t)\bigr) + w_y y_p p_t + w_z z_t\)
problems.solution: Trace the tree. \(s\) reaches the function only through \(p\) (since \(p = p(s,t)\) is the only place \(s\) appears), and \(p\) feeds \(y\) directly and \(v\) (which feeds \(x\)). For \(t\), there are direct paths to \(x\) and \(z\), plus paths through \(v\) and through \(p\) (which then reaches both \(y\) and \(v\)). \[\frac{\partial w}{\partial s} = \frac{\partial p}{\partial s}\!\left(\frac{\partial w}{\partial x}\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\frac{\partial v}{\partial p} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial y}\frac{dy}{dp}\right),\] \[\frac{\partial w}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial w}{\partial x}\!\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\!\left(\frac{\partial v}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial v}{\partial p}\frac{\partial p}{\partial t}\right)\right) + \frac{\partial w}{\partial y}\frac{dy}{dp}\frac{\partial p}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\frac{\partial z}{\partial t}.\]

problems.problem: Compute \(\displaystyle \frac{{dy}}{{dx}}\) for the following equation. \(\cos \left( {2x + 3y} \right) = {x^5} - 8{y^2}\)
problems.solution: Set \(F(x,y) = \cos(2x+3y) - x^5 + 8 y^2 = 0\). Then \(F_x = -2\sin(2x+3y) - 5 x^4\) and \(F_y = -3\sin(2x+3y) + 16 y\). The implicit derivative is \(dy/dx = -F_x/F_y\). \[\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{-2\sin(2x+3y) - 5 x^4}{-3\sin(2x+3y) + 16 y} = \frac{5 x^4 + 2\sin(2x+3y)}{16 y - 3\sin(2x+3y)}.\]

problems.problem: Compute \(\displaystyle \frac{{dy}}{{dx}}\) for the following equation. \(\cos \left( {2x} \right)\sin \left( {3y} \right) - xy = {y^4} + 9\)
problems.solution: Set \(F(x,y) = \cos(2x)\sin(3y) - x y - y^4 - 9 = 0\). Then \(F_x = -2\sin(2x)\sin(3y) - y\) and \(F_y = 3\cos(2x)\cos(3y) - x - 4 y^3\). \[\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{F_x}{F_y} = \frac{2\sin(2x)\sin(3y) + y}{3\cos(2x)\cos(3y) - x - 4 y^3}\cdot(-1) = -\frac{2\sin(2x)\sin(3y) + y}{3\cos(2x)\cos(3y) - x - 4 y^3}.\]

problems.problem: Compute \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial x}}\) and \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial y}}\) for the following equation. \({z^3}{y^4} - {x^2}\cos \left( {2y - 4z} \right) = 4z\)
problems.answer: \(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial x} = \dfrac{2 x \cos(2y - 4z)}{3 z^2 y^4 - 4 x^2 \sin(2y - 4z) - 4}\), \(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial y} = \dfrac{-2 x^2 \sin(2y - 4z) - 4 z^3 y^3}{3 z^2 y^4 - 4 x^2 \sin(2y - 4z) - 4}\)
problems.solution: Set \(F = z^3 y^4 - x^2 \cos(2y - 4z) - 4 z\). Then \(F_x = -2 x \cos(2y - 4z)\), \(F_y = 4 z^3 y^3 + 2 x^2 \sin(2y - 4z)\), \(F_z = 3 z^2 y^4 - 4 x^2 \sin(2y - 4z) - 4\). Apply \(\partial z/\partial x = -F_x/F_z\) and \(\partial z/\partial y = -F_y/F_z\). \[\frac{\partial z}{\partial x} = \frac{2 x \cos(2y - 4z)}{3 z^2 y^4 - 4 x^2 \sin(2y - 4z) - 4},\] \[\frac{\partial z}{\partial y} = -\frac{4 z^3 y^3 + 2 x^2 \sin(2y - 4z)}{3 z^2 y^4 - 4 x^2 \sin(2y - 4z) - 4}.\]

problems.problem: Compute \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial x}}\) and \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial y}}\) for the following equation. \(\sin \left( x \right){{\bf{e}}^{4x\,z}} + 2{z^2}y = \cos \left( z \right)\)
problems.answer: \(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial x} = -\dfrac{\cos(x) e^{4 x z} + 4 z \sin(x) e^{4 x z}}{4 x \sin(x) e^{4 x z} + 4 z y + \sin(z)}\), \(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial y} = -\dfrac{2 z^2}{4 x \sin(x) e^{4 x z} + 4 z y + \sin(z)}\)
problems.solution: Set \(F = \sin(x) e^{4 x z} + 2 z^2 y - \cos(z)\). Then \(F_x = \cos(x) e^{4 x z} + 4 z \sin(x) e^{4 x z}\), \(F_y = 2 z^2\), \(F_z = 4 x \sin(x) e^{4 x z} + 4 z y + \sin(z)\). \[\frac{\partial z}{\partial x} = -\frac{F_x}{F_z}, \qquad \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} = -\frac{F_y}{F_z}.\]

problems.problem: Determine \({f_{u\,u}}\) and \({f_{v\,v}}\) for the following situation. \(f = f\left( {x,y} \right)\hspace{0.5in}x = {{\bf{e}}^u}sin\left( v \right),\,\,\,\,\,\,\,y = {{\bf{e}}^u}\cos \left( v \right)\)
problems.answer: \(f_{uu} = e^u(f_x \sin v + f_y \cos v) + e^{2u}\bigl(f_{xx}\sin^2 v + 2 f_{xy}\sin v\cos v + f_{yy}\cos^2 v\bigr)\), \(f_{vv} = -e^u(f_x \sin v + f_y \cos v) + e^{2u}\bigl(f_{xx}\cos^2 v - 2 f_{xy}\sin v\cos v + f_{yy}\sin^2 v\bigr)\)
problems.solution: \(x_u = e^u\sin v\), \(y_u = e^u\cos v\), \(x_v = e^u\cos v\), \(y_v = -e^u\sin v\). First, \(f_u = e^u(f_x \sin v + f_y \cos v)\). Differentiate again, treating \(f_x\) and \(f_y\) as functions of \(u, v\) and applying the chain rule again: \[f_{uu} = e^u(f_x \sin v + f_y \cos v) + e^{2u}\bigl(f_{xx}\sin^2 v + 2 f_{xy}\sin v \cos v + f_{yy}\cos^2 v\bigr).\] For \(v\), \(f_v = e^u(f_x \cos v - f_y \sin v)\), and a second application yields \[f_{vv} = -e^u(f_x \sin v + f_y \cos v) + e^{2u}\bigl(f_{xx}\cos^2 v - 2 f_{xy}\sin v \cos v + f_{yy}\sin^2 v\bigr).\]

problems.problem: Determine \({f_{u\,u}}\) and \({f_{v\,v}}\) for the following situation. \(f = f\left( {x,y} \right)\hspace{0.5in}x = {u^2} - {v^2},\,\,\,\,\,\,\,y = \frac{u}{v}\)
problems.answer: \(f_{uu} = 2 f_x + 4 u^2 f_{xx} + \dfrac{4 u}{v} f_{xy} + \dfrac{1}{v^2} f_{yy}\), \(f_{vv} = -2 f_x + \dfrac{2 u}{v^3} f_y + 4 v^2 f_{xx} + \dfrac{4 u}{v} f_{xy} + \dfrac{u^2}{v^4} f_{yy}\)
problems.solution: \(x_u = 2u, y_u = 1/v, x_v = -2v, y_v = -u/v^2\). \(f_u = 2 u f_x + (1/v) f_y\). Differentiating again and chaining \(f_x, f_y\) through \(u\): \[f_{uu} = 2 f_x + 2 u\bigl(2 u f_{xx} + (1/v) f_{xy}\bigr) + (1/v)\bigl(2 u f_{xy} + (1/v) f_{yy}\bigr) = 2 f_x + 4 u^2 f_{xx} + \tfrac{4 u}{v} f_{xy} + \tfrac{1}{v^2} f_{yy}.\] For \(v\), \(f_v = -2 v f_x - (u/v^2) f_y\), so \[f_{vv} = -2 f_x + \tfrac{2 u}{v^3} f_y + 4 v^2 f_{xx} + \tfrac{4 u}{v} f_{xy} + \tfrac{u^2}{v^4} f_{yy}.\]

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \(\displaystyle \frac{{dz}}{{dt}}\) . \(z = \cos \left( {y\,{x^2}} \right)\,\hspace{0.5in}x = {t^4} - 2t,\,\,\,\,y = 1 - {t^6}\)
problems.answer: \(\dfrac{dz}{dt} = -\sin(y x^2)\bigl(2 x y(4 t^3 - 2) - 6 t^5 x^2\bigr)\)

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \(\displaystyle \frac{{dw}}{{dt}}\) . \(w = \frac{{{x^2} - z}}{{{y^4}}}\,\hspace{0.5in}x = {t^3} + 7,\,\,\,\,y = \cos \left( {2t} \right),\,\,\,\,z = 4t\)
problems.answer: \(\dfrac{dw}{dt} = \dfrac{6 t^2 x}{y^4} + \dfrac{4(x^2 - z) \sin(2t)}{y^5}\cdot 4 - \dfrac{4}{y^4}\), simplified: \(\dfrac{dw}{dt} = \dfrac{6 t^2 x}{y^4} + \dfrac{8(x^2 - z)\sin(2t)}{y^5} - \dfrac{4}{y^4}\)

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \(\displaystyle \frac{{dz}}{{dx}}\) . \(z = {x^2}{y^4} - 2y\,\hspace{0.5in}y = \sin \left( {{x^2}} \right)\)
problems.solution: \(z\) depends on \(x\) directly and through \(y\). \(\partial z/\partial x = 2 x y^4\), \(\partial z/\partial y = 4 x^2 y^3 - 2\), \(dy/dx = 2 x \cos(x^2)\). \[\frac{dz}{dx} = 2 x y^4 + (4 x^2 y^3 - 2)(2 x \cos(x^2)).\]

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial u}}\) and \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial v}}\) . \(z = {x^{ - 2}}{y^6} - 4x\,\hspace{0.5in}x = {u^2}v,\,\,\,\,y = v - 3u\)
problems.answer: \(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial u} = 2 u v\,(-2 x^{-3} y^6 - 4) - 3\cdot 6 x^{-2} y^5\), \(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial v} = u^2(-2 x^{-3} y^6 - 4) + 6 x^{-2} y^5\)

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \({z_t}\) and \({z_p}\) . \(z = 4y\sin \left( {2x} \right)\,\hspace{0.5in}x = 3u - p,\,\,\,\,y = {p^2}u,\,\,\,\,\,\,u = {t^2} + 1\)
problems.answer: \(z_t = 8 y \cos(2x)\cdot 6 t + 4 \sin(2x)\cdot 2 p^2 t\), \(z_p = -8 y \cos(2x) + 8 p u \sin(2x)\)
problems.solution: \(z_x = 8 y \cos(2x)\), \(z_y = 4 \sin(2x)\); \(u = t^2 + 1\), so \(u_t = 2t\). With \(x = 3 u - p\): \(\partial x/\partial t = 3 u_t = 6 t\), \(\partial x/\partial p = -1\). With \(y = p^2 u\): \(\partial y/\partial t = p^2 u_t = 2 p^2 t\), \(\partial y/\partial p = 2 p u\). \[z_t = 8 y \cos(2x)\cdot 6 t + 4 \sin(2x)\cdot 2 p^2 t = 48 t y \cos(2x) + 8 p^2 t \sin(2x),\] \[z_p = 8 y \cos(2x)\cdot(-1) + 4 \sin(2x)\cdot 2 p u = -8 y \cos(2x) + 8 p u \sin(2x).\]

problems.problem: Use the Chain Rule to compute the requested derivative. Given the following information use the Chain Rule to determine \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial w}}{{\partial t}}\) and \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial w}}{{\partial s}}\) . \(w = \sqrt {{x^2} + {y^2}} + \frac{{6z}}{y}\,\hspace{0.5in}x = \sin \left( p \right),\,\,\,\,y = p + 3t - 4s,\,\,\,\,z = \frac{{{t^3}}}{{{s^2}}},\,\,\,\,p = 1 - 2t\)
problems.answer: \(w_t = w_x \cos(p)(-2) + w_y\bigl(-2 + 3\bigr) + w_z\dfrac{3 t^2}{s^2} = -2\cos(p) w_x + w_y + \dfrac{3 t^2}{s^2} w_z\), \(w_s = -4\, w_y - \dfrac{2 t^3}{s^3} w_z\), where \(w_x = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^2+y^2}},\ w_y = \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{x^2+y^2}} - \dfrac{6 z}{y^2},\ w_z = \dfrac{6}{y}\)
problems.solution: Variables: \(x = \sin p\), \(y = p + 3 t - 4 s\), \(z = t^3/s^2\), \(p = 1 - 2t\). For \(t\): \(p_t = -2\); \(\partial x/\partial t = \cos(p) \cdot p_t = -2\cos(p)\); direct \(\partial y/\partial t = 3 + p_t \cdot 1 = 3 + (-2)\cdot 1\) only counts the \(p\)-path once, so total \(dy/dt = -2 + 3 = 1\); \(\partial z/\partial t = 3 t^2/s^2\). For \(s\): \(p\) does not depend on \(s\), so \(dx/ds = 0\); \(dy/ds = -4\); \(dz/ds = -2 t^3/s^3\). \[\frac{\partial w}{\partial t} = -2 \cos(p)\, w_x + w_y + \frac{3 t^2}{s^2}\, w_z, \qquad \frac{\partial w}{\partial s} = -4\, w_y - \frac{2 t^3}{s^3}\, w_z.\]

problems.problem: Determine formulas for \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial w}}{{\partial t}}\) and \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial w}}{{\partial v}}\) for the following situation. \(w = w\left( {x,y} \right)\hspace{0.5in}x = x\left( {p,q,s} \right),\,\,\,\,y = y\left( {p,u,v} \right),\,\,\,\,s = s\left( {u,v} \right),\,\,\,\,p = p\left( t \right)\)
problems.answer: \(\dfrac{\partial w}{\partial t} = p_t\bigl(w_x x_p + w_y y_p\bigr)\), \(\dfrac{\partial w}{\partial v} = w_x\, x_s\, s_v + w_y\, y_v\)
problems.solution: Trace the tree. \(t\) flows only into \(p\), and \(p\) feeds both \(x\) (via \(x(p,q,s)\)) and \(y\) (via \(y(p,u,v)\)). \(v\) feeds \(y\) directly and feeds \(x\) through \(s\) (via \(s(u,v)\)). \[\frac{\partial w}{\partial t} = \frac{dp}{dt}\!\left(\frac{\partial w}{\partial x}\frac{\partial x}{\partial p} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial p}\right),\] \[\frac{\partial w}{\partial v} = \frac{\partial w}{\partial x}\frac{\partial x}{\partial s}\frac{\partial s}{\partial v} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}.\]

problems.problem: Determine formulas for \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial w}}{{\partial t}}\) and \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial w}}{{\partial u}}\) for the following situation. \(w = w\left( {x,y,z} \right)\hspace{0.5in}x = x\left( t \right),\,\,\,\,y = y\left( {u,v,p} \right),\,\,\,\,z = z\left( {v,p} \right),\,\,\,\,v = v\left( {r,u} \right),\,\,\,\,p = p\left( {t,u} \right)\)
problems.answer: \(\dfrac{\partial w}{\partial t} = w_x\, x_t + p_t\bigl(w_y\, y_p + w_z\, z_p\bigr)\), \(\dfrac{\partial w}{\partial u} = w_y\bigl(y_u + y_v\, v_u + y_p\, p_u\bigr) + w_z\bigl(z_v\, v_u + z_p\, p_u\bigr)\)
problems.solution: For \(t\): only \(x = x(t)\) and \(p = p(t,u)\) depend on \(t\); \(p\) then feeds \(y\) and \(z\). For \(u\): \(y\) depends on \(u\) directly, and through \(v(r,u)\) and \(p(t,u)\); \(z\) depends on \(u\) through \(v\) and \(p\); \(x\) does not depend on \(u\). \[\frac{\partial w}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial w}{\partial x}\frac{dx}{dt} + \frac{\partial p}{\partial t}\!\left(\frac{\partial w}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial p} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\frac{\partial z}{\partial p}\right),\] \[\frac{\partial w}{\partial u} = \frac{\partial w}{\partial y}\!\left(\frac{\partial y}{\partial u} + \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\frac{\partial v}{\partial u} + \frac{\partial y}{\partial p}\frac{\partial p}{\partial u}\right) + \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\!\left(\frac{\partial z}{\partial v}\frac{\partial v}{\partial u} + \frac{\partial z}{\partial p}\frac{\partial p}{\partial u}\right).\]

problems.problem: Compute \(\displaystyle \frac{{dy}}{{dx}}\) for the following equation. \({x^2}{y^4} - 3 = \sin \left( {xy} \right)\)
problems.solution: Set \(F = x^2 y^4 - \sin(xy) - 3\). Then \(F_x = 2 x y^4 - y\cos(xy)\) and \(F_y = 4 x^2 y^3 - x\cos(xy)\). \[\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{F_x}{F_y} = -\frac{2 x y^4 - y\cos(xy)}{4 x^2 y^3 - x\cos(xy)} = \frac{y\bigl(\cos(xy) - 2 x y^3\bigr)}{x\bigl(4 x y^3 - \cos(xy)\bigr)}.\]

problems.problem: Compute \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial x}}\) and \(\displaystyle \frac{{\partial z}}{{\partial y}}\) for the following equation. \({{\bf{e}}^{z\,y}} + x{z^2} = 6x{y^4}{z^3}\)
problems.answer: \(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial x} = \dfrac{z^2(6 y^4 z - 1)}{2 x z + y e^{z y} - 18 x y^4 z^2}\), \(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial y} = \dfrac{z(24 x y^3 z^2 - e^{z y})}{2 x z + y e^{z y} - 18 x y^4 z^2}\)
problems.solution: Set \(F = e^{z y} + x z^2 - 6 x y^4 z^3\). Then \(F_x = z^2 - 6 y^4 z^3\), \(F_y = z e^{z y} - 24 x y^3 z^3\), \(F_z = y e^{z y} + 2 x z - 18 x y^4 z^2\). \[\frac{\partial z}{\partial x} = -\frac{z^2 - 6 y^4 z^3}{y e^{z y} + 2 x z - 18 x y^4 z^2} = \frac{z^2(6 y^4 z - 1)}{2 x z + y e^{z y} - 18 x y^4 z^2},\] \[\frac{\partial z}{\partial y} = -\frac{z e^{z y} - 24 x y^3 z^3}{y e^{z y} + 2 x z - 18 x y^4 z^2} = \frac{z(24 x y^3 z^2 - e^{z y})}{2 x z + y e^{z y} - 18 x y^4 z^2}.\]

problems.problem: Determine \({f_{u\,u}}\) for the following situation. \(f = f\left( {x,y} \right)\hspace{0.5in}x = {u^2} + 3v,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,y = uv\)
problems.solution: \(x_u = 2 u\), \(y_u = v\). Then \(f_u = 2 u f_x + v f_y\). Differentiate again, chaining \(f_x, f_y\) through \(u\): \[f_{uu} = 2 f_x + 2 u\bigl(f_{xx}\cdot 2u + f_{xy}\cdot v\bigr) + v\bigl(f_{xy}\cdot 2u + f_{yy}\cdot v\bigr) = 2 f_x + 4 u^2 f_{xx} + 4 u v\, f_{xy} + v^2 f_{yy}.\]

problems.problem: Determine the gradient of the given function. \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = {y^3}{x^5} + \ln \left( {xy} \right)\)
problems.solution: Note \(\ln(xy) = \ln x + \ln y\), so its partials are \(1/x\) and \(1/y\). \[f_x = 5 y^3 x^4 + \frac{1}{x}, \qquad f_y = 3 y^2 x^5 + \frac{1}{y}.\] Hence \(\nabla f = \langle f_x, f_y\rangle\) as shown.

problems.problem: Determine the gradient of the given function. \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = {{\bf{e}}^{\frac{x}{y}}} + {y^4}\sin \left( {xy} \right)\)
problems.answer: \(\nabla f = \left\langle \dfrac{1}{y} e^{x/y} + y^5 \cos(xy),\ -\dfrac{x}{y^2} e^{x/y} + 4 y^3 \sin(xy) + x y^4 \cos(xy)\right\rangle\)
problems.solution: Apply the chain rule to \(e^{x/y}\) and product rule to \(y^4 \sin(xy)\). \[f_x = \frac{1}{y} e^{x/y} + y^4 \cos(xy)\cdot y = \frac{1}{y} e^{x/y} + y^5 \cos(xy),\] \[f_y = -\frac{x}{y^2} e^{x/y} + 4 y^3 \sin(xy) + x y^4 \cos(xy).\] \(\nabla f = \langle f_x, f_y\rangle\).

problems.problem: Determine the gradient of the given function. \(\displaystyle f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = 4z - \frac{{{y^4}}}{{2{z^3}}} + \sqrt {{x^3}} \left( {z - 1} \right)\)
Determine the gradient of the given function. \(\displaystyle f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = \cos \left( {\frac{{xy}}{z}} \right) + {z^3}{y^2}x\)
problems.answer: \(\nabla f = \left\langle -\dfrac{y}{z}\sin\!\left(\dfrac{xy}{z}\right) + z^3 y^2,\ -\dfrac{x}{z}\sin\!\left(\dfrac{xy}{z}\right) + 2 z^3 y x,\ \dfrac{xy}{z^2}\sin\!\left(\dfrac{xy}{z}\right) + 3 z^2 y^2 x\right\rangle\)
problems.solution: Let \(u = xy/z\). Then \(u_x = y/z\), \(u_y = x/z\), \(u_z = -xy/z^2\). Apply the chain rule to \(\cos u\). \[f_x = -\frac{y}{z}\sin\!\left(\frac{xy}{z}\right) + z^3 y^2, \quad f_y = -\frac{x}{z}\sin\!\left(\frac{xy}{z}\right) + 2 z^3 y x, \quad f_z = \frac{xy}{z^2}\sin\!\left(\frac{xy}{z}\right) + 3 z^2 y^2 x.\]

problems.problem: Determine the gradient of the given function. \(\displaystyle f\left( {x,y} \right) = {x^2}\sec \left( {3x} \right) - \frac{{{x^2}}}{{{y^3}}}\)
problems.solution: Use the product rule on \(x^2 \sec(3x)\), with \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\sec(3x) = 3\sec(3x)\tan(3x)\). \[f_x = 2 x \sec(3x) + 3 x^2 \sec(3x)\tan(3x) - \frac{2 x}{y^3}, \qquad f_y = \frac{3 x^2}{y^4}.\] \(\nabla f = \langle f_x, f_y\rangle\).

problems.problem: Determine the gradient of the given function. \(f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = x\cos \left( {xy} \right) + {z^2}{y^4} - 7xz\)
problems.answer: \(\nabla f = \left\langle \cos(xy) - x y \sin(xy) - 7 z,\ -x^2 \sin(xy) + 4 y^3 z^2,\ 2 z y^4 - 7 x\right\rangle\)
problems.solution: Use the product rule on \(x \cos(xy)\): \(f_x = \cos(xy) + x \cdot(-y \sin(xy)) - 7 z = \cos(xy) - x y \sin(xy) - 7 z\). The other partials are direct. \[f_y = -x^2 \sin(xy) + 4 y^3 z^2, \qquad f_z = 2 z y^4 - 7 x.\] \(\nabla f = \langle f_x, f_y, f_z\rangle\).

problems.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to \(\displaystyle z = {x^2}{y^4} - \frac{{12x}}{y}\) at \(\left( { - 1,6} \right)\).
Find the equation of the tangent plane to \(z = \ln \left( {{x^2}y} \right) - x\,\sqrt y \) at \(\displaystyle \left( { - \frac{1}{2},4} \right)\).
problems.solution: With \(f(x,y)=\ln(x^{2}y)-x\sqrt{y}\), \(f(-\tfrac{1}{2},4)=\ln(1)+1=1\). The partials simplify nicely: \[ f_x = \tfrac{2}{x} - \sqrt{y}, \qquad f_y = \tfrac{1}{y} - \tfrac{x}{2\sqrt{y}}. \] Evaluating at \((-\tfrac{1}{2},4)\) gives \(f_x=-4-2=-6\) and \(f_y=\tfrac{1}{4}+\tfrac{1}{8}=\tfrac{3}{8}\). Thus the tangent plane is \(z = 1 - 6(x+\tfrac{1}{2}) + \tfrac{3}{8}(y-4)\).

problems.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to \(z = {{\bf{e}}^{x\,y}} + {y^2}{{\bf{e}}^{1 - y}}\) at \(\left( {0,1} \right)\).
Find the linear approximation to \(z = \cos \left( {\sin \left( y \right) - x} \right)\) at \(\left( { - 2,0} \right)\).
problems.solution: With \(f(x,y)=\cos(\sin y - x)\), \(f(-2,0)=\cos(0+2)=\cos 2\). The partials are \[ f_x = \sin(\sin y - x), \qquad f_y = -\sin(\sin y - x)\cos y. \] At \((-2,0)\) these are \(\sin 2\) and \(-\sin 2\). The linear approximation is \(L(x,y)=\cos 2+\sin 2\,(x+2)-\sin 2\,y\).

problems.problem: Find the linear approximation to \(\displaystyle z = \frac{{10{x^2}}}{{x - y}}\) at \(\left( {4, - 1} \right)\).
Find the equation of the tangent plane to \(\displaystyle z = {x^2}\cos \left( {\pi y} \right) - \frac{6}{{x{y^2}}}\) at \(\left( {2, - 1} \right)\).
Find the equation of the tangent plane to \(z = x\sqrt {{x^2} + {y^2}} + {y^3}\) at \(\left( { - 4,3} \right)\).
Find the linear approximation to \(z = 4{x^2} - y{{\bf{e}}^{2x + y}}\) at \(\left( { - 2,4} \right)\).

14.2.title: Gradient Vector, Tangent Planes and Normal Lines

problems.problem: Find the tangent plane and normal line to \(z\,y + 4x\sqrt z - {x^3}{y^2} = 221\) at \(\left( { - 2,5,9} \right)\).
problems.solution: Write the surface as \(F(x,y,z)=zy+4x\sqrt{z}-x^{3}y^{2}-221=0\). Then \[ F_x=4\sqrt{z}-3x^{2}y^{2}, \quad F_y=z-2x^{3}y, \quad F_z=y+\tfrac{2x}{\sqrt{z}}. \] At \((-2,5,9)\): \(F_x=12-300=-288\), \(F_y=9+80=89\), \(F_z=5-\tfrac{4}{3}=\tfrac{11}{3}\). The tangent plane is \(-288(x+2)+89(y-5)+\tfrac{11}{3}(z-9)=0\) and the normal line is \[ \langle x,y,z\rangle=\langle -2,5,9\rangle+t\,\langle -288,89,\tfrac{11}{3}\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Find the tangent plane and normal line to \(\displaystyle {{\bf{e}}^{x\,{y^{\,2}}}} + z{y^4} = 61 + \frac{{{z^2}}}{{x + 1}}\) at \(\left( {0, - 2,6} \right)\).
problems.solution: Set \(F(x,y,z)=e^{xy^{2}}+zy^{4}-61-\tfrac{z^{2}}{x+1}\). Then \[ F_x=y^{2}e^{xy^{2}}+\tfrac{z^{2}}{(x+1)^{2}}, \quad F_y=2xy\,e^{xy^{2}}+4zy^{3}, \quad F_z=y^{4}-\tfrac{2z}{x+1}. \] At \((0,-2,6)\) one checks \(F=1+96-61-36=0\). The partials evaluate to \(4+36=40\), \(0-192=-192\), and \(16-12=4\). Tangent plane: \(40x-192(y+2)+4(z-6)=0\). Normal line: \(\langle x,y,z\rangle=\langle 0,-2,6\rangle+t\,\langle 40,-192,4\rangle\).

problems.problem: Find the tangent plane and normal line to \(9yz - \sqrt {{x^2} - 8z} = x{y^2} - 26\) at \(\left( {3,1, - 2} \right)\).
problems.solution: Let \(F(x,y,z)=9yz-\sqrt{x^{2}-8z}-xy^{2}+26\). Then \[ F_x = -\tfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2}-8z}}-y^{2}, \quad F_y = 9z-2xy, \quad F_z = 9y+\tfrac{4}{\sqrt{x^{2}-8z}}. \] At \((3,1,-2)\), \(\sqrt{9+16}=5\), so \(F_x=-\tfrac{3}{5}-1=-\tfrac{8}{5}\), \(F_y=-18-6=-24\), and \(F_z=9+\tfrac{4}{5}=\tfrac{49}{5}\). The tangent plane and normal line follow with \(\nabla F\) as the normal direction.

problems.problem: Find the point(s) on \(6{x^2} + {y^2} - 3{z^2} = 4\) where the tangent plane to the surface is parallel to the plane given by \(2x + 7y - z = 6\).
problems.solution: With \(F=6x^{2}+y^{2}-3z^{2}-4\), \(\nabla F=\langle 12x,2y,-6z\rangle\). For this to be parallel to \(\langle 2,7,-1\rangle\) we need \[ \tfrac{12x}{2}=\tfrac{2y}{7}=\tfrac{-6z}{-1}, \quad\text{i.e.}\quad y=21x \text{ and } z=x. \] Substituting into the surface: \(6x^{2}+441x^{2}-3x^{2}=4\), so \(444x^{2}=4\) and \(x=\pm\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{111}}\). The two points are \(\bigl(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{111}},\tfrac{21}{\sqrt{111}},\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{111}}\bigr)\) and its negative.

problems.problem: Find the point(s) on \({x^2} - 8{y^2} - 2{z^2} = - 3\) where the tangent plane to the surface is parallel to the plane given by \( - 4x - y + 8z = 1\).
problems.solution: With \(F=x^{2}-8y^{2}-2z^{2}+3\), \(\nabla F=\langle 2x,-16y,-4z\rangle\). Parallel to \(\langle -4,-1,8\rangle\) requires \[ \tfrac{2x}{-4}=\tfrac{-16y}{-1}=\tfrac{-4z}{8}, \quad\text{so}\quad x=-32y \text{ and } z=x=-32y. \] The constraint becomes \(1024y^{2}-8y^{2}-2048y^{2}=-3\), i.e. \(-1032y^{2}=-3\), so \(y=\pm\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{344}}\). This gives the two points \(\bigl(\mp\tfrac{32}{\sqrt{344}},\pm\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{344}},\mp\tfrac{32}{\sqrt{344}}\bigr)\).

problems.problem: Find the tangent plane and normal line to \({x^2}y = 4z{{\bf{e}}^{x + y}} - 35\) at \(\left( {3, - 3,2} \right)\).
Find the tangent plane and normal line to \(\displaystyle \ln \left( {\frac{x}{{2y}}} \right) = {z^2}\left( {x - 2y} \right) + 3z + 3\) at \(\left( {4,2, - 1} \right)\).
problems.solution: Write \(F(x,y,z)=\ln\!\bigl(\tfrac{x}{2y}\bigr)-z^{2}(x-2y)-3z-3 = \ln x-\ln(2y)-z^{2}(x-2y)-3z-3\). Then \[ F_x=\tfrac{1}{x}-z^{2}, \quad F_y=-\tfrac{1}{y}+2z^{2}, \quad F_z=-2z(x-2y)-3. \] At \((4,2,-1)\): \(F_x=\tfrac{1}{4}-1=-\tfrac{3}{4}\), \(F_y=-\tfrac{1}{2}+2=\tfrac{3}{2}\), \(F_z=-2(-1)(0)-3=-3\). The plane and normal line use \(\nabla F\) as the normal vector.

problems.problem: Find and classify all the critical points of the given function. \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 2y - 9x - xy + 5{x^2} + {y^2}\)
problems.solution: For \(f=2y-9x-xy+5x^{2}+y^{2}\) the partials are \(f_x=-9-y+10x\) and \(f_y=2-x+2y\). Setting them to zero gives \(y=10x-9\) and \(2-x+2(10x-9)=0\), so \(19x=16\) and \(x=\tfrac{16}{19}\), \(y=-\tfrac{11}{19}\). The second derivatives are \(f_{xx}=10\), \(f_{yy}=2\), \(f_{xy}=-1\), giving \[ D = 10\cdot 2 - (-1)^{2} = 19 > 0, \quad f_{xx}>0, \] so the critical point is a relative minimum.

problems.problem: Find and classify all the critical points of the given function. \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = {x^3} - {y^3} + 8xy\)
problems.solution: With \(f=x^{3}-y^{3}+8xy\), \(f_x=3x^{2}+8y=0\) and \(f_y=-3y^{2}+8x=0\). From the first \(y=-\tfrac{3x^{2}}{8}\); substituting into the second gives \(x\!\left(\tfrac{27x^{3}}{64}-8\right)=0\). So \(x=0\) (giving \(y=0\)) or \(x=\tfrac{8}{3}\), \(y=-\tfrac{8}{3}\). With \(f_{xx}=6x\), \(f_{yy}=-6y\), \(f_{xy}=8\): \[ D(0,0)=0-64=-64<0, \quad D(\tfrac{8}{3},-\tfrac{8}{3})=16\cdot 16-64=192>0. \] The origin is a saddle and the second point is a relative minimum (since \(f_{xx}=16>0\)).

problems.problem: Find and classify all the critical points of the given function. \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = \left( {y - x} \right)\left( {1 - 2x - 3y} \right)\)
problems.solution: Expanding, \(f=(y-x)(1-2x-3y)=-x+y+2x^{2}+xy-3y^{2}\). Then \(f_x=-1+4x+y=0\) and \(f_y=1+x-6y=0\). From the first \(y=1-4x\); plugging in gives \(25x=5\), so \(x=\tfrac{1}{5}\), \(y=\tfrac{1}{5}\). With \(f_{xx}=4\), \(f_{yy}=-6\), \(f_{xy}=1\): \(D=-24-1=-25<0\), so the point is a saddle.

problems.problem: Find and classify all the critical points of the given function. \(\displaystyle f\left( {x,y} \right) = \frac{1}{2}{x^4} - 4x{y^2} - 2{x^2} + 8{y^2}\)
problems.answer: Saddle at \((0,0)\); relative minima at \((\sqrt{2},0)\) and \((-\sqrt{2},0)\); saddles at \((2,\sqrt{2})\) and \((2,-\sqrt{2})\).

problems.problem: Find and classify all the critical points of the given function. \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = xy\,{{\bf{e}}^{ - 8\left( {{x^2} + {y^2}} \right)}}\)
problems.answer: Saddle at \((0,0)\); relative maxima at \(\left(\tfrac{1}{4},\tfrac{1}{4}\right)\) and \(\left(-\tfrac{1}{4},-\tfrac{1}{4}\right)\); relative minima at \(\left(\tfrac{1}{4},-\tfrac{1}{4}\right)\) and \(\left(-\tfrac{1}{4},\tfrac{1}{4}\right)\).
problems.solution: Let \(f=xy\,e^{-8(x^{2}+y^{2})}\). Then \(f_x=y(1-16x^{2})e^{-8(x^{2}+y^{2})}\) and \(f_y=x(1-16y^{2})e^{-8(x^{2}+y^{2})}\). Setting both to zero gives \((0,0)\) and the four points \(\left(\pm\tfrac{1}{4},\pm\tfrac{1}{4}\right)\). At the four nonzero points, \(f_{xy}=(1-16x^{2})(1-16y^{2})e^{-8(x^{2}+y^{2})}=0\), and direct computation gives \[ f_{xx} = -16xy\,e^{-8(x^{2}+y^{2})}, \qquad f_{yy} = -16xy\,e^{-8(x^{2}+y^{2})}. \] So \(D=f_{xx}f_{yy}>0\) at all four; the sign of \(f_{xx}\) is opposite to \(\operatorname{sign}(xy)\), giving maxima where \(xy>0\) and minima where \(xy<0\). At \((0,0)\), \(f_{xx}=f_{yy}=0\) and \(f_{xy}=1\), so \(D=-1<0\): a saddle.

problems.problem: Find and classify all the critical points of the given function. \(\displaystyle f\left( {x,y} \right) = 8x - x\sqrt {y - 1} + {x^3} + \frac{1}{2}y - 12{x^2}\)
problems.solution: For \(f=8x-x\sqrt{y-1}+x^{3}+\tfrac{1}{2}y-12x^{2}\) (with \(y>1\)), \(f_y=-\tfrac{x}{2\sqrt{y-1}}+\tfrac{1}{2}=0\) gives \(\sqrt{y-1}=x\) (so \(x\geq 0\)). Then \(f_x=8-x+3x^{2}-24x=3x^{2}-25x+8=0\) yields \(x=8\) or \(x=\tfrac{1}{3}\), so points \((8,65)\) and \(\left(\tfrac{1}{3},\tfrac{10}{9}\right)\). With \(f_{xx}=6x-24\), \(f_{yy}=\tfrac{x}{4(y-1)^{3/2}}\), \(f_{xy}=-\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt{y-1}}\): \[ D(8,65)=24\cdot\tfrac{1}{256}-\tfrac{1}{256}=\tfrac{23}{256}>0,\ f_{xx}>0; \quad D(\tfrac{1}{3},\tfrac{10}{9})=-22\cdot\tfrac{9}{4}-\tfrac{9}{4}<0. \] So \((8,65)\) is a relative minimum and \(\left(\tfrac{1}{3},\tfrac{10}{9}\right)\) is a saddle.

problems.problem: Find and classify all the critical points of the given function. \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = \left( {y - 2} \right){x^2} - {y^2}\)
problems.answer: Relative maximum at \((0,0)\); saddles at \((2,2)\) and \((-2,2)\).

problems.problem: Find and classify all the critical points of the given function. \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 7x - 8y + 2xy - {x^2} + {y^3}\)
problems.solution: For \(f=7x-8y+2xy-x^{2}+y^{3}\), \(f_x=7+2y-2x=0\) gives \(x=\tfrac{7+2y}{2}\). Then \(f_y=-8+2x+3y^{2}=-8+(7+2y)+3y^{2}=3y^{2}+2y-1=0\), so \(y=\tfrac{1}{3}\) or \(y=-1\). This gives \(\left(\tfrac{23}{6},\tfrac{1}{3}\right)\) and \(\left(\tfrac{5}{2},-1\right)\). With \(f_{xx}=-2\), \(f_{yy}=6y\), \(f_{xy}=2\): \[ D(\tfrac{23}{6},\tfrac{1}{3})=(-2)(2)-4=-8<0;\quad D(\tfrac{5}{2},-1)=(-2)(-6)-4=8>0,\ f_{xx}<0. \] So the first point is a saddle and the second is a relative maximum.

problems.problem: Find and classify all the critical points of the given function. \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = \left( {3x + 4{x^3}} \right)\left( {{y^2} + 2y} \right)\)
Find and classify all the critical points of the given function. \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 3{y^3} - {x^2}{y^2} + 8{y^2} + 4{x^2} - 20y\)
problems.answer: Relative minimum at \(\left(0,\tfrac{-8+2\sqrt{61}}{9}\right)\); relative maximum at \(\left(0,\tfrac{-8-2\sqrt{61}}{9}\right)\); saddles at \((\pm 2\sqrt{3},2)\) and \((\pm 2,-2)\).
problems.solution: For \(f=3y^{3}-x^{2}y^{2}+8y^{2}+4x^{2}-20y\), \(f_x=2x(4-y^{2})\) and \(f_y=9y^{2}-2x^{2}y+16y-20\). From \(f_x=0\): \(x=0\) or \(y=\pm 2\). \[ x=0:\ 9y^{2}+16y-20=0\ \Rightarrow\ y=\tfrac{-8\pm 2\sqrt{61}}{9};\quad y=2:\ x=\pm 2\sqrt{3};\quad y=-2:\ x=\pm 2. \] With \(f_{xx}=8-2y^{2}\), \(f_{yy}=18y-2x^{2}+16\), \(f_{xy}=-4xy\): at the two \(x=0\) points, \(f_{xy}=0\) and \(f_{xx}f_{yy}>0\) by direct sign check, with \(f_{xx}>0\) for the larger \(y\) (relative minimum) and \(f_{xx}<0\) for the smaller \(y\) (relative maximum). At \(y=\pm 2\), \(f_{xx}=0\), so \(D=-f_{xy}^{2}<0\) and those four points are saddles.

problems.problem: Find the absolute minimum and absolute maximum of \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 18{x^2} + 4{y^2} - {y^2}x - 2\) on the triangle with vertices \(\left( { - 1, - 1} \right)\), \(\left( {5, - 1} \right)\) and \(\left( {5,17} \right)\).
problems.answer: Absolute maximum \(448\) at \((5,0)\); absolute minimum \(-2\) at \((0,0)\).
problems.solution: For \(f=18x^{2}+4y^{2}-y^{2}x-2\), \(f_x=36x-y^{2}\) and \(f_y=2y(4-x)\). Interior critical points (within the triangle): \((0,0)\) and \((4,12)\), with \(f(0,0)=-2\) and \(f(4,12)=286\). On \(y=-1\), \(f=18x^{2}-x+2\) has minimum near \(x=\tfrac{1}{36}\) with value \(\approx 2\); endpoints give \(21\) and \(447\). On \(x=5\), \(f=448-y^{2}\), maximum \(448\) at \(y=0\). On the hypotenuse \(y=3x+2\), the resulting cubic has interior maxima below \(448\). \[ \text{Max}=f(5,0)=448,\qquad \text{Min}=f(0,0)=-2. \]

problems.problem: Find the absolute minimum and absolute maximum of \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 2{x^3} - 4{y^3} + 24xy\) on the rectangle given by \(0 \le x \le 5\), \( - 3 \le y \le - 1\).
problems.answer: Absolute maximum \(134\) at \((5,-1)\); absolute minimum \(-64\) at \(\left(2^{5/3},-2^{4/3}\right)\).
problems.solution: For \(f=2x^{3}-4y^{3}+24xy\) on \([0,5]\times[-3,-1]\): \(f_x=6x^{2}+24y\) and \(f_y=-12y^{2}+24x\). Solving gives the interior critical point \(y^{3}=-16\), \(x=\tfrac{y^{2}}{2}\), i.e. \(y=-2^{4/3}\), \(x=2^{5/3}\), where \(f=128-192=-64\). On the four edges: \(y=-1\) yields critical \(x=2\) with \(f(2,-1)=-28\); \(y=-3\) yields \(x=2\sqrt{3}\) with \(f=108-96\sqrt{3}\approx -58.4\); the vertical edges give corners only. Vertex values: \(f(5,-1)=134\), \(f(5,-3)=-2\), \(f(0,-1)=4\), \(f(0,-3)=108\). \[ \text{Max}=134,\qquad \text{Min}=-64. \]

problems.problem: Find the absolute minimum and absolute maximum of \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = {x^2} - {y^2} + xy - 5x\) on the region bounded by \(y = 5 - {x^2}\) and the \(x\)-axis.
problems.answer: Absolute maximum \(5+5\sqrt{5}\) at \((-\sqrt{5},0)\); absolute minimum \(-25\) at \((0,5)\).
problems.solution: For \(f=x^{2}-y^{2}+xy-5x\), \(\nabla f=0\) gives \(x=2y\), \(y=1\), so \((2,1)\), which lies on the boundary parabola. On \(y=0\), \(x\in[-\sqrt{5},\sqrt{5}]\), \(f=x^{2}-5x\) has critical \(x=5/2\) outside the interval, so only the endpoints matter: \(f(\sqrt{5},0)=5-5\sqrt{5}\) and \(f(-\sqrt{5},0)=5+5\sqrt{5}\). On \(y=5-x^{2}\), substituting yields \(g(x)=-x^{4}-x^{3}+11x^{2}-25\); \(g'(x)=x(-4x^{2}-3x+22)=0\) gives \(x=0,2\) inside \([-\sqrt 5,\sqrt 5]\), with \(g(0)=-25\) and \(g(2)=-5\). \[ \text{Max}=5+5\sqrt{5},\qquad \text{Min}=-25. \]

problems.problem: Find the absolute minimum and absolute maximum of \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 192{x^3} + {y^2} - 4x{y^2}\) on the triangle with vertices \(\left( {0,0} \right)\), \(\left( {4,2} \right)\) and \(\left( { - 2,2} \right)\).
problems.answer: Absolute maximum \(12228\) at \((4,2)\); absolute minimum \(-1500\) at \((-2,2)\).
problems.solution: For \(f=192x^{3}+y^{2}-4xy^{2}\) on the triangle with vertices \((0,0),(4,2),(-2,2)\): \(f_x=576x^{2}-4y^{2}\), \(f_y=2y(1-4x)\). Solving gives \(y=0\) or \(x=\tfrac{1}{4}\), and combining with \(f_x=0\) yields \((0,0)\) and \((\tfrac{1}{4},\pm 3)\); the latter lie outside the region (which requires \(0\le y\le 2\)). On \(y=2\): \(f=192x^{3}-16x+4\), with critical points \(x=\pm\tfrac{1}{6}\), values \(\tfrac{20}{9}\) and \(\tfrac{52}{9}\). On the slanted edges (\(y=-x\) for \(x\in[-2,0]\) and \(y=x/2\) for \(x\in[0,4]\)), the critical points reduce to interior points already found or boundary endpoints. Comparing all candidates including vertices \(f(4,2)=12228\), \(f(-2,2)=-1500\), \(f(0,0)=0\): \[ \text{Max}=12228,\qquad \text{Min}=-1500. \]

problems.problem: Find the absolute minimum and absolute maximum of \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = \left( {9{x^2} - 1} \right)\left( {1 + 4y} \right)\) on the rectangle given by \( - 2 \le x \le 3\), \( - 1 \le y \le 4\).
problems.answer: Absolute maximum \(1360\) at \((3,4)\); absolute minimum \(-240\) at \((3,-1)\).
problems.solution: For \(f=(9x^{2}-1)(1+4y)\) on \([-2,3]\times[-1,4]\): \(f_x=18x(1+4y)\), \(f_y=4(9x^{2}-1)\). The critical lines \(x=\pm\tfrac{1}{3}\), \(y=-\tfrac{1}{4}\) give \(f=0\). On the four edges, \(f\) is linear in one variable or quadratic with critical \(x=0\). The candidate values are: \[ f(0,-1)=3,\ f(0,4)=-17,\ f(-2,-1)=-105,\ f(-2,4)=595,\ f(3,-1)=-240,\ f(3,4)=1360. \] So the maximum is \(1360\) and the minimum is \(-240\).

problems.problem: Find the maximum and minimum values of \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 10{y^2} - 4{x^2}\) subject to the constraint \({x^4} + {y^4} = 1\).
problems.solution: With \(f=10y^{2}-4x^{2}\) and \(g=x^{4}+y^{4}-1\), \(\nabla f=\lambda\nabla g\) gives \[ -8x=4\lambda x^{3},\qquad 20y=4\lambda y^{3}. \] From the first, \(x=0\) or \(\lambda x^{2}=-2\); from the second, \(y=0\) or \(\lambda y^{2}=5\). The mixed case forces \(\lambda\) to be both negative and positive, which is impossible. So either \(x=0\) (giving \(y=\pm 1\), \(f=10\)) or \(y=0\) (giving \(x=\pm 1\), \(f=-4\)). Maximum \(10\), minimum \(-4\).

problems.problem: Find the maximum and minimum values of \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 3x - 6y\) subject to the constraint \(4{x^2} + 2{y^2} = 25\).
problems.solution: With \(f=3x-6y\), \(g=4x^{2}+2y^{2}-25\): \((3,-6)=\lambda(8x,4y)\), so \(x=\tfrac{3}{8\lambda}\) and \(y=-\tfrac{3}{2\lambda}\). Substituting into the constraint: \(\tfrac{9}{16\lambda^{2}}+\tfrac{9}{2\lambda^{2}}=25\Rightarrow \lambda^{2}=\tfrac{81}{400}\), so \(\lambda=\pm\tfrac{9}{20}\). \[ \lambda=\tfrac{9}{20}:\ (x,y)=\left(\tfrac{5}{6},-\tfrac{10}{3}\right),\ f=\tfrac{45}{2}; \quad \lambda=-\tfrac{9}{20}:\ f=-\tfrac{45}{2}. \] Maximum \(\tfrac{45}{2}\), minimum \(-\tfrac{45}{2}\).

problems.problem: Find the maximum and minimum values of \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = xy\) subject to the constraint \({x^2} - y = 12\). Assume that \(y \le 0\) for this problem. Why is this assumption needed?
problems.solution: With \(f=xy\) and \(g=x^{2}-y-12\): \((y,x)=\lambda(2x,-1)\) gives \(\lambda=-x\) and \(y=-2x^{2}\). Combined with \(y=x^{2}-12\): \(-2x^{2}=x^{2}-12\Rightarrow x^{2}=4\), so \(x=\pm 2\) and \(y=-8\). \[ f(2,-8)=-16,\qquad f(-2,-8)=16. \] Without the assumption \(y\le 0\), the constraint \(y=x^{2}-12\) lets \(y\) (and \(x\)) tend to \(\infty\), so \(f=xy\) is unbounded above. The restriction makes the feasible set compact and ensures finite extrema.

problems.problem: Find the maximum and minimum values of \(f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = {x^2} + 3{y^2}\) subject to the constraint \({x^2} + 4{y^2} + {z^2} = 36\).
problems.solution: With \(f=x^{2}+3y^{2}\) and \(g=x^{2}+4y^{2}+z^{2}-36\): \((2x,6y,0)=\lambda(2x,8y,2z)\) gives \[ x(1-\lambda)=0,\quad y(6-8\lambda)=0,\quad \lambda z=0. \] Working through the cases: \((\pm 6,0,0)\) gives \(f=36\); \((0,\pm 3,0)\) gives \(f=27\); \((0,0,\pm 6)\) gives \(f=0\). Maximum \(36\), minimum \(0\).

problems.problem: Find the maximum and minimum values of \(f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = xyz\) subject to the constraint \({x^2} + 2{y^2} + 4{z^2} = 24\).
problems.answer: Maximum \(8\); minimum \(-8\) (each attained at \((\pm 2\sqrt{2},\pm 2,\pm\sqrt{2})\) with appropriate sign choices).
problems.solution:
With \(f=xyz\), \(g=x^{2}+2y^{2}+4z^{2}-24\): \(
abla f=\lambda
abla g\) gives \(yz=2\lambda x\), \(xz=4\lambda y\), \(xy=8\lambda z\). Assuming \(x,y,z
eq 0\), these imply \(x^{2}=2y^{2}\) and \(y^{2}=2z^{2}\). The constraint becomes \[ 2y^{2}+2y^{2}+2y^{2}=6y^{2}=24,\quad y^{2}=4. \] So \(y=\pm 2\), \(z^{2}=2\), \(x^{2}=8\), giving \(f^{2}=x^{2}y^{2}z^{2}=64\). The extrema are \(\pm 8\); cases with any coordinate zero give \(f=0\) and are not extreme.

problems.problem: Find the maximum and minimum values of \(f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = 2x + 4y + {z^2}\) subject to the constraints \({y^2} + {z^2} = 1\) and \({x^2} + {z^2} = 1\).
problems.solution:
With \(f=2x+4y+z^{2}\) and constraints \(g_{1}=y^{2}+z^{2}-1\), \(g_{2}=x^{2}+z^{2}-1\): \(
abla f=\lambda
abla g_{1}+\mu
abla g_{2}\) yields \(2=2\mu x\), \(4=2\lambda y\), and \(z(1-\lambda-\mu)=0\). If \(z=0\): \(y^{2}=x^{2}=1\), so \(f=2x+4y\) with extremes \(\pm 6\). If \(z
eq 0\): \(\lambda+\mu=1\), and combined with \(\lambda=	frac{2}{y}\), \(\mu=	frac{1}{x}\), \(y=\pm x\); both subcases force \(z^{2}<0\) or contradict \(z
eq 0\). \[ 	ext{Max}=6\ 	ext{at}\ (1,1,0),\qquad 	ext{Min}=-6\ 	ext{at}\ (-1,-1,0). \]

problems.problem: Find the maximum and minimum values of \(f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = x + y + {z^2}\) subject to the constraints \(x + y + z = 1\) and \({x^2} + {z^2} = 1\).
problems.solution:
For \(f=x+y+z^{2}\) with \(g_{1}=x+y+z-1\), \(g_{2}=x^{2}+z^{2}-1\): \(
abla f=\lambda
abla g_{1}+\mu
abla g_{2}\) gives \(\lambda=1\), \(2\mu x=0\), and \(z(1-\mu)=	frac{1}{2}\). Case \(\mu=0\): \(z=	frac{1}{2}\), \(x^{2}=	frac{3}{4}\), \(y=	frac{1}{2}-x\), giving \(f=	frac{3}{4}\). Case \(x=0\): \(z=\pm 1\), \(y=1-z\); \(z=1\Rightarrow f=1\), \(z=-1\Rightarrow f=3\). \[ 	ext{Max}=3,\qquad 	ext{Min}=	frac{3}{4}. \]

problems.problem: Find the maximum and minimum values of \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 81{x^2} + {y^2}\) subject to the constraint \(4{x^2} + {y^2} = 9\).
problems.solution: With \(f=81x^{2}+y^{2}\) and \(g=4x^{2}+y^{2}-9\): \((162x,2y)=\lambda(8x,2y)\) gives \(x(162-8\lambda)=0\) and \(y(1-\lambda)=0\). The two consistent cases are \(x=0\) (so \(y^{2}=9\), \(f=9\)) and \(y=0\) (so \(x^{2}=\tfrac{9}{4}\), \(f=\tfrac{729}{4}\)). The mixed case requires \(\lambda=\tfrac{81}{4}\) and \(\lambda=1\) simultaneously, which is impossible. Maximum \(\tfrac{729}{4}\), minimum \(9\).

problems.problem: Find the maximum and minimum values of \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 8{x^2} - 2y\) subject to the constraint \({x^2} + {y^2} = 1\).
Find the maximum and minimum values of \(f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = {y^2} - 10z\) subject to the constraint \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 36\).
Find the maximum and minimum values of \(f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = xyz\) subject to the constraint \(x + 9{y^2} + {z^2} = 4\). Assume that \(x \ge 0\) for this problem. Why is this assumption needed?
problems.answer: Maximum \(\tfrac{2}{3}\); minimum \(-\tfrac{2}{3}\) (at \((2,\pm\tfrac{1}{3},\pm 1)\) with the sign of \(yz\) matching).
problems.solution: With \(f=xyz\) and \(g=x+9y^{2}+z^{2}-4\): \((yz,xz,xy)=\lambda(1,18y,2z)\). Assuming \(y,z\neq 0\), \(xz=18\lambda y\) and \(yz=\lambda\) give \(x=18y^{2}\); similarly \(x=2z^{2}\), so \(z^{2}=9y^{2}\). The constraint becomes \(18y^{2}+9y^{2}+9y^{2}=36y^{2}=4\), so \(y^{2}=\tfrac{1}{9}\), \(z^{2}=1\), \(x=2\). Then \(f=xyz=2\cdot(\pm\tfrac{1}{3})(\pm 1)=\pm\tfrac{2}{3}\). Without \(x\geq 0\), as \(x\to-\infty\) the constraint allows \(9y^{2}+z^{2}=4-x\to\infty\), so \(|y|,|z|\) and \(|x|\) all grow without bound and \(|xyz|\to\infty\); the assumption keeps the feasible set compact.

problems.problem: Find the maximum and minimum values of \(f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = 3{x^2} + y\) subject to the constraints \(4x - 3y = 9\) and \({x^2} + {z^2} = 9\).

Use the Midpoint Rule to estimate the volume under \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 4x + 8y\) and above the rectangle given by \(0 \le x \le 4\), \(2 \le y \le 6\) in the \(xy\)-plane. Use 4 subdivisions in the \(x\) direction and 4 subdivisions in the \(y\) direction.
problems.solution: With \(\Delta x = 1\) and \(\Delta y = 1\) the midpoints are \(x_i \in \{0.5,1.5,2.5,3.5\}\) and \(y_j \in \{2.5,3.5,4.5,5.5\}\). The Midpoint Rule gives \[ V \approx \sum_{i=1}^{4}\sum_{j=1}^{4}(4x_i+8y_j)\,\Delta x\,\Delta y. \] Since \(\sum 4x_i = 32\) and \(\sum 8y_j = 128\), \[ V \approx 4(32) + 4(128) = 128 + 512 = 640. \]

problems.problem: Use the Midpoint Rule to estimate the volume under \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 4x - {y^2}\) and above the rectangle given by \(0 \le x \le 2\), \( - 2 \le y \le 1\) in the \(xy\)-plane. Use 2 subdivisions in the \(x\) direction and 3 subdivisions in the \(y\) direction.
problems.solution: With \(\Delta x = 1\), \(\Delta y = 1\), midpoints are \(x_i \in \{0.5,1.5\}\) and \(y_j \in \{-1.5,-0.5,0.5\}\). Then \[ V \approx \sum_{i,j}(4x_i - y_j^2). \] \(\sum 4x_i = 8\) (per row of 3 \(y\) values gives \(24\) total). \(\sum y_j^2 = 2.75\) per column of 2 \(x\) values gives \(5.5\). So \(V \approx 24 - 5.5 = \tfrac{37}{2}\).

problems.problem: Use the Midpoint Rule to estimate the volume under \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = {x^2} + y\) and above the rectangle given by \( - 1 \le x \le 3\), \(0 \le y \le 4\) in the \(xy\)-plane. Use 4 subdivisions in the \(x\) direction and 2 subdivisions in the \(y\) direction.
problems.solution: With \(\Delta x = 1\), \(\Delta y = 2\), the midpoints are \(x_i \in \{-0.5,0.5,1.5,2.5\}\) and \(y_j \in \{1,3\}\). The Midpoint Rule gives \[ V \approx \sum_{i,j}(x_i^2 + y_j)\,\Delta x\,\Delta y. \] \(\sum x_i^2 = 9\) (over 2 \(y\) values: 18, times \(\Delta A=2\) gives 36). \(\sum y_j = 4\) (over 4 \(x\) values: 16, times 2 gives 32). Total \(36+32=68\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{8y{x^3}\,dA}}\) where \(D = \left\{ {\left( {x,y} \right)| - 1 \le y \le 2, - 1 \le x \le 1 + {y^2}} \right\}\)
problems.solution: Set up with \(y\) outer since \(x\) bounds depend on \(y\): \[ \int_{-1}^{2}\int_{-1}^{1+y^2} 8yx^3\,dx\,dy = \int_{-1}^{2} 2y\big[(1+y^2)^4 - 1\big]\,dy. \] Substituting \(u=1+y^2\), \(du=2y\,dy\) (limits \(2\to 5\)) gives \[ \int_{2}^{5}(u^4-1)\,du = \left[\tfrac{u^5}{5}-u\right]_{2}^{5} = \tfrac{3078}{5}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{12{x^2}y - {y^2}\,dA}}\) where \(D = \left\{ {\left( {x,y} \right)| - 2 \le x \le 2, - {x^2} \le y \le {x^2}} \right\}\)
problems.solution: With \(x\) outer and \(y\in[-x^2,x^2]\), the inner integral is \[ \int_{-x^2}^{x^2}(12x^2 y - y^2)\,dy = 0 - \tfrac{2}{3}x^6 = -\tfrac{2}{3}x^6 \] (the \(12x^2 y\) part is odd in \(y\)). Then \[ \int_{-2}^{2} -\tfrac{2}{3}x^6\,dx = -\tfrac{2}{3}\cdot\tfrac{2\cdot 128}{7} = -\tfrac{512}{21}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{9 - \frac{{6{y^2}}}{{{x^2}}}\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region in the 1 st quadrant bounded by \(y = {x^3}\) and \(y = 4x\).
problems.solution: On \([0,2]\) the curve \(y=4x\) lies above \(y=x^3\). Take \(x\) outer: \[ \int_{0}^{2}\int_{x^3}^{4x}\!\left(9-\tfrac{6y^2}{x^2}\right)dy\,dx = \int_{0}^{2}\!\left[9(4x-x^3) - \tfrac{2}{x^2}(64x^3 - x^9)\right]dx. \] Simplifying gives \(\int_{0}^{2}(-92x - 9x^3 + 2x^7)\,dx = -184 - 36 + 64 = -156.\)

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{15{x^2} - 6y\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region bounded by \(x = \frac{1}{2}{y^2}\) and \(x = 4\sqrt y \).
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{6y{{\left( {x + 6} \right)}^2}\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region bounded by \(x = - {y^2}\) and \(x = y - 6\).
problems.solution: The curves \(x=-y^2\) and \(x=y-6\) meet at \(y=-3,2\); on this range \(-y^2 > y-6\). Take \(y\) outer: \[ \int_{-3}^{2}\int_{y-6}^{-y^2} 6y(x+6)^2\,dx\,dy = \int_{-3}^{2} 2y\big[(6-y^2)^3 - y^3\big]\,dy. \] Expanding and integrating term by term yields \(-\tfrac{375}{4}\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{{{\bf{e}}^{{y^{\,2}} + 1}}\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the triangle with vertices \(\left( {0,0} \right)\), \(\left( { - 2,4} \right)\) and \(\left( {8,4} \right)\).
problems.solution: The triangle has edges \(y=-2x\), \(y=x/2\), and \(y=4\). Because \(e^{y^2+1}\) cannot be integrated in \(y\), put \(y\) outer with \(x\in[-y/2, 2y]\): \[ \int_{0}^{4}\int_{-y/2}^{2y} e^{y^2+1}\,dx\,dy = \int_{0}^{4} \tfrac{5y}{2}\,e^{y^2+1}\,dy. \] With \(u=y^2+1\), this is \(\tfrac{5}{4}\int_{1}^{17} e^u\,du = \tfrac{5}{4}(e^{17}-e).\)

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{7{y^3}{{\bf{e}}^{{x^{\,2}} + 1}}\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region bounded by\(y = 2\,\,\sqrt[4]{x}\), \(x = 9\) and the \(x\)-axis.
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{{x^5}\sin \left( {{y^4}} \right)\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region in the 2 nd quadrant bounded by \(y = 3{x^2}\), \(y = 12\) and the \(y\)-axis.
problems.solution: Because \(\sin(y^4)\) blocks integrating in \(y\) first, switch the order. The 2nd-quadrant region is \(0\le y\le 12\), \(-\sqrt{y/3}\le x\le 0\): \[ \int_{0}^{12}\int_{-\sqrt{y/3}}^{0} x^5\sin(y^4)\,dx\,dy = -\int_{0}^{12}\tfrac{y^3}{162}\sin(y^4)\,dy. \] With \(u=y^4\), this becomes \(-\tfrac{1}{648}[1-\cos(20736)] = \tfrac{\cos(20736)-1}{648}.\)

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{\frac{{{x^3}}}{{{y^2}}}\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region bounded by \(\displaystyle y = \frac{1}{{{x^2}}}\), \(x = 1\) and \(\displaystyle y = \frac{1}{4}\) in the order given below. Integrate with respect to \(x\) first and then \(y\). Integrate with respect to \(y\) first and then \(x\).
problems.solution: The region is \(1\le x\le 2\), \(\tfrac14\le y\le \tfrac{1}{x^2}\). With \(dy\) inner: \[ \int_{1}^{2}\int_{1/4}^{1/x^2}\tfrac{x^3}{y^2}\,dy\,dx = \int_{1}^{2}(4x^3 - x^5)\,dx = \tfrac{9}{2}. \] With \(dx\) inner (\(y\in[1/4,1]\), \(x\in[1, 1/\sqrt{y}]\)): \[ \int_{1/4}^{1}\tfrac{1}{4y^2}\!\left(\tfrac{1}{y^2}-1\right)dy = \tfrac{9}{2}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{xy - {y^3}\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region bounded by \(y = {x^2}\), \(y = - {x^2}\) and \(x = 2\) in the order given below. Integrate with respect to \(x\) first and then \(y\). Integrate with respect to \(y\) first and then \(x\).
problems.solution: The integrand \(xy - y^3\) is odd in \(y\) and the strip \(-x^2\le y\le x^2\) is symmetric, so with \(dy\) inner the \(y\) integral vanishes: \[ \int_{0}^{2}\int_{-x^2}^{x^2}(xy - y^3)\,dy\,dx = 0. \] Reversing to \(dx\) inner with \(y\in[-4,4]\), \(x\in[\sqrt{|y|},2]\) likewise gives 0 since each surviving term is odd in \(y\).

problems.problem: Evaluate\( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{42{y^2} - 12x\,dA}}\) where \(D = \left\{ {\left( {x,y} \right)|0 \le x \le 4,{{\left( {x - 2} \right)}^2} \le y \le 6} \right\}\)
problems.solution: With \(x\) outer and \(y\in[(x-2)^2,6]\): \[ \int_{0}^{4}\int_{(x-2)^2}^{6}(42y^2-12x)\,dy\,dx = \int_{0}^{4}\!\left[3024 - 72x - 14(x-2)^6 + 12x(x-2)^2\right]dx. \] Substituting \(u=x-2\) makes the integrand odd-plus-even on \([-2,2]\); the even part gives \(2\int_{0}^{2}(2880 - 14u^6 + 24u^2)\,du = 11136.\)

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{2y{x^2} + 9{y^3}\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region bounded by \( \displaystyle y = \frac{2}{3}x\) and \(y = 2\sqrt x \).
problems.solution: The curves meet at \(x=0,9\) with \(2\sqrt{x}\geq 2x/3\). Take \(x\) outer: \[ \int_{0}^{9}\int_{2x/3}^{2\sqrt x}(2yx^2 + 9y^3)\,dy\,dx = \int_{0}^{9}\!\left[4x^3 + 36x^2 - \tfrac{8x^4}{9}\right]dx. \] This evaluates to \(6561 + 8748 - \tfrac{472392}{45} = \tfrac{24057}{5}.\)

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{10{x^2}{y^3} - 6\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region bounded by \(x = - 2{y^2}\) and \(x = {y^3}\).
problems.solution: The curves \(x=-2y^2\) and \(x=y^3\) meet at \(y=-2,0\); on this range \(y^3 \geq -2y^2\). Take \(y\) outer: \[ \int_{-2}^{0}\int_{-2y^2}^{y^3}(10x^2 y^3 - 6)\,dx\,dy = \int_{-2}^{0}\!\left[\tfrac{10}{3}y^{12} - 6y^3 + \tfrac{80}{3}y^9 - 12y^2\right]dy. \] Evaluating gives \(-\tfrac{8296}{13}\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{x\left( {y - 1} \right)\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region bounded by \(y = 1 - {x^2}\) and \(y = {x^2} - 3\).
problems.solution: The curves meet at \(x=\pm\sqrt 2\) and the region \(x^2-3\le y\le 1-x^2\) is symmetric in \(x\). The integrand \(x(y-1)\) is odd in \(x\), so \[ \iint_D x(y-1)\,dA = 0. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{5{x^3}\cos \left( {{y^3}} \right)\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region bounded by \(y = 2\), \( \displaystyle y = \frac{1}{4}{x^2}\) and the \(y\)-axis.
problems.solution: Switch to \(y\) outer with \(y\in[0,2]\), \(x\in[0,2\sqrt y]\) so we can attack \(\cos(y^3)\) via substitution: \[ \int_{0}^{2}\int_{0}^{2\sqrt y} 5x^3\cos(y^3)\,dx\,dy = \int_{0}^{2} 20y^2\cos(y^3)\,dy. \] With \(u=y^3\), this is \(\tfrac{20}{3}\int_{0}^{8}\cos u\,du = \tfrac{20}{3}\sin(8).\)

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{\frac{1}{{{y^{\frac{1}{3}}}\left( {{x^3} + 1} \right)}}\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region bounded by \(x = - {y^{\frac{1}{3}}}\), \(x = 3\) and the \(x\)-axis.
problems.solution: The three boundary curves meet at \((0,0)\), \((3,0)\) and \((3,-27)\); the region lies in \(y\le 0\). Switching to \(x\) outer with \(y\in[-x^3,0]\): \[ \int_{0}^{3}\int_{-x^3}^{0}\frac{dy}{y^{1/3}(x^3+1)}\,dx = \int_{0}^{3} -\frac{3x^2}{2(x^3+1)}\,dx. \] With \(u=x^3+1\): \(-\tfrac{1}{2}\ln u \Big|_{1}^{28} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\ln 28.\)

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{7{x^2} + 14y\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region bounded by \(x = 2{y^2}\) and \(x = 8\) in the order given below. Integrate with respect to \(x\) first and then \(y\). Integrate with respect to \(y\) first and then \(x\).
problems.solution: With \(y\) outer (\(y\in[-2,2]\), \(x\in[2y^2,8]\)): \[ \int_{-2}^{2}\int_{2y^2}^{8}(7x^2+14y)\,dx\,dy = \int_{-2}^{2}\!\left[\tfrac{3584}{3} - \tfrac{56y^6}{3}\right]dy = 4096. \] With \(x\) outer (\(x\in[0,8]\), \(|y|\le\sqrt{x/2}\)) the \(14y\) term vanishes by symmetry and \[ \int_{0}^{8} 14x^2 \sqrt{x/2}\cdot 2\cdot\tfrac{1}{2}\,dx = 4096. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{3x{y^2} - 2\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the unit circle centered at the origin.
problems.solution: In polar with \(D=\{0\le r\le 1, 0\le\theta\le 2\pi\}\) and \(3xy^2 = 3r^3\cos\theta\sin^2\theta\): \[ \int_{0}^{2\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}(3r^3\cos\theta\sin^2\theta - 2)r\,dr\,d\theta = \int_{0}^{2\pi}\!\left[\tfrac{3}{5}\cos\theta\sin^2\theta - 1\right]d\theta. \] The first term integrates to 0 over a full period, leaving \(-2\pi\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{4x - 2y\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the top half of region between \({x^2} + {y^2} = 4\) and \({x^2} + {y^2} = 25\).
problems.solution: Top half annulus: \(\theta\in[0,\pi]\), \(r\in[2,5]\). Then \[ \int_{0}^{\pi}\!\!\int_{2}^{5}(4r\cos\theta - 2r\sin\theta)\,r\,dr\,d\theta = \big[4\sin\theta+2\cos\theta\big]_0^{\pi}\cdot\tfrac{125-8}{3}. \] This is \((-4)(39) = -156\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{6xy + 4{x^2}\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the portion of \({x^2} + {y^2} = 9\) in the 2nd quadrant.
problems.solution: The 2nd-quadrant disk piece is \(\theta\in[\pi/2,\pi]\), \(r\in[0,3]\). With \(6xy = 3r^2\sin 2\theta\) and \(4x^2 = 4r^2\cos^2\theta\): \[ \int_{\pi/2}^{\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{3}(3r^2\sin 2\theta + 4r^2\cos^2\theta)r\,dr\,d\theta = \tfrac{81}{4}\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi}(3\sin 2\theta + 2 + 2\cos 2\theta)\,d\theta. \] The \(\theta\) integral equals \(\pi-3\), giving \(\tfrac{81(\pi-3)}{4}\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{\sin \left( {3{x^2} + 3{y^2}} \right)\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region between \({x^2} + {y^2} = 1\) and \({x^2} + {y^2} = 7\).
problems.solution: The annulus \(1\le r^2\le 7\) becomes \(1\le r\le\sqrt 7\). With \(u=3r^2\): \[ \int_{0}^{2\pi}\!\!\int_{1}^{\sqrt 7}\sin(3r^2)\,r\,dr\,d\theta = 2\pi\cdot\tfrac{1}{6}\int_{3}^{21}\sin u\,du = \tfrac{\pi}{3}(\cos 3 - \cos 21). \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{{{\bf{e}}^{1 - {x^{\,2}} - {y^{\,2}}}}\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region in the 4th quadrant between \({x^2} + {y^2} = 16\) and \({x^2} + {y^2} = 36\).
Use a double integral to determine the area of the region that is inside \(r = 6 - 4\cos \theta \).
problems.solution: Since \(6>4\), this limaçon has no inner loop. \[ A = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{2\pi}(6-4\cos\theta)^2\,d\theta = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{2\pi}(44 - 48\cos\theta + 8\cos 2\theta)\,d\theta = 44\pi. \]

problems.problem: Use a double integral to determine the area of the region that is inside \(r = 4\) and outside \(r = 8 + 6\sin \theta \).
problems.solution: Inside \(r=4\) and outside \(r=8+6\sin\theta\) requires \(8+6\sin\theta\le 4\), i.e. \(\sin\theta\le -\tfrac{2}{3}\). With \(\alpha=\arcsin(2/3)\), this is \(\theta\in[\pi+\alpha,\,2\pi-\alpha]\). \[ A = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_{\pi+\alpha}^{2\pi-\alpha}\!\!\big[16 - (8+6\sin\theta)^2\big]\,d\theta. \] Expanding and evaluating gives \(28\sqrt 5 + 66\arcsin(\tfrac{2}{3}) - 33\pi\) (about \(7.06\)).

problems.problem: Evaluate the following integral by first converting to an integral in polar coordinates. \(\int_{{ - 2}}^{0}{{\int_{{ - \sqrt {4 - {y^{\,2}}} }}^{{\sqrt {4 - {y^{\,2}}} }}{{\,\,\,{x^2}\,dx}}\,dy}}\)
problems.solution: The region is the lower half of the disk \(x^2+y^2\le 4\): \(\theta\in[\pi,2\pi]\), \(r\in[0,2]\). With \(x^2 = r^2\cos^2\theta\): \[ \int_{\pi}^{2\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{2} r^2\cos^2\theta\cdot r\,dr\,d\theta = \int_{\pi}^{2\pi}\cos^2\theta\,d\theta\cdot 4 = \tfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot 4 = 2\pi. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate the following integral by first converting to an integral in polar coordinates. \(\int_{{ - 1}}^{1}{{\int_{0}^{{\sqrt {1 - {x^{\,2}}} }}{{\,\,\,\sqrt {{x^2} + {y^2}} \,dy}}\,dx}}\)
problems.solution: Top half of the unit disk: \(\theta\in[0,\pi]\), \(r\in[0,1]\), and \(\sqrt{x^2+y^2}=r\): \[ \int_{0}^{\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{1} r\cdot r\,dr\,d\theta = \pi\cdot\tfrac{1}{3} = \tfrac{\pi}{3}. \]

problems.problem: Use a double integral to determine the volume of the solid that is below \(z = 9 - 4{x^2} - 4{y^2}\) and above the \(xy\)-plane.
Use a double integral to determine the volume of the solid that is bounded by \(z = 12 - 3{x^2} - 3{y^2}\) and \(z = {x^2} + {y^2} - 8\).
Use a double integral to determine the volume of the solid that is inside both the cylinder \({x^2} + {y^2} = 9\) and the sphere \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 16\).
problems.solution: Inside the cylinder \(r=3\) and the sphere of radius 4, \(z\) runs from \(-\sqrt{16-r^2}\) to \(\sqrt{16-r^2}\): \[ V = \int_{0}^{2\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{3} 2\sqrt{16-r^2}\,r\,dr\,d\theta = 4\pi\cdot\tfrac{1}{3}\big[-(16-r^2)^{3/2}\big]_0^{3} \cdot (-1). \] This evaluates to \(\tfrac{4\pi}{3}(64-7\sqrt 7)\).

problems.problem: Use a double integral to derive the area of a circle of radius \(a\).
problems.solution: In polar the disk of radius \(a\) is \(\{0\le r\le a, 0\le\theta\le 2\pi\}\): \[ A = \int_{0}^{2\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{a} r\,dr\,d\theta = 2\pi\cdot\tfrac{a^2}{2} = \pi a^2. \]

problems.problem: Use a double integral to derive the area of the region between circles of radius a and b with \(\alpha \le \theta \le \beta \). See the image below for a sketch of the region.
problems.solution: With \(\theta\in[\alpha,\beta]\) and \(r\in[a,b]\), \[ A = \int_{\alpha}^{\beta}\!\!\int_{a}^{b} r\,dr\,d\theta = (\beta-\alpha)\cdot\tfrac{b^2-a^2}{2}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{{y^2} + 3x\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the region in the 3rd quadrant between \({x^2} + {y^2} = 1\) and \({x^2} + {y^2} = 9\).
problems.solution: 3rd-quadrant annulus: \(\theta\in[\pi,3\pi/2]\), \(r\in[1,3]\). With \(y^2+3x = r^2\sin^2\theta + 3r\cos\theta\): \[ \int_{\pi}^{3\pi/2}\!\!\int_{1}^{3}(r^3\sin^2\theta + 3r^2\cos\theta)\,dr\,d\theta = \int_{\pi}^{3\pi/2}\!(20\sin^2\theta + 26\cos\theta)\,d\theta = 5\pi - 26. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{\sqrt {1 + 4{x^2} + 4{y^2}} \,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the bottom half of \({x^2} + {y^2} = 16\).
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{D}{{4xy - 7\,dA}}\) where \(D\) is the portion of \({x^2} + {y^2} = 2\) in the 1st quadrant.
problems.solution: Q1 disk piece, \(r\in[0,\sqrt 2]\), \(\theta\in[0,\pi/2]\). With \(4xy = 2r^2\sin 2\theta\): \[ \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\!\!\int_{0}^{\sqrt 2}(2r^3\sin 2\theta - 7r)\,dr\,d\theta = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\!(2\sin 2\theta - 7)\,d\theta = 2 - \tfrac{7\pi}{2}. \]

problems.problem: Use a double integral to determine the area of the region that is inside \(r = 4 + 2\sin \theta \) and outside \(r = 3 - \sin \theta \).
problems.solution: The curves meet when \(\sin\theta = -1/3\). With \(\alpha=\arcsin(1/3)\), the region lies on \(\theta\in[-\alpha,\pi+\alpha]\). \[ A = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_{-\alpha}^{\pi+\alpha}\!\big[(4+2\sin\theta)^2 - (3-\sin\theta)^2\big]\,d\theta. \] Expanding to \(17/2 + 22\sin\theta - (3/2)\cos 2\theta\) and using \(\sin\alpha=1/3,\cos\alpha=2\sqrt 2/3\) gives the stated value.

problems.problem: Evaluate the following integral by first converting to an integral in polar coordinates. \(\int_{0}^{3}{{\int_{{ - \sqrt {9 - {x^{\,2}}} }}^{0}{{\,\,\,{{\bf{e}}^{{x^{\,2}} + {y^{\,2}}}}\,dy}}\,dx}}\)
Use a double integral to determine the volume of the solid that is inside the cylinder \({x^2} + {y^2} = 16\), below \(z = 2{x^2} + 2{y^2}\) and above the \(xy\)-plane.
problems.solution: Inside \(r=4\), above \(z=0\), below \(z=2r^2\): \[ V = \int_{0}^{2\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{4} 2r^2\cdot r\,dr\,d\theta = 2\pi\cdot 2\cdot\tfrac{4^4}{4} = 256\pi. \]

problems.problem: Use a double integral to determine the volume of the solid that is bounded by \(z = 8 - {x^2} - {y^2}\) and \(z = 3{x^2} + 3{y^2} - 4\).

problems.solution: Innermost \(\int_{0}^{2z}(3x-\sqrt{1+z^2})\,dx = 6z^2 - 2z\sqrt{1+z^2}\). \[ \int_{0}^{1}\!\left(6z^2 - 2z\sqrt{1+z^2}\right)dz = 2 - \tfrac{2}{3}(2\sqrt 2 - 1) = \tfrac{8 - 4\sqrt 2}{3}. \] Outer integration over \(y\in[-1,2]\) (length 3) gives \(8 - 4\sqrt 2\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{12y\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region below \(6x + 4y + 3z = 12\) in the first octant.
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{5{x^2}\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region below \(x + 2y + 4z = 8\) in the first octant.
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{10{z^2} - x\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region below \(z = 8 - y\) and above the region in the \(xy\)-plane bounded by \(y = 2x\), \(x = 3\) and \(y = 0\).
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{4{y^2}\,dV}}\)where \(E\) is the region below \(z = - 3{x^2} - 3{y^2}\) and above \(z = - 12\).

Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{2y - 9z\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region behind \(6x + 3y + 3z = 15\) front of the triangle in the \(xy\)-plane with vertices, in \(\left( {x,z} \right)\) form :\(\left( {0,0} \right)\), \(\left( {0,4} \right)\)and \(\left( {2,4} \right)\).
problems.solution: Reading the \(xz\)-plane triangle as \(0\le x\le 2\), \(2x\le z\le 4\), and \(y\in[0, 5-2x-z]\): \[ \int_{0}^{2}\!\!\int_{2x}^{4}\!\!\int_{0}^{5-2x-z}(2y-9z)\,dy\,dz\,dx. \] After the \(y\) integration the integrand reduces to \(25 + 4x^2 + 10z^2 - 20x - 55z + 22xz\), and the remaining integration evaluates to \(-\tfrac{100}{3}\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{18x\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region behind the surface \(y = 4 - {x^2}\) that is in front of the region in the \(xz\)-plane bounded by \(z = - 3x\), \(z = 2x\) and \(z = 2\).
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{20{x^3}\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region bounded by \(x = 2 - {y^2} - {z^2}\) and \(x = 5{y^2} + 5{z^2} - 6\).
problems.solution: Use \(yz\)-polar with \(r^2=y^2+z^2\). The paraboloids meet at \(r^2=4/3\) and \(x\in[5r^2-6, 2-r^2]\). \[ \int_{0}^{2\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{2/\sqrt 3} 5\big[(2-r^2)^4 - (5r^2-6)^4\big]r\,dr\,d\theta. \] With \(u=r^2\) the radial integral is \(5\big[F(4/3)-F(0)\big]\) where \(F(u) = -\tfrac{(2-u)^5}{5} - \tfrac{(5u-6)^5}{25}\), giving the stated value.

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{6{z^2}\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region behind \(x + 6y + 2z = 8\) that is in front of the region in the \(xy\)-plane bounded by \(z = 2y\) and \(z = \sqrt {4y} \).
problems.solution: Reading the \"region in the \(xy\)-plane\" as the \(yz\)-region bounded by \(z=2y\) and \(z=2\sqrt y\) (intersect at \(y=0,1\)), with \(x\in[0,8-6y-2z]\): \[ \int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{2y}^{2\sqrt y} 6z^2(8-6y-2z)\,dz\,dy = 80 - \tfrac{192}{7} - 48 = \tfrac{32}{7}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{8y\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region between \(x + y + z = 6\) and \(x + y + z = 10\) above the triangle in the \(xy\)-plane with vertices, in \(\left( {x,y} \right)\) form : \(\left( {0,0} \right)\), \(\left( {1,2} \right)\) and \(\left( {1,4} \right)\).

Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{8y\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region between \(x + y + z = 6\) and \(x + y + z = 10\) in front of the triangle in the \(xy\)-plane with vertices, in \(\left( {x,z} \right)\) form : \(\left( {0,0} \right)\), \(\left( {1,2} \right)\) and \(\left( {1,4} \right)\).
problems.solution: With the triangle in the \(xz\)-plane (\(x\in[0,1]\), \(2x\le z\le 4x\)), \(y\) lies between the two planes: \(y\in[6-x-z, 10-x-z]\). Difference of squares gives \[ \int 8y\,dy = 4y^2\Big|_{6-x-z}^{10-x-z} = 16(16-2x-2z), \] \[ \int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{2x}^{4x}(256-32x-32z)\,dz\,dx = \int_{0}^{1}(512x-256x^2)\,dx = \tfrac{512}{3}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{8y\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region between \(x + y + z = 6\) and \(x + y + z = 10\) in front of the triangle in the \(xy\)-plane with vertices, in \(\left( {y,z} \right)\) form : \(\left( {0,0} \right)\), \(\left( {1,2} \right)\) and \(\left( {1,4} \right)\).
Use a triple integral to determine the volume of the region below \(z = 8 - y\) and above the region in the \(xy\)-plane bounded by \(y = 2x\), \(x = 3\) and \(y = 0\).
Use a triple integral to determine the volume of the region in the 1st octant that is below \(4x + 8y + z = 16\).

Use a triple integral to determine the volume of the region behind \(6x + 3y + 3z = 15\) front of the triangle in the \(xz\)-plane with vertices, in \(\left( {x,z} \right)\) form :\(\left( {0,0} \right)\), \(\left( {0,4} \right)\)and \(\left( {2,4} \right)\).
Use a triple integral to determine the volume of the region bounded by \(y = {x^2} + {z^2}\) and \(y = \sqrt {{x^2} + {z^2}} \).
problems.solution: Use polar in the \(xz\)-plane (axis is \(y\)): \(r^2=x^2+z^2\), \(y\in[r^2, r]\), \(r\in[0,1]\). \[ V = \int_{0}^{2\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}(r-r^2)\,r\,dr\,d\theta = 2\pi\!\left(\tfrac{1}{3}-\tfrac{1}{4}\right) = \tfrac{\pi}{6}. \]

problems.problem: Use a triple integral to determine the volume of the region behind \(x + 6y + 2z = 8\) that is in front of the region in the \(xy\)-plane bounded by \(z = 2y\) and \(z = \sqrt {4y} \).
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int_{0}^{1}{{\int_{0}^{{{z^{\,2}}}}{{\int_{0}^{3}{{y\cos \left( {{z^5}} \right)\,dx}}\,dy}}\,dz}}\)
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{6{z^2}\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region below \(4x + y + 2z = 10\) in the first octant.
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{3 - 4x\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region below \(z = 4 - xy\) and above the region in the \(xy\)-plane defined by \(0 \le x \le 2\), \(0 \le y \le 1\).

Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{12y - 8x\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region behind \(y = 10 - 2z\) and in front of the region in the \(xz\)-plane bounded by \(z = 2x\), \(z = 5\) and \(x = 0\).
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{yz\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region bounded by \(x = 2{y^2} + 2{z^2} - 5\) and the plane \(x = 1\).
problems.solution: In \(yz\)-polar (\(r^2=y^2+z^2\)) with \(yz = \tfrac{r^2}{2}\sin 2\theta\) and \(\theta\in[0,2\pi]\), the \(\theta\) integral of \(\sin 2\theta\) vanishes, so the integral is \(0\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{15z\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region between \(2x + y + z = 4\) and \(4x + 4y + 2z = 20\) that is in front of the region in the \(yz\)-plane bounded by \(z = 2{y^2}\) and \(z = \sqrt {4y} \).
problems.solution: \(yz\)-region: \(y\in[0,1]\), \(2y^2\le z\le 2\sqrt y\); \(x\) between the planes gives width \[ \tfrac{10-2y-z}{2} - \tfrac{4-y-z}{2} = \tfrac{6-y}{2}. \] \[ \iiint 15z\,dV = \tfrac{15}{2}\int_{0}^{1}(6-y)\!\int_{2y^2}^{2\sqrt y} z\,dz\,dy = 15\int_{0}^{1}(6y - 6y^4 - y^2 + y^5)\,dy = \tfrac{49}{2}. \]

problems.problem: Use a triple integral to determine the volume of the region below \(z = 4 - xy\) and above the region in the \(xy\)-plane defined by \(0 \le x \le 2\), \(0 \le y \le 1\).
Use a triple integral to determine the volume of the region that is below \(z = 8 - {x^2} - {y^2}\) above \(z = - \sqrt {4{x^2} + 4{y^2}} \) and inside \({x^2} + {y^2} = 4\).
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{8z\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region bounded by \(z = 2{x^2} + 2{y^2} - 4\) and \(z = 5 - {x^2} - {y^2}\) in the 1st octant.
problems.solution: Cylindrical, 1st octant (\(\theta\in[0,\pi/2]\)). The lower paraboloid \(z=2r^2-4\) hits \(z=0\) at \(r=\sqrt 2\); top \(z=5-r^2\) meets bottom at \(r=\sqrt 3\). Split: \[ \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\!\!\int_{0}^{\sqrt 2}\!\!\int_{0}^{5-r^2} 8z\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta + \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\!\!\int_{\sqrt 2}^{\sqrt 3}\!\!\int_{2r^2-4}^{5-r^2} 8z\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta. \] The pieces evaluate to \(\tfrac{98\pi}{3}\) and \(5\pi\), giving \(\tfrac{113\pi}{3}\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{6xy\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region above \(z = 2x - 10\), below \(z = 2\) and inside the cylinder \({x^2} + {y^2} = 4\).
problems.solution: In cylindrical, \(6xy = 3r^2\sin 2\theta\) and \(z\in[2r\cos\theta-10,\,2]\). The \(\theta\)-integrals \(\int_{0}^{2\pi}\sin 2\theta\,d\theta\) and \(\int_{0}^{2\pi}\sin 2\theta\cos\theta\,d\theta\) both vanish, so the integral is \(0\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{9y{z^3}\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region between \(x = - \sqrt {9{y^2} + 9{z^2}} \) and \(x = \sqrt {{y^2} + {z^2}} \) inside the cylinder \({y^2} + {z^2} = 1\).
problems.solution: Cylindrical with axis \(x\): \(y=r\cos\theta\), \(z=r\sin\theta\), \(r\in[0,1]\), \(x\in[-3r,r]\). The integrand \(9yz^3\) becomes \(9r^4\cos\theta\sin^3\theta\); since \(\int_{0}^{2\pi}\cos\theta\sin^3\theta\,d\theta = 0\), the result is \(0\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{x + 2\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region bounded by \(x = 18 - 4{y^2} - 4{z^2}\) and \(x = 2\) with \(z \ge 0\).
problems.solution: \(yz\)-polar with axis \(x\): paraboloid meets plane at \(r=2\); \(z\ge 0\) gives \(\theta\in[0,\pi]\); \(x\in[2, 18-4r^2]\). \[ \int(x+2)\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}+2x\big|_{2}^{18-4r^2}. \] \[ \int_{0}^{\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{2}(192 - 80r^2 + 8r^4)\,r\,dr\,d\theta = \pi\cdot\tfrac{448}{3} = \tfrac{448\pi}{3}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{x + 2\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region between the two planes \(2x + y + z = 6\) and \(6x + 3y + 3z = 12\) inside the cylinder \({x^2} + {z^2} = 16\).
problems.solution: \(xz\)-polar with axis \(y\): \(r\in[0,4]\), \(\theta\in[0,2\pi]\). \(y\in[4-2x-z, 6-2x-z]\) (width 2). \[ \iiint(x+2)\,dV = 2\int_{0}^{2\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{4}(r\cos\theta+2)\,r\,dr\,d\theta = 2\cdot 2\pi\cdot 16 = 64\pi. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{{x^2}\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region bounded by \(y = {x^2} + {z^2} - 4\) and \(y = 8 - 5{x^2} - 5{z^2}\) with \(x \le 0\).
problems.solution: \(xz\)-polar with axis \(y\): paraboloids meet at \(r^2=2\); \(x\le 0\) gives \(\theta\in[\pi/2,3\pi/2]\); \(y\in[r^2-4,\,8-5r^2]\) (width \(12-6r^2\)). \[ \int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}\!\!\int_{0}^{\sqrt 2} r^2\cos^2\theta\cdot r(12-6r^2)\,dr\,d\theta = \tfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot 4 = 2\pi. \]

problems.problem: Use a triple integral to determine the volume of the region bounded by \(z = \sqrt {{x^2} + {y^2}} \), and \(z = {x^2} + {y^2}\) in the 1st octant.
problems.solution: Cylindrical, 1st octant (\(\theta\in[0,\pi/2]\)). \(z=r\) and \(z=r^2\) meet at \(r=1\), and the cone is above the paraboloid. \[ V = \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}(r-r^2)\,r\,dr\,d\theta = \tfrac{\pi}{2}\!\left(\tfrac{1}{3}-\tfrac{1}{4}\right) = \tfrac{\pi}{24}. \]

problems.problem: Use a triple integral to determine the volume of the region bounded by \(y = \sqrt {9{x^2} + 9{z^2}} \), and \(y = - 3{x^2} - 3{z^2}\) in the 1st octant.
problems.solution: (To be reviewed — solution not generated.)

problems.problem: Use a triple integral to determine the volume of the region behind \(x = z + 3\), in front of \(x = - z - 6\) and inside the cylinder \({y^2} + {z^2} = 4\).
problems.solution: \(yz\)-polar with axis \(x\): \(r\in[0,2]\), \(\theta\in[0,2\pi]\). The thickness in \(x\) is \((z+3)-(-z-6) = 2z+9 = 2r\sin\theta+9\). \[ V = \int_{0}^{2\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{2}(2r\sin\theta + 9)\,r\,dr\,d\theta = 0 + 2\pi\cdot 18 = 36\pi. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate the following integral by first converting to an integral in cylindrical coordinates. \(\int_{{ - 4}}^{4}{{\int_{0}^{{\sqrt {16 - {y^{\,2}}} }}{{\int_{0}^{{6 + x}}{{\,\,\,6y{x^2}\,\,dz}}\,dx}}\,dy}}\)
problems.solution: Cylindrical (\(x=r\cos\theta\), \(y=r\sin\theta\)): right half disk \(\theta\in[-\pi/2,\pi/2]\), \(r\in[0,4]\), \(z\in[0,6+r\cos\theta]\). The integrand \(6yx^2\) becomes \(6r^3\sin\theta\cos^2\theta\), which is odd in \(\theta\) about 0; the integral is \(0\).

problems.problem: Evaluate the following integral by first converting to an integral in cylindrical coordinates. \(\int_{0}^{3}{{\int_{{ - \sqrt {9 - {x^{\,2}}} }}^{{\sqrt {9 - {x^{\,2}}} }}{{\int_{{ - \sqrt {2{x^{\,2}} + 2{y^{\,2}}} }}^{{6 + {x^{\,2}} + {y^{\,2}}}}{{\,\,\,15z\,\,dz}}\,dy}}\,dx}}\)
problems.solution: Cylindrical: right half disk \(\theta\in[-\pi/2,\pi/2]\), \(r\in[0,3]\); \(z\in[-\sqrt 2 r,\,6+r^2]\). \[ \int 15z\,dz = \tfrac{15}{2}\big[(6+r^2)^2 - 2r^2\big] = \tfrac{15}{2}(36 + 10r^2 + r^4). \] \[ \pi\cdot\tfrac{15}{2}\int_{0}^{3}(36r + 10r^3 + r^5)\,dr = \pi\cdot\tfrac{15}{2}\cdot 486 = 3645\pi. \]

problems.problem: Use a triple integral in cylindrical coordinates to derive the volume of a cylinder of height \(h\) and radius \(a\).
problems.solution: \[ V = \int_{0}^{2\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{a}\!\!\int_{0}^{h} r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta = 2\pi\cdot\tfrac{a^2}{2}\cdot h = \pi a^2 h. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{4xy\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region bounded by \(z = 2{x^2} + 2{y^2} - 7\) and \(z = 1\).
problems.solution: In cylindrical, \(4xy = 2r^2\sin 2\theta\) and \(\int_{0}^{2\pi}\sin 2\theta\,d\theta = 0\), so the integral is \(0\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{{{\bf{e}}^{ - {x^{\,2}} - {z^{\,2}}}}\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region between the two cylinders \({x^2} + {z^2} = 4\) and \({x^2} + {z^2} = 9\) with \(1 \le y \le 5\) and \(z \le 0\).
problems.solution: Cylindrical with axis \(y\): \(r\in[2,3]\), \(z=r\sin\theta\le 0\) gives \(\theta\in[\pi,2\pi]\) (length \(\pi\)); \(y\in[1,5]\) (length 4). \[ \int_{\pi}^{2\pi}\!\!\int_{2}^{3}\!\!\int_{1}^{5} e^{-r^2}\,r\,dy\,dr\,d\theta = \pi\cdot 4\cdot\tfrac{1}{2}(e^{-4}-e^{-9}) = 2\pi(e^{-4}-e^{-9}). \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{z\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region between the two planes \(x + y + z = 2\) and \(x = 0\) and inside the cylinder \({y^2} + {z^2} = 1\).
problems.solution: \(yz\)-polar with axis \(x\): \(r\in[0,1]\), \(\theta\in[0,2\pi]\); \(x\in[0, 2-r\cos\theta-r\sin\theta]\); \(z=r\sin\theta\). \[ \iiint z\,dV = \int_{0}^{2\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\big[2r^2\sin\theta - r^3\sin\theta(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)\big]\,dr\,d\theta. \] Only \(-\sin^2\theta\) survives, giving \(-\pi\cdot\tfrac{1}{4} = -\tfrac{\pi}{4}\).

problems.problem: Use a triple integral to determine the volume of the region below \(z = 6 - x\), above \(z = - \sqrt {4{x^2} + 4{y^2}} \) inside the cylinder \({x^2} + {y^2} = 3\) with \(x \le 0\).
problems.solution: Cylindrical with \(x\le 0\): \(\theta\in[\pi/2,3\pi/2]\), \(r\in[0,\sqrt 3]\); \(z\in[-2r,\,6-r\cos\theta]\). \[ V = \int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}\!\!\int_{0}^{\sqrt 3}(6 + 2r - r\cos\theta)\,r\,dr\,d\theta = \int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}(9+2\sqrt 3 - \sqrt 3\cos\theta)\,d\theta. \] This is \(\pi(9+2\sqrt 3) - \sqrt 3\cdot(-2) = \pi(9+2\sqrt 3) + 2\sqrt 3\).

problems.problem: Evaluate the following integral by first converting to an integral in cylindrical coordinates. \(\int_{0}^{{\sqrt 5 }}{{\int_{{ - \sqrt {5 - {x^{\,2}}} }}^{0}{{\int_{{{x^{\,2}} + {y^{\,2}} - 11}}^{{9 - 3{x^{\,2}} - 3{y^{\,2}}}}{{\,\,\,2x - 3y\,\,\,dz}}\,dy}}\,dx}}\)
problems.solution: Cylindrical: 4th-quadrant quarter disk \(\theta\in[-\pi/2,0]\), \(r\in[0,\sqrt 5]\); \(z\in[r^2-11,\,9-3r^2]\) (width \(20-4r^2\)). \[ \int_{-\pi/2}^{0}(2\cos\theta-3\sin\theta)\,d\theta\cdot\int_{0}^{\sqrt 5}(20r^2-4r^4)\,dr = 5\cdot\tfrac{40\sqrt 5}{3} = \tfrac{200\sqrt 5}{3}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{4{y^2}\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the sphere \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 9\).
problems.solution: Spherical with full sphere \(\rho\in[0,3]\), \(\phi\in[0,\pi]\), \(\theta\in[0,2\pi]\); \(y^2 = \rho^2\sin^2\phi\sin^2\theta\). \[ \iiint 4y^2\,dV = \int_{0}^{2\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\cdot\int_{0}^{\pi}\sin^3\phi\,d\phi\cdot\int_{0}^{3} 4\rho^4\,d\rho = \pi\cdot\tfrac{4}{3}\cdot\tfrac{972}{5} = \tfrac{1296\pi}{5}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{3x - 2y\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region between the spheres \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 1\) and \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 4\) with \(z \le 0\).
problems.solution: In spherical, \(3x-2y\) has \(\theta\)-dependence \(3\cos\theta - 2\sin\theta\), and \(\int_{0}^{2\pi}\) of either is \(0\). The integral is \(0\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{2yz\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region inside both \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 16\) and \(z = \sqrt {3{x^2} + 3{y^2}} \) that is in the 1st octant.
problems.solution: Cone \(z=\sqrt 3\,r\) corresponds to \(\phi=\pi/6\); 1st octant adds \(\theta\in[0,\pi/2]\). With \(2yz = 2\rho^2\sin\phi\cos\phi\sin\theta\): \[ \int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sin\theta\,d\theta\cdot\int_{0}^{\pi/6}\sin^2\phi\cos\phi\,d\phi\cdot\int_{0}^{4} 2\rho^4\,d\rho = 1\cdot\tfrac{1}{24}\cdot\tfrac{2048}{5} = \tfrac{256}{15}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{{z^2}\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region between the spheres \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 4\) and \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 25\) and inside \(\displaystyle z = - \sqrt {\frac{1}{3}{x^2} + \frac{1}{3}{y^2}} \).
problems.solution: The cone \(z=-r/\sqrt 3\) is \(\cos\phi=-\tfrac{1}{2}\), i.e. \(\phi=2\pi/3\); \"inside\" the downward cone gives \(\phi\in[2\pi/3,\pi]\).
