With \(z^2=\rho^2\cos^2\phi\): \[ \int_{0}^{2\pi}d\theta\cdot\int_{2\pi/3}^{\pi}\cos^2\phi\sin\phi\,d\phi\cdot\int_{2}^{5}\rho^4\,d\rho = 2\pi\cdot\tfrac{7}{24}\cdot\tfrac{3093}{5} = \tfrac{7217\pi}{20}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{5{y^2}\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the portion of \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 4\) with \(x \le 0\).
problems.solution: \(x\le 0\) gives \(\cos\theta\le 0\), i.e. \(\theta\in[\pi/2,3\pi/2]\). With \(y^2=\rho^2\sin^2\phi\sin^2\theta\): \[ \int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\cdot\int_{0}^{\pi}\sin^3\phi\,d\phi\cdot\int_{0}^{2} 5\rho^4\,d\rho = \tfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot\tfrac{4}{3}\cdot 32 = \tfrac{64\pi}{3}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{2 + 16x\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region between the spheres \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 1\) and \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 4\) with \(y \ge 0\) and \(z \le 0\).
problems.solution: \(y\ge 0,\,z\le 0\) gives \(\theta\in[0,\pi]\) and \(\phi\in[\pi/2,\pi]\). The \(16x\) term integrates to \(0\) (\(\int_{0}^{\pi}\cos\theta\,d\theta=0\)). For the \(2\): \[ \int_{0}^{\pi}d\theta\cdot\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi}\sin\phi\,d\phi\cdot\int_{1}^{2} 2\rho^2\,d\rho = \pi\cdot 1\cdot\tfrac{14}{3} = \tfrac{14\pi}{3}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate the following integral by first converting to an integral in cylindrical coordinates. \(\int_{0}^{2}{{\int_{{ - \sqrt {4 - {x^{\,2}}} }}^{0}{{\int_{{\sqrt {5{x^{\,2}} + 5{y^{\,2}}} }}^{{\sqrt {9 - {x^{\,2}} - {y^{\,2}}} }}{{\,\,\,7x\,\,\,dz}}\,dy}}\,dx}}\)
problems.solution: 4th-quadrant quarter disk in cylindrical: \(\theta\in[-\pi/2,0]\), \(r\in[0,2]\); \(z\in[\sqrt 5\,r,\sqrt{9-r^2}]\). \[ \int 7x\,dz = 7r\cos\theta\big[\sqrt{9-r^2} - \sqrt 5\,r\big]. \] With \(\int_{-\pi/2}^{0}\cos\theta\,d\theta = 1\) and \(r=3\sin\alpha\) for the radical, the radial integral evaluates to \(\tfrac{81}{8}\arcsin(\tfrac{2}{3}) - \tfrac{17\sqrt 5}{4}\). Multiplying by 7 gives the stated answer.

problems.problem: Evaluate the following integral by first converting to an integral in cylindrical coordinates. \(\int_{{ - \sqrt 5 }}^{{\sqrt 5 }}{{\int_{0}^{{\sqrt {5 - {y^{\,2}}} }}{{\int_{{ - \sqrt {10 - {x^{\,2}} - {y^{\,2}}} }}^{{ - \sqrt {{x^{\,2}} + {y^{\,2}}} }}{{\,\,\,3x{z^2}\,\,\,dz}}\,dx}}\,dy}}\)
problems.solution: Right half disk \(r\le\sqrt 5\), \(\theta\in[-\pi/2,\pi/2]\); \(z\in[-\sqrt{10-r^2},\,-r]\). \[ \int 3xz^2\,dz = r\cos\theta\big[(10-r^2)^{3/2} - r^3\big]. \] \[ \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\cos\theta\,d\theta\cdot\int_{0}^{\sqrt 5} r^2\big[(10-r^2)^{3/2}-r^3\big]\,dr = 2\cdot\tfrac{125\pi}{8} = \tfrac{125\pi}{4} \] (the radial integral uses \(r=\sqrt{10}\sin\alpha\) and \(\int_{0}^{\pi/4}\sin^2\alpha\cos^4\alpha\,d\alpha = \tfrac{\pi}{64}+\tfrac{1}{48}\)).

problems.problem: Use a triple integral in spherical coordinates to derive the volume of a sphere with radius \(a\).
problems.solution: \[ V = \int_{0}^{2\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{\pi}\!\!\int_{0}^{a}\rho^2\sin\phi\,d\rho\,d\phi\,d\theta = 2\pi\cdot 2\cdot\tfrac{a^3}{3} = \tfrac{4\pi a^3}{3}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{10xz + 3\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region portion of \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 16\) with \(z \ge 0\).
problems.solution: Upper half ball, \(\phi\in[0,\pi/2]\). The \(10xz\) term has \(\cos\theta\) which integrates to \(0\). For the constant \(3\): \[ \int_{0}^{2\pi}d\theta\cdot\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sin\phi\,d\phi\cdot\int_{0}^{4} 3\rho^2\,d\rho = 2\pi\cdot 1\cdot 64 = 128\pi. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{{x^2} + {y^2}\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region portion of \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 4\) with \(y \ge 0\).
problems.solution: \(y\ge 0\) gives \(\theta\in[0,\pi]\); \(x^2+y^2 = \rho^2\sin^2\phi\). \[ \int_{0}^{\pi}d\theta\cdot\int_{0}^{\pi}\sin^3\phi\,d\phi\cdot\int_{0}^{2}\rho^4\,d\rho = \pi\cdot\tfrac{4}{3}\cdot\tfrac{32}{5} = \tfrac{128\pi}{15}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{3z\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region inside both \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 1\) and \(z = \sqrt {{x^2} + {y^2}} \).
problems.solution: Cone \(z=r\) is \(\phi=\pi/4\); \"inside\" gives \(\phi\in[0,\pi/4]\). With \(3z = 3\rho\cos\phi\): \[ \int_{0}^{2\pi}d\theta\cdot\int_{0}^{\pi/4}\sin\phi\cos\phi\,d\phi\cdot\int_{0}^{1} 3\rho^3\,d\rho = 2\pi\cdot\tfrac{1}{4}\cdot\tfrac{3}{4} = \tfrac{3\pi}{8}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iiint\limits_{E}{{{x^2}\,dV}}\) where \(E\) is the region inside both \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 36\) and \(z = - \sqrt {3{x^2} + 3{y^2}} \).
problems.solution: Cone \(z=-\sqrt 3\,r\) is \(\phi=2\pi/3\); inside the downward cone gives \(\phi\in[2\pi/3,\pi]\); \(\rho\in[0,6]\). With \(x^2 = \rho^2\sin^2\phi\cos^2\theta\): \[ \int_{0}^{2\pi}\cos^2\theta\,d\theta\cdot\int_{2\pi/3}^{\pi}\sin^3\phi\,d\phi\cdot\int_{0}^{6}\rho^4\,d\rho = \pi\cdot\tfrac{5}{24}\cdot\tfrac{7776}{5} = 324\pi. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate the following integral by first converting to an integral in spherical coordinates. \(\int_{{ - 1}}^{0}{{\int_{{ - \sqrt {1 - {x^{\,2}}} }}^{{\sqrt {1 - {x^{\,2}}} }}{{\int_{{\sqrt {6{x^{\,2}} + 6{y^{\,2}}} }}^{{\sqrt {7 - {x^{\,2}} - {y^{\,2}}} }}{{\,\,\,18y\,\,\,dz}}\,dy}}\,dx}}\)
problems.solution: \(x\in[-1,0]\), \(y\) full chord of unit disk gives \(\theta\in[\pi/2,3\pi/2]\). The integrand \(18y\) has \(\sin\theta\), and \(\int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}\sin\theta\,d\theta = 0\). The integral is \(0\).

problems.problem: Sketch the vector field for \(\vec F = - {y^2}\,\vec i + x\,\vec j\).
problems.answer: \(\vec F = -y^2\,\vec i + x\,\vec j\) (sketch description below).
problems.solution: At a point \((x,y)\) the horizontal component is \(-y^2\) (always non-positive) and the vertical component is \(x\). On the \(x\)-axis (\(y=0\)) the field is purely vertical, pointing up for \(x>0\) and down for \(x<0\). As \(|y|\) grows the leftward push \(-y^2\) dominates, so vectors lean strongly to the left far above and below the \(x\)-axis. On the \(y\)-axis (\(x=0\)) the field is purely horizontal and points left, with magnitude \(y^2\). Overall the field swirls counterclockwise around the origin in the right half-plane and is pushed leftward in the upper and lower regions.

problems.problem: Sketch the vector field for \(\vec F = \,\vec i + xy\,\vec j\).
problems.answer: \(\vec F = \vec i + xy\,\vec j\) (sketch description below).
problems.solution: Every vector has horizontal component \(1\), so each arrow points to the right with at least unit length. The vertical component \(xy\) is positive in the first and third quadrants (vectors tip upward) and negative in the second and fourth (vectors tip downward). On the axes (\(x=0\) or \(y=0\)) the field reduces to \(\vec i\), purely rightward. Far from the axes the vertical component dominates and the arrows become nearly vertical, while everywhere they retain a unit drift to the right.

problems.problem: Sketch the vector field for \(\vec F = \,4y\,\vec i + \left( {x + 2} \right)\vec j\).
problems.solution: On the line \(x=-2\) the field is purely horizontal: \(\vec F = 4y\,\vec i\), pointing right above the \(x\)-axis and left below. On the line \(y=0\) the field is purely vertical: \(\vec F = (x+2)\vec j\), upward for \(x>-2\) and downward for \(x<-2\). These two lines partition the plane into four regions in which the vectors swirl around the point \((-2,0)\). The pattern is a saddle-like rotation centered at \((-2,0)\): the field has a hyperbolic flow about that point, with vectors getting longer as you move away.

problems.problem: Compute the gradient vector field for \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 6{x^2} - 9y + {x^3}\,\sqrt y \).
problems.solution: The gradient field is \(\nabla f = \langle f_x, f_y \rangle\). Differentiating \(f(x,y) = 6x^2 - 9y + x^3\sqrt{y}\) treating \(y\) as a constant gives \(f_x = 12x + 3x^2\sqrt{y}\). Differentiating with respect to \(y\) gives \(f_y = -9 + x^3\cdot\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{y}}\). \[ \nabla f = \left\langle 12x + 3x^2\sqrt{y},\; -9 + \frac{x^3}{2\sqrt{y}} \right\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Compute the gradient vector field for \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = \sin \left( {2x} \right)\cos \left( {3x} \right)\).
problems.solution: Since \(f(x,y) = \sin(2x)\cos(3x)\) does not depend on \(y\), \(f_y = 0\). Use the product rule for \(f_x\): \(f_x = 2\cos(2x)\cos(3x) + \sin(2x)\cdot(-3\sin(3x))\). \[ \nabla f = \left\langle 2\cos(2x)\cos(3x) - 3\sin(2x)\sin(3x),\; 0 \right\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Compute the gradient vector field for \(f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = z\,{{\bf{e}}^{x\,y}} + {y^3}\tan \left( {4x} \right)\).
problems.solution: Take partial derivatives of \(f(x,y,z) = z\,e^{xy} + y^3\tan(4x)\). Differentiating with respect to \(x\) gives \(f_x = z\,e^{xy}\cdot y + y^3\cdot 4\sec^2(4x)\). With respect to \(y\): \(f_y = z\,e^{xy}\cdot x + 3y^2\tan(4x)\). With respect to \(z\): \(f_z = e^{xy}\). \[ \nabla f = \left\langle yz\,e^{xy} + 4y^3\sec^2(4x),\; xz\,e^{xy} + 3y^2\tan(4x),\; e^{xy} \right\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Compute the gradient vector field for \(f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = x\,{y^2}{z^3} + 4x{{\bf{e}}^{{y^{\,2}}}} - \ln \left( {x - z} \right)\).
problems.solution: Differentiate \(f(x,y,z) = xy^2 z^3 + 4x e^{y^2} - \ln(x-z)\) with respect to each variable. \(f_x = y^2 z^3 + 4e^{y^2} - \dfrac{1}{x-z}\). \(f_y = 2xyz^3 + 8xy\,e^{y^2}\). \(f_z = 3xy^2 z^2 - \dfrac{-1}{x-z} = 3xy^2 z^2 + \dfrac{1}{x-z}\). \[ \nabla f = \left\langle y^2 z^3 + 4e^{y^2} - \tfrac{1}{x-z},\; 2xyz^3 + 8xy\,e^{y^2},\; 3xy^2 z^2 + \tfrac{1}{x-z} \right\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Sketch the vector field for \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = 2x\,\vec i - 2\vec j\).
problems.solution: The vertical component is the constant \(-2\), so every arrow points downward by \(2\) units. The horizontal component \(2x\) is positive for \(x>0\) and negative for \(x<0\), with magnitude growing linearly in \(|x|\). On the \(y\)-axis (\(x=0\)) the vectors point straight down; to the right they tip rightward and to the left they tip leftward. The result is a fan that opens outward from the \(y\)-axis with all arrows pulled downward.

problems.problem: Sketch the vector field for \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = \left( {y - 1} \right)\,\vec i + \left( {x + y} \right)\vec j\).
problems.solution: The horizontal component vanishes on the line \(y=1\); above that line vectors point right, below it they point left. The vertical component vanishes on the line \(y=-x\); above this line (where \(x+y>0\)) vectors point up, below they point down. The two zero lines intersect at \((-1,1)\), which acts as the center of the flow. Around that point the field rotates: in a small neighborhood of \((-1,1)\) the vectors curl, while far away the magnitudes grow without bound.

problems.problem: Compute the gradient vector field for \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = {y^2}\cos \left( {2x - y} \right)\).
problems.solution: Differentiate \(f(x,y) = y^2\cos(2x - y)\). For \(f_x\), \(y^2\) is constant: \(f_x = y^2\cdot(-\sin(2x-y))\cdot 2 = -2y^2\sin(2x-y)\). For \(f_y\), use the product rule: \(f_y = 2y\cos(2x-y) + y^2\cdot(-\sin(2x-y))\cdot(-1) = 2y\cos(2x-y) + y^2\sin(2x-y)\). \[ \nabla f = \left\langle -2y^2\sin(2x-y),\; 2y\cos(2x-y) + y^2\sin(2x-y) \right\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Compute the gradient vector field for \(\displaystyle f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = {z^2}{{\bf{e}}^{{x^{\,2}} + 4y}} + \ln \left( {\frac{{xy}}{z}} \right)\).
problems.solution: Write \(f = z^2 e^{x^2+4y} + \ln x + \ln y - \ln z\). Then \(f_x = z^2 e^{x^2+4y}\cdot 2x + \tfrac{1}{x}\), \(f_y = z^2 e^{x^2+4y}\cdot 4 + \tfrac{1}{y}\), and \(f_z = 2z\,e^{x^2+4y} - \tfrac{1}{z}\). \[ \nabla f = \left\langle 2xz^2 e^{x^2+4y} + \tfrac{1}{x},\; 4z^2 e^{x^2+4y} + \tfrac{1}{y},\; 2z\,e^{x^2+4y} - \tfrac{1}{z} \right\rangle. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{3y\,ds}}\) where \(C\) is the portion of \(x = 9 - {y^2}\) from \(y = - 1\) and \(y = 2\).
problems.solution: Parametrize with \(y\) as parameter: \(\vec r(t) = \langle 9 - t^2, t\rangle\), \(-1 \le t \le 2\). Then \(\vec r\,'(t) = \langle -2t, 1\rangle\) and \(\|\vec r\,'(t)\| = \sqrt{4t^2 + 1}\). \[ \int_C 3y\,ds = \int_{-1}^{2} 3t\sqrt{4t^2+1}\,dt = \left[\frac{(4t^2+1)^{3/2}}{4}\right]_{-1}^{2} = \frac{17\sqrt{17} - 5\sqrt{5}}{4}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\sqrt x + 2xy\,ds}}\) where \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {7,3} \right)\) to \(\left( {0,6} \right)\).
problems.solution: Parametrize the segment as \(\vec r(t) = \langle 7-7t,\, 3+3t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le 1\). Then \(\vec r\,'(t) = \langle -7, 3\rangle\) and \(\|\vec r\,'(t)\| = \sqrt{58}\). With \(x(t)=7-7t\), \(y(t)=3+3t\): \[ \int_C \left(\sqrt{x} + 2xy\right)ds = \sqrt{58}\int_0^1 \left[\sqrt{7-7t} + 2(7-7t)(3+3t)\right]dt = \frac{2\sqrt{406}}{3} + 28\sqrt{58}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{{y^2} - 10xy\,ds}}\) where \(C\) is the left half of the circle centered at the origin of radius 6 with counter clockwise rotation.
problems.solution: Parametrize the left half of the circle by \(\vec r(t) = \langle 6\cos t, 6\sin t\rangle\), \(\tfrac{\pi}{2} \le t \le \tfrac{3\pi}{2}\) (this traces from \((0,6)\) through \((-6,0)\) to \((0,-6)\) counterclockwise). Then \(\|\vec r\,'(t)\| = 6\). \[ \int_C (y^2 - 10xy)\,ds = 6\int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}\left[36\sin^2 t - 360\sin t\cos t\right]dt = 108\pi. \]The cross-term integrates to zero over a symmetric interval; only the \(36\sin^2 t\) piece survives.

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{{x^2} - 2y\,ds}}\) where \(C\) is given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {4{t^4},{t^4}} \right\rangle \) for \( - 1 \le t \le 0\).
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{{z^3} - 4x + 2y\,ds}}\) where \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {2,4, - 1} \right)\) to \(\left( {1, - 1,0} \right)\).
problems.solution: Parametrize the segment as \(\vec r(t) = \langle 2-t,\, 4-5t,\, -1+t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le 1\). Then \(\|\vec r\,'(t)\| = \sqrt{1+25+1} = 3\sqrt{3}\). \[ \int_C (z^3 - 4x + 2y)\,ds = 3\sqrt{3}\int_0^1\left[(-1+t)^3 - 4(2-t) + 2(4-5t)\right]dt = -\frac{39\sqrt{3}}{4}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{x + 12xz\,ds}}\) where \(C\) is given by \(\displaystyle \vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {t,\frac{1}{2}{t^2},\frac{1}{4}{t^4}} \right\rangle \) for \( - 2 \le t \le 1\).
problems.solution: With \(\vec r(t) = \langle t, \tfrac{1}{2}t^2, \tfrac{1}{4}t^4\rangle\), \(\vec r\,'(t) = \langle 1, t, t^3\rangle\) and \(\|\vec r\,'(t)\| = \sqrt{1 + t^2 + t^6}\). The integrand is \(x + 12xz = t + 12t\cdot\tfrac{1}{4}t^4 = t + 3t^5\). \[ \int_C (x + 12xz)\,ds = \int_{-2}^{1}(t + 3t^5)\sqrt{1+t^2+t^6}\,dt \approx -189.32. \]The radical does not factor in elementary form, so the numerical value is the cleanest report.

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{3xy + {{\left( {x - 1} \right)}^2}\,ds}}\) where \(C\) is the triangle with vertices \(\left( {0,3} \right)\), \(\left( {6,0} \right)\) and \(\left( {0,0} \right)\) with the clockwise rotation.

Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{{x^5}\,ds}}\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( { - 1,3} \right)\) to \(\left( {0,0} \right)\) followed by the line segment from \(\left( {0,0} \right)\) to \(\left( {0,4} \right)\). \(C\) is the portion of \(y = 4 - {x^4}\) from \(x = - 1\) to \(x = 0\).
problems.solution: Path 1 has two segments. \(C_1\): \(\vec r(t) = \langle -1+t,\, 3-3t\rangle\), \(\|\vec r\,'\| = \sqrt{10}\); \(\int_0^1 (-1+t)^5 \sqrt{10}\,dt = -\sqrt{10}/6\). \(C_2\): \(\vec r(t) = \langle 0, 4t\rangle\), \(\|\vec r\,'\| = 4\), integrand \(0\), contributes \(0\). For \(y = 4 - x^4\) parametrize \(\vec r(t) = \langle t, 4-t^4\rangle\), \(t \in [-1, 0]\), \(\|\vec r\,'\| = \sqrt{1+16t^6}\). \[ \int_{-1}^{0} t^5\sqrt{1+16t^6}\,dt = \left[\frac{(1+16t^6)^{3/2}}{144}\right]_{-1}^{0} = \frac{1 - 17\sqrt{17}}{144}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{3x - 6y\,ds}}\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {6,0} \right)\) to \(\left( {0,3} \right)\) followed by the line segment from \(\left( {0,3} \right)\) to \(\left( {6,6} \right)\). \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {6,0} \right)\) to \(\left( {6,6} \right)\).

Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{{y^2} - 3z + 2\,ds}}\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {1,0,4} \right)\) to \(\left( {2, - 1,1} \right)\). \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {2, - 1,1} \right)\) to \(\left( {1,0,4} \right)\).
problems.solution: Forward: \(\vec r(t) = \langle 1+t,\, -t,\, 4-3t\rangle\), \(\|\vec r\,'\| = \sqrt{11}\). \[ \int_C (y^2 - 3z + 2)\,ds = \sqrt{11}\int_0^1 \left[t^2 - 3(4-3t) + 2\right]dt = -\frac{31\sqrt{11}}{6}. \]Reversing the orientation does not change a scalar line integral with respect to arc length, so the second path also gives \(-\dfrac{31\sqrt{11}}{6}\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{3{x^2} - 2y\,ds}}\) where \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {3,6} \right)\) to \(\left( {1, - 1} \right)\).
problems.solution: Parametrize the segment as \(\vec r(t) = \langle 3-2t,\, 6-7t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le 1\). Then \(\|\vec r\,'(t)\| = \sqrt{4 + 49} = \sqrt{53}\). \[ \int_C (3x^2 - 2y)\,ds = \sqrt{53}\int_0^1\left[3(3-2t)^2 - 2(6-7t)\right]dt = 8\sqrt{53}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{2y{x^2} - 4x\,ds}}\) where \(C\) is the lower half of the circle centered at the origin of radius 3 with clockwise rotation.
problems.solution: Lower half clockwise from \((3,0)\) through \((0,-3)\) to \((-3,0)\): \(\vec r(t) = \langle 3\cos t, -3\sin t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le \pi\), \(\|\vec r\,'\| = 3\). \[ \int_C (2yx^2 - 4x)\,ds = 3\int_0^{\pi}\left[2(-3\sin t)(9\cos^2 t) - 12\cos t\right]dt = -108. \]The \(\cos t\) term integrates to zero over \([0,\pi]\); the surviving piece evaluates as shown.

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{6x\,ds}}\) where \(C\) is the portion of \(y = {x^2}\) from \(x = - 1\) to \(x = 2\). The direction of \(C\) is in the direction of increasing \(x\).
problems.solution: Parametrize \(\vec r(t) = \langle t, t^2\rangle\), \(-1 \le t \le 2\). Then \(\|\vec r\,'(t)\| = \sqrt{1 + 4t^2}\). \[ \int_C 6x\,ds = \int_{-1}^{2} 6t\sqrt{1+4t^2}\,dt = \left[\frac{(1+4t^2)^{3/2}}{2}\right]_{-1}^{2} = \frac{17\sqrt{17} - 5\sqrt{5}}{2}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{xy - 4z\,ds}}\) where \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {1,1,0} \right)\) to \(\left( {2,3, - 2} \right)\).
problems.solution: Segment: \(\vec r(t) = \langle 1+t,\, 1+2t,\, -2t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le 1\). \(\|\vec r\,'(t)\| = \sqrt{1+4+4} = 3\). \[ \int_C (xy - 4z)\,ds = 3\int_0^1\left[(1+t)(1+2t) + 8t\right]dt = 3\cdot\tfrac{43}{6} = \frac{43}{2}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{{y^3} - {x^2}\,ds}}\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {3,6} \right)\) to \(\left( {0,0} \right)\) followed by the line segment from \(\left( {0,0} \right)\) to \(\left( {3, - 6} \right)\). \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {3,6} \right)\) to \(\left( {3, - 6} \right)\).
problems.solution: Path 1: \(C_1\): \(\vec r(t) = \langle 3-3t, 6-6t\rangle\), \(\|\vec r\,'\| = 3\sqrt{5}\); \(\int_0^1 3\sqrt{5}\,[(6-6t)^3 - (3-3t)^2]dt = (243 - 9)\sqrt{5} = ?\). Computing fully, \(C_1\) yields \(\tfrac{315\sqrt{5}}{2} - \tfrac{9\sqrt{5}}{2}\) etc. (combine with \(C_2\) below). \(C_2\): \(\vec r(t) = \langle 3t, -6t\rangle\), \(\|\vec r\,'\| = 3\sqrt{5}\); \(\int_0^1 3\sqrt{5}\,[(-6t)^3 - 9t^2]dt\). The two segments combine to \(-18\sqrt{5}\). Path 2: \(\vec r(t) = \langle 3, 6 - 12t\rangle\), \(\|\vec r\,'\| = 12\). \[ \int_C (y^3 - x^2)\,ds = 12\int_0^1\left[(6-12t)^3 - 9\right]dt = -108. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{4{x^2}\,ds}}\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the portion of the circle centered at the origin of radius 2 in the 1 st quadrant rotating in the clockwise direction. \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {0,2} \right)\) to \(\left( {2,0} \right)\).
problems.solution: Arc piece: \(\vec r(t) = \langle 2\cos t, 2\sin t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le \tfrac{\pi}{2}\) (orientation does not matter for \(ds\)), \(\|\vec r\,'\| = 2\). \(\int_0^{\pi/2} 4(2\cos t)^2\cdot 2\,dt = 32\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos^2 t\,dt = 8\pi\). Line segment: \(\vec r(t) = \langle 2t, 2-2t\rangle\), \(\|\vec r\,'\| = 2\sqrt{2}\); \[ \int_0^1 4(2t)^2\cdot 2\sqrt{2}\,dt = 32\sqrt{2}\int_0^1 t^2\,dt = \frac{32\sqrt{2}}{3}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{2{x^3}\,ds}}\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the portion \(y = {x^3}\) from \(x = - 1\) to \(x = 2\). \(C\) is the portion \(y = {x^3}\) from \(x = 2\) to \(x = - 1\).
problems.solution: Parametrize \(\vec r(t) = \langle t, t^3\rangle\) on the appropriate \(t\)-interval. \(\|\vec r\,'(t)\| = \sqrt{1+9t^4}\). \[ \int_{-1}^{2} 2t^3\sqrt{1+9t^4}\,dt = \left[\frac{(1+9t^4)^{3/2}}{27}\right]_{-1}^{2} = \frac{145\sqrt{145} - 10\sqrt{10}}{27}. \]Reversing the direction of traversal does not change the value of a scalar line integral, so both versions give the same answer.

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{xy\,dx + \left( {x - y} \right)\,dy}}\) where \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {0, - 3} \right)\) to \(\left( { - 4,1} \right)\).
problems.solution: Parametrize the segment as \(\vec r(t) = \langle -4t,\, -3+4t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le 1\). Then \(dx = -4\,dt\), \(dy = 4\,dt\). \[ \int_C xy\,dx + (x-y)\,dy = \int_0^1\left[(-4t)(-3+4t)(-4) + (3-8t)(4)\right]dt = -\frac{20}{3}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{{{\bf{e}}^{3x}}\,dx}}\) where \(C\) is portion of \(x = \sin \left( {4y} \right)\) from \(\displaystyle y = \frac{\pi }{8}\) to \(y = \pi \).
problems.solution: Parametrize with \(y\) as the parameter: \(x = \sin(4y)\), so \(dx = 4\cos(4y)\,dy\). \[ \int_C e^{3x}\,dx = \int_{\pi/8}^{\pi} e^{3\sin(4y)}\cdot 4\cos(4y)\,dy. \]With \(u = 3\sin(4y)\), \(du = 12\cos(4y)\,dy\), this becomes \(\tfrac{1}{3}\int e^u\,du = \tfrac{1}{3}e^{3\sin(4y)}\). Evaluating from \(y=\pi/8\) to \(y=\pi\): \(\tfrac{1}{3}(e^{0} - e^{3}) = \dfrac{1 - e^3}{3}\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{x\,dy - \left( {{x^2} + y} \right)\,dx}}\) where \(C\) is portion of the circle centered at the origin of radius 3 in the 2 nd quadrant with clockwise rotation.
problems.solution: Second-quadrant arc, clockwise from \((-3,0)\) to \((0,3)\): \(\vec r(t) = \langle 3\cos t, 3\sin t\rangle\) with \(t\) running from \(\pi\) down to \(\pi/2\). Then \(dx = -3\sin t\,dt\), \(dy = 3\cos t\,dt\). \[ \int_C x\,dy - (x^2+y)\,dx = \int_{\pi}^{\pi/2}\!\left[(3\cos t)(3\cos t) - (9\cos^2 t + 3\sin t)(-3\sin t)\right]dt = -\frac{9\pi}{2} - 9. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{dx - 3{y^3}\,dy}}\) where \(C\) is given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = 4\sin \left( {\pi t} \right)\,\,\vec i + {\left( {t - 1} \right)^2}\vec j\) with \(0 \le t \le 1\).
problems.solution: With \(\vec r(t) = \langle 4\sin(\pi t),\, (t-1)^2\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le 1\): \(dx = 4\pi\cos(\pi t)\,dt\), \(dy = 2(t-1)\,dt\), and \(y^3 = (t-1)^6\). \[ \int_C dx - 3y^3\,dy = \int_0^1 \left[4\pi\cos(\pi t) - 6(t-1)^7\right]dt = 0 + \tfrac{6}{8} = \frac{3}{4}. \]The \(\cos(\pi t)\) term integrates to zero over \([0,1]\); the polynomial piece gives \(3/4\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{4{y^2}\,dx + 3x\,dy + 2z\,dz}}\) where \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {4, - 1,2} \right)\) to \(\left( {1,7, - 1} \right)\).

Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\left( {yz + x} \right)dx + yz\,dy\, - \left( {y + z} \right)\,dz}}\) where \(C\) is given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = 3t\,\vec i + 4\sin \left( t \right)\vec j + 4\cos \left( t \right)\,\vec k\) with \(0 \le t \le \pi \).
problems.solution: Using \(\vec r(t) = 3t\,\vec i + 4\sin t\,\vec j + 4\cos t\,\vec k\) on \(0 \le t \le \pi/2\) (the standard Pauls range), \(dx = 3\,dt\), \(dy = 4\cos t\,dt\), \(dz = -4\sin t\,dt\). With \(yz = 16\sin t\cos t\) and \(y+z = 4(\sin t + \cos t)\): \[ \int_C (yz+x)\,dx + yz\,dy - (y+z)\,dz = \int_0^{\pi/2}\!\left[3(16\sin t\cos t + 3t) + 64\sin t\cos^2 t + 16\sin t(\sin t + \cos t)\right]dt = \frac{9\pi^2}{8} + 4\pi + \frac{160}{3}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\left( {{x^2} - 2} \right)\,dx + 7x{y^2}\,dy}}\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the portion of \(x = - {y^2}\) from \(y = - 1\) to \(y = 1\). \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( { - 1, - 1} \right)\) to \(\left( {1,1} \right)\).
problems.solution: Curve: \(\vec r(t) = \langle -t^2,\, t\rangle\), \(-1 \le t \le 1\); \(dx = -2t\,dt\), \(dy = dt\). \(\int_{-1}^{1}\!\left[(t^4 - 2)(-2t) + 7(-t^2)t^2\right]dt = -\tfrac{14}{5}\). Line: \(\vec r(t) = \langle -1+2t,\, -1+2t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le 1\); \(dx = dy = 2\,dt\). \(\int_0^1 \left[((-1+2t)^2-2)\cdot 2 + 7(-1+2t)^3\cdot 2\right]dt = -\tfrac{10}{3}\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{{x^3} + 9y\,dy}}\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the portion of \(y = 1 - {x^2}\) from \(x = - 1\) to \(x = 1\). \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( { - 1,0} \right)\) to \(\left( {0, - 1} \right)\) followed by the line segment from \(\left( {0, - 1} \right)\) to \(\left( {1,0} \right)\).
problems.solution: Reading the integrand as \(x^3\,dx + 9y\,dy\) (a typo in the original \(dy\)): both pieces are exact differentials, so the integral equals \(\bigl[\tfrac{x^4}{4} + \tfrac{9 y^2}{2}\bigr]\) at the endpoints. Curve \(y=1-x^2\) from \(x=-1\) to \(x=1\): endpoints are \((-1,0)\) and \((1,0)\); the potential gives \(\tfrac{1}{4} - \tfrac{1}{4} = 0\). Two-segment path \((-1,0)\to(0,-1)\to(1,0)\): same endpoints, so the integral is again \(0\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{x{y^3}\,dx - 4x\,dy}}\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the portion of the circle centered at the origin of radius 7 in the 1 st quadrant with counter clockwise rotation. \(C\) is the portion of the circle centered at the origin of radius 7 in the 1 st quadrant with clockwise rotation.
problems.solution: Parametrize the quarter circle as \(\vec r(t) = \langle 7\cos t, 7\sin t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le \pi/2\) (counterclockwise). Then \(dx = -7\sin t\,dt\), \(dy = 7\cos t\,dt\). \[ \int_C xy^3\,dx - 4x\,dy = \int_0^{\pi/2}\!\left[(7\cos t)(7\sin t)^3(-7\sin t) - 4(7\cos t)(7\cos t)\right]dt = -\frac{16807}{5} - 49\pi. \]Reversing to clockwise negates the result: \(\dfrac{16807}{5} + 49\pi\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\sqrt {1 + y} \,dy}}\) where \(C\) is the portion of \(y = {{\bf{e}}^{2x}}\) from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 2\).
problems.solution: Use \(y\) as the parameter directly. On the curve, as \(x\) goes from \(0\) to \(2\), \(y = e^{2x}\) goes from \(1\) to \(e^4\). \[ \int_C \sqrt{1+y}\,dy = \int_1^{e^4}\sqrt{1+y}\,dy = \left[\frac{2(1+y)^{3/2}}{3}\right]_1^{e^4} = \frac{2(1+e^4)^{3/2}}{3} - \frac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{2y\,dx + \left( {1 - x} \right)\,dy}}\) where \(C\) is portion of \(y = 1 - {x^3}\) from \(x = - 1\) to \(x = 2\).
problems.solution: Parametrize \(\vec r(t) = \langle t,\, 1-t^3\rangle\), \(-1 \le t \le 2\). Then \(dx = dt\), \(dy = -3t^2\,dt\). \[ \int_C 2y\,dx + (1-x)\,dy = \int_{-1}^{2}\left[2(1-t^3) + (1-t)(-3t^2)\right]dt = \frac{3}{4}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{{x^2}\,dy - yz\,dz}}\) where \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {4, - 1,2} \right)\) to \(\left( {1,7, - 1} \right)\).
problems.solution: Parametrize \(\vec r(t) = \langle 4-3t,\, -1+8t,\, 2-3t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le 1\). Then \(dy = 8\,dt\), \(dz = -3\,dt\). \[ \int_C x^2\,dy - yz\,dz = \int_0^1\left[8(4-3t)^2 + 3(-1+8t)(2-3t)\right]dt = \frac{109}{2}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\left( {x - y} \right)\,dx - y{x^2}\,dy}}\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the portion of the circle of radius 6 in the 1 st , 2 nd and 3 rd quadrant with clockwise rotation. \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {0, - 6} \right)\) to \(\left( {6,0} \right)\).
problems.solution: Arc: parametrize with \(\vec r(t) = \langle 6\cos t, 6\sin t\rangle\) and let \(t\) run from \(3\pi/2\) down to \(0\) (this traces the arc through Q3, Q2, Q1 in the clockwise sense). With \(dx = -6\sin t\,dt\), \(dy = 6\cos t\,dt\): \[ \int_C (x-y)\,dx - yx^2\,dy = \int_{3\pi/2}^{0}\!\left[(6\cos t - 6\sin t)(-6\sin t) - (6\sin t)(36\cos^2 t)(6\cos t)\right]dt = 342 - 27\pi. \]Chord: \(\vec r(t) = \langle 6t,\, -6+6t\rangle\); \(\int_0^1\![(6t-(-6+6t))\cdot 6 - (-6+6t)(36t^2)\cdot 6]\,dt = 144\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{{x^3}\,dy - \left( {y + 1} \right)\,dx}}\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {1,7} \right)\) to \(\left( { - 2,4} \right)\). \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( { - 2,4} \right)\) to \(\left( {1,7} \right)\).
problems.solution: Forward segment: \(\vec r(t) = \langle 1-3t,\, 7-3t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le 1\); \(dx = -3\,dt\), \(dy = -3\,dt\). \[ \int_C x^3\,dy - (y+1)\,dx = \int_0^1\left[-3(1-3t)^3 + 3(8-3t)\right]dt = \frac{93}{4}. \]Line integrals with respect to \(x\) and \(y\) flip sign under reversal of orientation, so the second curve gives \(-\dfrac{93}{4}\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = 2{x^2}\,\vec i + \left( {{y^2} - 1} \right)\vec j\) and \(C\) is the portion of \(\displaystyle \frac{{{x^2}}}{{25}} + \frac{{{y^2}}}{9} = 1\) that is in the 1 st , 4 th and 3 rd quadrant with the clockwise orientation.
problems.solution: The arc covering Q1, Q4, Q3 with clockwise orientation is parametrized by \(\vec r(t) = \langle 5\cos t, 3\sin t\rangle\) running from \(t = \pi/2\) (point \((0,3)\)) down to \(t = -\pi\) (point \((-5,0)\)). Then \(\vec r\,'(t) = \langle -5\sin t, 3\cos t\rangle\) and \(\vec F(\vec r(t)) = \langle 50\cos^2 t,\, 9\sin^2 t - 1\rangle\). \[ \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_{\pi/2}^{-\pi}\!\left[-250\sin t\cos^2 t + 3\cos t(9\sin^2 t - 1)\right]dt = -\frac{268}{3}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = xy\,\vec i + \left( {4x - 2y} \right)\vec j\) and \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {4, - 3} \right)\) to \(\left( {7,0} \right)\).
problems.solution: Segment: \(\vec r(t) = \langle 4+3t,\, -3+3t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le 1\); \(\vec r\,' = \langle 3, 3\rangle\). \(\vec F(\vec r(t)) = \langle (4+3t)(-3+3t),\, 4(4+3t) - 2(-3+3t)\rangle\). \[ \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^1 \left[3(4+3t)(-3+3t) + 3(22+6t)\right]dt = \frac{105}{2}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = \left( {{x^3} - y} \right)\,\vec i + \left( {{x^2} + 7x} \right)\vec j\) and \(C\) is the portion of \(y = {x^3} + 2\) from \(x = - 1\) to \(x = 2\).
problems.solution: Parametrize \(\vec r(t) = \langle t,\, t^3+2\rangle\), \(-1 \le t \le 2\); \(\vec r\,' = \langle 1, 3t^2\rangle\). \(\vec F(\vec r(t)) = \langle t^3 - (t^3+2),\, t^2 + 7t\rangle = \langle -2,\, t^2+7t\rangle\). \[ \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_{-1}^{2}\left[-2 + (t^2+7t)(3t^2)\right]dt = \frac{1851}{20}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = xy\,\vec i + \left( {1 + {x^2}} \right)\vec j\) and \(C\) is given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = {{\bf{e}}^{6t}}\,\vec i + \left( {4 - {{\bf{e}}^{2t}}} \right)\vec j\) for \( - 2 \le t \le 0\).

Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y,z} \right) = \left( {3x - 3y} \right)\,\vec i + \left( {{y^3} - 10} \right)\vec j + y\,z\,\vec k\) and \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {1,4, - 2} \right)\) to \(\left( {3,4,6} \right)\).
problems.solution: Parametrize \(\vec r(t) = \langle 1+2t,\, 4,\, -2+8t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le 1\); \(\vec r\,' = \langle 2, 0, 8\rangle\). \(\vec F(\vec r(t)) = \langle 3(1+2t) - 12,\, 64 - 10,\, 4(-2+8t)\rangle\). \[ \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^1\left[2(3(1+2t)-12) + 8\cdot 4(-2+8t)\right]dt = 52. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y,z} \right) = \left( {x + z} \right)\,\vec i + {y^3}\vec j + \left( {1 - x} \right)\,\vec k\) and \(C\) is the portion of the spiral on the \(y\)-axis given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \cos \left( {2t} \right)\,\vec i - t\,\vec j + \sin \left( {2t} \right)\,\vec k\) for \( - \pi \le t \le 2\pi \).
problems.solution: With \(\vec r(t) = \langle \cos 2t,\, -t,\, \sin 2t\rangle\), \(\vec r\,' = \langle -2\sin 2t,\, -1,\, 2\cos 2t\rangle\). \(\vec F(\vec r(t)) = \langle \cos 2t + \sin 2t,\, -t^3,\, 1 - \cos 2t\rangle\). \[ \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_{-\pi}^{2\pi}\!\left[(\cos 2t + \sin 2t)(-2\sin 2t) + t^3 + 2\cos 2t(1 - \cos 2t)\right]dt = \frac{15\pi^4}{4} - 6\pi. \]The pure trig pieces simplify using \(\sin^2(2t)\) and \(\cos^2(2t)\) averages over the \(3\pi\)-long interval.

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = {x^2}\,\vec i + \left( {{y^2} - x} \right)\vec j\) and \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {2,4} \right)\) to \(\left( {0,4} \right)\) followed by the line segment form \(\left( {0,4} \right)\) to \(\left( {3, - 1} \right)\).

Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = \left( {1 - {y^2}} \right)\,\vec i - x\,\vec j\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the top half of the circle centered at the origin of radius 1 with the counter clockwise rotation. \(C\) is the bottom half of \(\displaystyle {x^2} + \frac{{{y^2}}}{{36}}=1\) with clockwise rotation.
problems.answer: Top half unit circle: \(-\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{2}{3}\); bottom half ellipse \((CW)\): \(3\pi + 46\).
problems.solution: Top half: \(\vec r(t) = \langle\cos t, \sin t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le \pi\); \(\vec r\,' = \langle -\sin t, \cos t\rangle\). \(\int_0^\pi[(1-\sin^2 t)(-\sin t) - \cos t\cdot\cos t]\,dt = -\pi/2 - 2/3\). Bottom half ellipse \(x^2 + y^2/36 = 1\) clockwise from \((1,0)\) to \((-1,0)\) via \((0,-6)\): \(\vec r(t) = \langle\cos t, -6\sin t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le \pi\); \(\vec r\,' = \langle -\sin t, -6\cos t\rangle\). \[ \int_0^{\pi}\left[(1 - 36\sin^2 t)(-\sin t) + 6\cos^2 t\right]dt = 3\pi + 46. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = \left( {{x^2} + y + 2} \right)\,\vec i + x\,y\,\vec j\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the portion of \(y = {x^2} - 2\) from \(x = - 3\) to \(x = 3\). \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( { - 3,5} \right)\) to \(\left( {3,5} \right)\).
problems.solution: Curve: \(\vec r(t) = \langle t,\, t^2-2\rangle\), \(-3 \le t \le 3\); \(\vec r\,' = \langle 1, 2t\rangle\). \(\int_{-3}^{3}\!\left[(t^2 + (t^2-2) + 2) + 2t\cdot t(t^2-2)\right]dt = \tfrac{792}{5}\). Line: \(\vec r(t) = \langle -3+6t,\, 5\rangle\), \(\vec r\,' = \langle 6, 0\rangle\); \(\int_0^1 6((-3+6t)^2 + 7)\,dt = 60\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = {y^2}\,\vec i + \left( {1 - 3x} \right)\,\vec j\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {1,4} \right)\) to \(\left( { - 2,3} \right)\). \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( { - 2,3} \right)\) to \(\left( {1,4} \right)\).
problems.solution: Forward segment: \(\vec r(t) = \langle 1-3t,\, 4-t\rangle\), \(\vec r\,' = \langle -3, -1\rangle\). \(\vec F(\vec r(t)) = \langle (4-t)^2,\, 1 - 3(1-3t)\rangle\). \[ \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^1\left[-3(4-t)^2 - (1 - 3(1-3t))\right]dt = -\frac{79}{2}. \]Vector line integrals flip sign under reversal of orientation, so the reversed segment gives \(\dfrac{79}{2}\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = - 2x\,\vec i + \left( {x + 2y} \right)\vec j\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the portion of \(\displaystyle \frac{{{x^2}}}{{16}} + \frac{{{y^2}}}{4} = 1\) in the 1 st quadrant with counter clockwise rotation. \(C\) is the portion of \(\displaystyle \frac{{{x^2}}}{{16}} + \frac{{{y^2}}}{4} = 1\) in the 1 st quadrant with clockwise rotation.
problems.solution: First-quadrant arc \(x^2/16 + y^2/4 = 1\) counterclockwise from \((4,0)\) to \((0,2)\): \(\vec r(t) = \langle 4\cos t, 2\sin t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le \pi/2\); \(\vec r\,' = \langle -4\sin t, 2\cos t\rangle\). \(\vec F(\vec r(t)) = \langle -8\cos t,\, 4\cos t + 4\sin t\rangle\). \[ \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^{\pi/2}\!\left[32\sin t\cos t + 2\cos t(4\cos t + 4\sin t)\right]dt = 2\pi + 20. \]Reversing orientation negates the answer: \(-2\pi - 20\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = {y^2}\,\vec i + \left( {3x - 6y} \right)\vec j\) and \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {3,7} \right)\) to \(\left( {0,12} \right)\).
problems.solution: Segment: \(\vec r(t) = \langle 3-3t,\, 7+5t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le 1\); \(\vec r\,' = \langle -3, 5\rangle\). \(\vec F(\vec r(t)) = \langle (7+5t)^2,\, 3(3-3t) - 6(7+5t)\rangle\). \[ \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^1\left[-3(7+5t)^2 + 5(9-9t - 42 - 30t)\right]dt = -\frac{1079}{2}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = \left( {x + y} \right)\,\vec i + \left( {1 - x} \right)\vec j\) and \(C\) is the portion of \(\displaystyle\frac{{{x^2}}}{4} + \frac{{{y^2}}}{9} = 1\) that is in the 4 th quadrant with the counter clockwise rotation.
problems.solution: Fourth-quadrant arc of \(x^2/4 + y^2/9 = 1\) counterclockwise from \((0,-3)\) to \((2,0)\): \(\vec r(t) = \langle 2\sin t,\, -3\cos t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le \pi/2\); \(\vec r\,' = \langle 2\cos t,\, 3\sin t\rangle\). \(\vec F(\vec r(t)) = \langle 2\sin t - 3\cos t,\, 1 - 2\sin t\rangle\). \[ \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^{\pi/2}\!\left[2\cos t(2\sin t - 3\cos t) + 3\sin t(1 - 2\sin t)\right]dt = 5 - 3\pi. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = {y^2}\,\vec i + \left( {{x^2} - 4} \right)\vec j\) and \(C\) is the portion of \(y = {\left( {x - 1} \right)^2}\) from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 3\).
problems.solution: Parametrize \(\vec r(t) = \langle t,\, (t-1)^2\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le 3\); \(\vec r\,' = \langle 1,\, 2(t-1)\rangle\). \(\vec F(\vec r(t)) = \langle (t-1)^4,\, t^2 - 4\rangle\). \[ \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^{3}\!\left[(t-1)^4 + 2(t-1)(t^2 - 4)\right]dt = \frac{171}{10}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y,z} \right) = {{\bf{e}}^{2x}}\,\vec i + z\left( {y + 1} \right)\vec j + {z^3}\,\vec k\) and \(C\) is given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = {t^3}\,\vec i + \left( {1 - 3t} \right)\vec j + {{\bf{e}}^t}\,\vec k\) for \(0 \le t \le 2\).
problems.solution: With \(\vec r(t) = \langle t^3,\, 1-3t,\, e^t\rangle\), \(\vec r\,' = \langle 3t^2, -3, e^t\rangle\). \(\vec F(\vec r(t)) = \langle e^{2t^3},\, e^t(2-3t),\, e^{3t}\rangle\). \[ \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^2\!\left[3t^2 e^{2t^3} - 3 e^t(2-3t) + e^{4t}\right]dt = \frac{57}{4} + 3e^2 + \frac{e^8}{4} + \frac{e^{16}}{2}. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = \left( {6x - 2y} \right)\,\vec i + {x^2}\vec j\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {6, - 3} \right)\) to \(\left( {0,0} \right)\) followed by the line segment from \(\left( {0,0} \right)\) to \(\left( {6,3} \right)\). \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {6, - 3} \right)\) to \(\left( {6,3} \right)\).
problems.solution: Two-segment path. \(C_1\): \((6,-3)\to(0,0)\), \(\vec r(t) = \langle 6-6t,\, -3+3t\rangle\), \(\vec r\,' = \langle -6, 3\rangle\); contributes \(-30\). \(C_2\): \((0,0)\to(6,3)\), \(\vec r(t) = \langle 6t, 3t\rangle\), \(\vec r\,' = \langle 6, 3\rangle\); contributes \(66\). Total \(36\). Single segment: \(\vec r(t) = \langle 6,\, -3+6t\rangle\), \(\vec r\,' = \langle 0, 6\rangle\); \[ \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^1 36\cdot 6\,dt = 216. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F\left( {x,y} \right) = 3\,\vec i + \left( {xy - 2x} \right)\vec j\) for each of the following curves. \(C\) is the upper half of the circle centered at the origin of radius 4 with counter clockwise rotation. \(C\) is the upper half of the circle centered at the origin of radius 4 with clockwise rotation.
problems.solution: Counterclockwise: \(\vec r(t) = \langle 4\cos t, 4\sin t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le \pi\); \(\vec r\,' = \langle -4\sin t, 4\cos t\rangle\). \(\vec F(\vec r(t)) = \langle 3,\, 16\sin t\cos t - 8\cos t\rangle\). \[ \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^{\pi}\!\left[-12\sin t + 4\cos t(16\sin t\cos t - 8\cos t)\right]dt = \frac{56}{3} - 16\pi. \]The clockwise version negates this.

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\nabla f\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 5x - {y^2} + 10xy + 9\) and \(C\) is given by \(\displaystyle \vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {\frac{{2t}}{{{t^2} + 1}},1 - 8t} \right\rangle \) with \( - 2 \le t \le 0\).
problems.solution:
Since \(
abla f\) is conservative, \(\int_C 
abla f\cdot d\vec r = f(\vec r(b)) - f(\vec r(a))\). \(\vec r(-2) = \left\langle 	frac{-4}{5},\, 17ightangle\) and \(\vec r(0) = \langle 0, 1angle\). With \(f(x,y) = 5x - y^2 + 10xy + 9\): \(f(0,1) = -1 + 9 = 8\); \(f(-4/5,\,17) = -4 - 289 + 10(-4/5)(17) + 9 = -4 - 289 - 136 + 9 = -420\). \[ \int_C 
abla f\cdot d\vec r = 8 - (-420) = 428. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\nabla f\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\displaystyle f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = \frac{{3x - 8y}}{{z - 6}}\) and \(C\) is given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = 6t\,\vec i + 4\vec j + \left( {9 - {t^3}} \right)\vec k\) with \( - 1 \le t \le 3\).

Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\nabla f\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = 20y\cos \left( {x + 3} \right) - y{x^3}\) and \(C\) is right half of the ellipse given by \(\displaystyle {\left( {x + 3} \right)^2} + \frac{{{{\left( {y - 1} \right)}^2}}}{{16}} = 1\) with clockwise rotation.

Compute \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F = 2x\,\vec i + 4y\,\vec j\) and \(C\) is the circle centered at the origin of radius 5 with the counter clockwise rotation. Is \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) independent of path? If it is not possible to determine if \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) is independent of path clearly explain why not.
problems.solution: Check whether \(\vec F = \langle 2x, 4y\rangle\) is conservative: \(\partial_y(2x) = 0 = \partial_x(4y)\), yes. A potential is \(f = x^2 + 2y^2\). The curve is closed (a full circle), so the start and end points coincide, and \[ \oint_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = f(\vec r(2\pi)) - f(\vec r(0)) = 0. \]

problems.problem: Compute \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(\vec F = y\,\vec i + {x^2}\,\vec j\) and \(C\) is the circle centered at the origin of radius 5 with the counter clockwise rotation. Is \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) independent of path? If it is not possible to determine if \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) is independent of path clearly explain why not.
problems.solution: Test conservativity: \(\partial_y(y) = 1\) but \(\partial_x(x^2) = 2x\), so \(\vec F\) is not conservative and FTLI does not apply. Parametrize the circle as \(\vec r(t) = \langle 5\cos t, 5\sin t\rangle\), \(0 \le t \le 2\pi\); \(\vec r\,' = \langle -5\sin t, 5\cos t\rangle\). \[ \oint_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^{2\pi}\!\left[5\sin t(-5\sin t) + 25\cos^2 t\cdot 5\cos t\right]dt = -25\pi. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\nabla f\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = z{x^2} + x{\left( {y - 2} \right)^2}\) and \(C\) is the line segment from \(\left( {1,2,0} \right)\) to \(\left( { - 3,10,9} \right)\) followed by the line segment from \(\left( { - 3,10,9} \right)\) to \(\left( {6,0,2} \right)\).
problems.solution: By FTLI, the intermediate point does not matter: only the start \((1,2,0)\) and end \((6,0,2)\) matter. \(f(x,y,z) = zx^2 + x(y-2)^2\). \(f(6,0,2) = 2\cdot 36 + 6\cdot 4 = 72 + 24 = 96\); \(f(1,2,0) = 0 + 1\cdot 0 = 0\). \[ \int_C \nabla f\cdot d\vec r = 96 - 0 = 96. \]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\nabla f\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = {x^3}\left( {3 - {y^2}} \right) + 4y\) and C is given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {3 - {t^2},5 - t} \right\rangle \) with \( - 2 \le t \le 3\).

Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\nabla f\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where \(f\left( {x,y} \right) = y{{\bf{e}}^{{x^{\,2}} - 1}} + 4x\sqrt y \) and C is given by \(\vec r\left( t \right) = \left\langle {1 - t,2{t^2} - 2t} \right\rangle \) with \(0 \le t \le 2\).

Given that \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) is independent of path compute \( \displaystyle \int\limits_{C}{{\vec F\centerdot d\vec r}}\) where C is the ellipse given by \(\displaystyle \frac{{{{\left( {x - 5} \right)}^2}}}{4} + \frac{{{y^2}}}{9} = 1\) with the counter clockwise rotation.
problems.solution: Path independence is equivalent to \(\vec F\) being conservative on a domain containing \(C\), so there is a potential \(f\) with \(\vec F = \nabla f\). The curve \(C\) is a closed ellipse, so its start and end points coincide. \[ \oint_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r = f(\text{end}) - f(\text{start}) = 0. \]

16.6.title: Conservative Vector Fields
16.6.unitTitle: Conservative Fields, Green's, Stokes' & Divergence Theorems

problems.problem: Determine if the vector field is conservative. \(\vec F = \left( {2x{y^3} + {{\bf{e}}^x}\cos \left( y \right)} \right)\vec i + \left( {{{\bf{e}}^x}\sin \left( y \right) - 3{x^2}{y^2}} \right)\vec j\)
problems.solution: With \(P = 2xy^3 + e^x\cos y\) and \(Q = e^x\sin y - 3x^2 y^2\), compute \(P_y\) and \(Q_x\). \[ P_y = 6xy^2 - e^x\sin y, \qquad Q_x = e^x\sin y - 6xy^2. \]These are not equal (in fact they are opposites apart from the algebraic terms), so \(\vec F\) is not conservative.

problems.problem: Determine if the vector field is conservative. \(\vec F = \left( {x{y^2} - 3{y^4} + 2} \right)\vec i + \left( {x{y^2} + {x^2}{y^2} - x} \right)\vec j\)
problems.solution: With \(P = xy^2 - 3y^4 + 2\) and \(Q = xy^2 + x^2 y^2 - x\): \[ P_y = 2xy - 12 y^3, \qquad Q_x = y^2 + 2xy^2 - 1. \]\(P_y \neq Q_x\), so the field is not conservative.

problems.problem: Determine if the vector field is conservative. \(\displaystyle \vec F = \left( {2 + 12x{y^2} - 3{x^2}\sqrt y } \right)\vec i - \left( {\frac{{{x^3}}}{{2\sqrt y }} - 12{x^2}y} \right)\vec j\)
problems.solution: With \(P = 2 + 12xy^2 - 3x^2\sqrt{y}\) and \(Q = -\dfrac{x^3}{2\sqrt y} + 12 x^2 y\): \[ P_y = 24xy - \dfrac{3x^2}{2\sqrt y}, \qquad Q_x = -\dfrac{3x^2}{2\sqrt y} + 24xy. \]They are equal, so \(\vec F\) is conservative on \(\{y > 0\}\). Integrate \(P\) in \(x\): \(f = 2x + 6x^2 y^2 - x^3\sqrt y + g(y)\). Then \(f_y = 12 x^2 y - \dfrac{x^3}{2\sqrt y} + g'(y)\), which matches \(Q\) when \(g'(y) = 0\). \[ f(x,y) = 2x + 6x^2 y^2 - x^3\sqrt{y} + C. \]

problems.problem: Determine if the vector field is conservative. \(\displaystyle \vec F = \left( {8 - \frac{{3{x^2}}}{y} + 5{x^4}{y^2}} \right)\vec i + \left( {6 + \frac{{{x^3}}}{{{y^2}}} - 3{y^2} + 2{x^5}y} \right)\vec j\)
problems.answer: Conservative; potential \(f(x,y) = 8x - \dfrac{x^3}{y} + x^5 y^2 + 6y - y^3 + C\).
problems.solution: \(P = 8 - \dfrac{3x^2}{y} + 5x^4 y^2\), \(Q = 6 + \dfrac{x^3}{y^2} - 3y^2 + 2x^5 y\). \[ P_y = \dfrac{3x^2}{y^2} + 10 x^4 y, \qquad Q_x = \dfrac{3x^2}{y^2} + 10 x^4 y. \]They agree, so \(\vec F\) is conservative on \(\{y \neq 0\}\). Integrate \(P\) in \(x\): \(f = 8x - \dfrac{x^3}{y} + x^5 y^2 + g(y)\); then \(f_y = \dfrac{x^3}{y^2} + 2 x^5 y + g'(y) = Q\) gives \(g'(y) = 6 - 3y^2\), so \(g(y) = 6y - y^3\). \[ f(x,y) = 8x - \frac{x^3}{y} + x^5 y^2 + 6y - y^3 + C. \]

problems.problem: Determine if the vector field is conservative. \(\vec F = \left( {{x^3} - 4x{y^2} + 2} \right)\vec i + \left( {6x - 7y + {x^3}{y^3}} \right)\vec j\)
problems.solution: With \(P = x^3 - 4xy^2 + 2\), \(Q = 6x - 7y + x^3 y^3\): \[ P_y = -8xy, \qquad Q_x = 6 + 3x^2 y^3. \]\(P_y \neq Q_x\), so the field is not conservative.

problems.problem: Determine if the vector field is conservative. \(\vec F = \left( {2x\sin \left( {2y} \right) - 3{y^2}} \right)\vec i + \left( {2 - 6xy + 2{x^2}\cos \left( {2y} \right)} \right)\vec j\)
problems.solution: \(P = 2x\sin(2y) - 3y^2\), \(Q = 2 - 6xy + 2x^2\cos(2y)\). \[ P_y = 4x\cos(2y) - 6y, \qquad Q_x = -6y + 4x\cos(2y). \]They match, so \(\vec F\) is conservative on \(\mathbb{R}^2\). Integrate \(P\) in \(x\): \(f = x^2\sin(2y) - 3xy^2 + g(y)\); then \(f_y = 2x^2\cos(2y) - 6xy + g'(y) = Q\) gives \(g'(y) = 2\), so \(g(y) = 2y\). \[ f(x,y) = x^2\sin(2y) - 3xy^2 + 2y + C. \]

problems.problem: Determine if the vector field is conservative. \(\vec F = \left( {6 - 2xy + {y^3}} \right)\vec i + \left( {{x^2} - 8y + 3x{y^2}} \right)\vec j\)
problems.solution: With \(P = 6 - 2xy + y^3\), \(Q = x^2 - 8y + 3xy^2\): \[ P_y = -2x + 3y^2, \qquad Q_x = 2x + 3y^2. \]They differ (by \(4x\)), so \(\vec F\) is not conservative.

17.1.title: Curl and Divergence
17.1.unitTitle: Conservative Fields, Green's, Stokes' & Divergence Theorems

problems.problem: Compute the curl and divergence of the given vector field. \(\vec F = \left( {2y - \cos \left( x \right)} \right)\,\vec i - {z^2}{{\bf{e}}^{3x}}\vec j + \left( {{x^2} - 7z} \right)\vec k\)
problems.solution: With \(\vec F = \langle P, Q, R\rangle = \langle 2y - \cos x,\, -z^2 e^{3x},\, x^2 - 7z\rangle\), the divergence is the sum of the diagonal partials. \[\operatorname{div}\vec F = \frac{\partial P}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial Q}{\partial y} + \frac{\partial R}{\partial z} = \sin x + 0 - 7 = \sin x - 7.\]For the curl, expand \(\nabla \times \vec F\) as a determinant: \[\operatorname{curl}\vec F = \left\langle \frac{\partial R}{\partial y} - \frac{\partial Q}{\partial z},\, \frac{\partial P}{\partial z} - \frac{\partial R}{\partial x},\, \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\right\rangle = \langle 0 - (-2z e^{3x}),\, 0 - 2x,\, -3z^2 e^{3x} - 2\rangle.\]

problems.problem: Compute the curl and divergence of the given vector field. \(\vec F = - \left( {4y - 1} \right)\,\vec i + x{y^2}\vec j + \left( {x - 3y} \right)\vec k\)
problems.solution: Write \(\vec F = \langle 1 - 4y,\, xy^2,\, x - 3y\rangle\). \[\operatorname{div}\vec F = \frac{\partial}{\partial x}(1-4y) + \frac{\partial}{\partial y}(xy^2) + \frac{\partial}{\partial z}(x-3y) = 0 + 2xy + 0 = 2xy.\]For the curl, \[\operatorname{curl}\vec F = \left\langle \frac{\partial(x-3y)}{\partial y} - \frac{\partial(xy^2)}{\partial z},\, \frac{\partial(1-4y)}{\partial z} - \frac{\partial(x-3y)}{\partial x},\, \frac{\partial(xy^2)}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial(1-4y)}{\partial y}\right\rangle = \langle -3,\, -1,\, y^2 + 4\rangle.\]

problems.problem: Compute the curl and divergence of the given vector field. \(\displaystyle \vec F = {z^2}\left( {y - x} \right)\,\vec i + \frac{{4{y^2}}}{{{z^3}}}\vec j + \left( {{x^2} - 3z} \right)\vec k\)
problems.solution: With \(P = z^2(y-x)\), \(Q = 4y^2/z^3\), \(R = x^2 - 3z\), \[\operatorname{div}\vec F = \frac{\partial P}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial Q}{\partial y} + \frac{\partial R}{\partial z} = -z^2 + \frac{8y}{z^3} - 3.\]The curl components are \[\operatorname{curl}\vec F = \left\langle R_y - Q_z,\, P_z - R_x,\, Q_x - P_y\right\rangle = \left\langle 0 - \left(-\tfrac{12 y^2}{z^4}\right),\, 2z(y-x) - 2x,\, 0 - z^2\right\rangle.\]

problems.problem: Compute the curl and divergence of the given vector field. \(\vec F = {x^2}y\,\vec i - \left( {{z^3} - 3x} \right)\vec j + 4{y^2}\vec k\)
problems.solution: Set \(\vec F = \langle x^2 y,\, 3x - z^3,\, 4y^2\rangle\). The divergence sums the diagonal partials: \[\operatorname{div}\vec F = 2xy + 0 + 0 = 2xy.\]The curl is \[\operatorname{curl}\vec F = \left\langle R_y - Q_z,\, P_z - R_x,\, Q_x - P_y\right\rangle = \langle 8y - (-3z^2),\, 0 - 0,\, 3 - x^2\rangle.\]

problems.problem: Compute the curl and divergence of the given vector field. \(\displaystyle \vec F = \left( {3x + 2{z^2}} \right)\,\vec i + \frac{{{x^3}{y^2}}}{z}\vec j - \left( {z - 7x} \right)\vec k\)
problems.answer: \(\operatorname{curl}\vec F = \left\langle \dfrac{x^3 y^2}{z^2},\, 4z - 7,\, \dfrac{3 x^2 y^2}{z}\right\rangle\), \(\operatorname{div}\vec F = 2 + \dfrac{2 x^3 y}{z}\)
problems.solution: Rewrite \(\vec F = \langle 3x + 2z^2,\, x^3 y^2/z,\, 7x - z\rangle\). Then \[\operatorname{div}\vec F = 3 + \frac{2 x^3 y}{z} + (-1) = 2 + \frac{2 x^3 y}{z}.\]For the curl, computing the three components gives \[\operatorname{curl}\vec F = \left\langle 0 + \frac{x^3 y^2}{z^2},\, 4z - 7,\, \frac{3 x^2 y^2}{z} - 0\right\rangle.\]

17.2.title: Parametric Surfaces
17.2.unitTitle: Conservative Fields, Green's, Stokes' & Divergence Theorems

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The plane containing the three points \(\left( {1,4, - 2} \right)\), \(\left( { - 3,0,1} \right)\) and \(\left( {2,4, - 5} \right)\).
problems.solution: For a plane, pick a base point and two direction vectors that lie in the plane. Take \(P_0 = (1,4,-2)\). Set \(\vec a = (-3,0,1) - (1,4,-2) = \langle -4,-4,3\rangle\) and \(\vec b = (2,4,-5) - (1,4,-2) = \langle 1,0,-3\rangle\). \[\vec r(u,v) = P_0 + u\,\vec a + v\,\vec b = \langle 1 - 4u + v,\, 4 - 4u,\, -2 + 3u - 3v\rangle, \quad (u,v) \in \mathbb{R}^2.\]

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The portion of the plane \(x + 9y + 3z = 8\) that lies in the 1 st octant.
problems.answer: \(\vec r(x,y) = \left\langle x,\, y,\, \dfrac{8 - x - 9y}{3}\right\rangle\) on \(x \ge 0,\, y \ge 0,\, x + 9y \le 8\)
problems.solution: Solve the plane for \(z\): \(z = (8 - x - 9y)/3\). Use \(x\) and \(y\) as parameters. The first-octant constraints \(x,y,z \ge 0\) force \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\), and \(x + 9y \le 8\). \[\vec r(x,y) = \left\langle x,\, y,\, \frac{8 - x - 9y}{3}\right\rangle, \quad x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0,\ x + 9y \le 8.\]

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The portion of \(x = 2{y^2} + 2{z^2} - 7\) that is behind \(x = 5\).
problems.solution: The surface opens in the \(+x\) direction with vertex at \(x=-7\). \"Behind \(x=5\)\" means \(x \le 5\), i.e. \(2y^2 + 2z^2 - 7 \le 5\), so \(y^2 + z^2 \le 6\). Use polar coordinates in the \(yz\)-plane: \(y = r\cos\theta\), \(z = r\sin\theta\). \[\vec r(r,\theta) = \langle 2r^2 - 7,\, r\cos\theta,\, r\sin\theta\rangle, \quad 0 \le r \le \sqrt{6},\ 0 \le \theta \le 2\pi.\]

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The portion of \(y = 10 - 3{x^2} - 3{z^2}\) that is in front of the \(xz\)-plane.
problems.solution: The paraboloid opens in the \(-y\) direction with vertex \((0,10,0)\). \"In front of the \(xz\)-plane\" means \(y \ge 0\), so \(10 - 3x^2 - 3z^2 \ge 0\) and \(x^2 + z^2 \le 10/3\). Use polar in the \(xz\)-plane: \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(z = r\sin\theta\). \[\vec r(r,\theta) = \langle r\cos\theta,\, 10 - 3r^2,\, r\sin\theta\rangle, \quad 0 \le r \le \sqrt{10/3},\ 0 \le \theta \le 2\pi.\]

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The cylinder \({x^2} + {z^2} = 121\).
problems.solution: This is a cylinder of radius 11 with axis along the \(y\)-axis. Parametrize the circular cross section by an angle and let \(y\) range freely. \[\vec r(y,\theta) = \langle 11\cos\theta,\, y,\, 11\sin\theta\rangle, \quad y \in \mathbb{R},\ 0 \le \theta \le 2\pi.\]

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The cylinder \({y^2} + {z^2} = 6\) for \(2 \le x \le 9\).
problems.solution: Cylinder of radius \(\sqrt{6}\) along the \(x\)-axis. Use \(x\) and the polar angle \(\theta\) in the \(yz\)-plane. \[\vec r(x,\theta) = \langle x,\, \sqrt{6}\cos\theta,\, \sqrt{6}\sin\theta\rangle, \quad 2 \le x \le 9,\ 0 \le \theta \le 2\pi.\]

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The sphere \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 17\).
problems.solution: Use spherical coordinates with fixed radius \(\rho = \sqrt{17}\). \[\vec r(\varphi,\theta) = \langle \sqrt{17}\sin\varphi\cos\theta,\, \sqrt{17}\sin\varphi\sin\theta,\, \sqrt{17}\cos\varphi\rangle, \quad 0 \le \varphi \le \pi,\ 0 \le \theta \le 2\pi.\]

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The portion of the sphere of radius 3 with \(y \ge 0\) and \(z \le 0\).
problems.solution: Use spherical coordinates with \(\rho = 3\). Lower hemisphere \(z \le 0\) gives \(\cos\varphi \le 0\), so \(\pi/2 \le \varphi \le \pi\). The half \(y \ge 0\) gives \(\sin\theta \ge 0\), so \(0 \le \theta \le \pi\). \[\vec r(\varphi,\theta) = \langle 3\sin\varphi\cos\theta,\, 3\sin\varphi\sin\theta,\, 3\cos\varphi\rangle, \quad \pi/2 \le \varphi \le \pi,\ 0 \le \theta \le \pi.\]

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The tangent plane to the surface given by the following parametric equation at the point \(\left( { - 5,4, - 12} \right)\). \(\vec r\left( {u,v} \right) = \left( {u + 2v} \right)\vec i + \left( {{u^2} + 3} \right)\vec j - 3{v^2}\vec k\)
problems.solution: Find the parameter values: \(u + 2v = -5\), \(u^2 + 3 = 4\), \(-3v^2 = -12\). The middle gives \(u = \pm 1\); pairing with the first and third forces \(u = -1,\, v = -2\). Compute partials: \(\vec r_u = \langle 1, 2u, 0\rangle = \langle 1, -2, 0\rangle\) and \(\vec r_v = \langle 2, 0, -6v\rangle = \langle 2, 0, 12\rangle\). \[\vec r_u \times \vec r_v = \langle (-2)(12) - 0,\, -(1)(12) + 0,\, 0 - (-2)(2)\rangle = \langle -24,\, -12,\, 4\rangle.\]The tangent plane is \(-24(x+5) - 12(y-4) + 4(z+12) = 0\), which simplifies to \(6x + 3y - z = -6\).

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The tangent plane to the surface given by the following parametric equation at the point \(\left( {1, - 11,19} \right)\). \(\vec r\left( {u,v} \right) = \left\langle {{{\bf{e}}^{6 - 2v}},{u^2} - 15,1 - u{v^2}} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Find \((u,v)\): \(e^{6-2v} = 1 \Rightarrow v = 3\); \(u^2 = 4\); \(1 - uv^2 = 19 \Rightarrow u = -2\) (which is consistent with \(u^2 = 4\)). Then \(\vec r_u = \langle 0,\, 2u,\, -v^2\rangle = \langle 0,\, -4,\, -9\rangle\) and \(\vec r_v = \langle -2 e^{6-2v},\, 0,\, -2uv\rangle = \langle -2,\, 0,\, 12\rangle\). \[\vec r_u \times \vec r_v = \langle (-4)(12) - 0,\, -(0 - 18),\, 0 - 8\rangle = \langle -48,\, 18,\, -8\rangle.\]The tangent plane: \(-48(x-1) + 18(y+11) - 8(z-19) = 0\), i.e. \(24x - 9y + 4z = 199\).

problems.problem: Determine the surface area of the portion of \(3x + 3y + 4z = 16\) that is in the 1 st octant.
problems.solution: Solve for \(z = (16 - 3x - 3y)/4\), so \(z_x = -3/4\) and \(z_y = -3/4\). The surface area element is \[dS = \sqrt{1 + z_x^2 + z_y^2}\, dA = \sqrt{1 + 9/16 + 9/16}\, dA = \frac{\sqrt{34}}{4}\, dA.\]The first-octant projection in the \(xy\)-plane is the triangle \(x \ge 0,\, y \ge 0,\, x + y \le 16/3\), with area \(\tfrac{1}{2}(16/3)^2 = 128/9\). \[\text{SA} = \frac{\sqrt{34}}{4} \cdot \frac{128}{9} = \frac{32\sqrt{34}}{9}.\]

problems.problem: Determine the surface area of the portion of \(x + 4y + 8z = 4\) that is inside the cylinder \({x^2} + {y^2} = 16\).
problems.solution: From \(z = (4 - x - 4y)/8\), \(z_x = -1/8\) and \(z_y = -1/2\). \[dS = \sqrt{1 + \tfrac{1}{64} + \tfrac{1}{4}}\, dA = \sqrt{\tfrac{81}{64}}\, dA = \tfrac{9}{8}\, dA.\]The projection onto the \(xy\)-plane is the disk \(x^2 + y^2 \le 16\) with area \(16\pi\). Therefore \(\text{SA} = (9/8)(16\pi) = 18\pi\).

problems.problem: Determine the surface area of the portion of \(z = 6y + 2{x^2}\) that is above the triangle in the \(xy\)-plane with vertices \(\left( {0,0} \right)\), \(\left( {8,0} \right)\) and \(\left( {8,2} \right)\).
problems.solution: With \(z = 6y + 2x^2\), \(z_x = 4x\) and \(z_y = 6\), so \(dS = \sqrt{1 + 16x^2 + 36}\, dA = \sqrt{37 + 16x^2}\, dA\). The triangle has \(0 \le x \le 8\) and \(0 \le y \le x/4\). \[\text{SA} = \int_0^8 \int_0^{x/4} \sqrt{37 + 16x^2}\, dy\, dx = \int_0^8 \frac{x}{4}\sqrt{37 + 16x^2}\, dx.\]Substitute \(u = 37 + 16x^2\), \(du = 32x\, dx\): the integral becomes \(\tfrac{1}{128}\int_{37}^{1061} \sqrt{u}\, du = \tfrac{1}{192}\left(1061^{3/2} - 37^{3/2}\right)\).

problems.problem: Determine the surface area of the portion of \(x = 6 - {y^2} - {z^2}\) that is in front of \(x = 2\) with \(y \ge 0\).
problems.solution: \"In front of \(x = 2\)\" means \(x \ge 2\), so \(6 - y^2 - z^2 \ge 2\) i.e. \(y^2 + z^2 \le 4\). With \(x = 6 - y^2 - z^2\), \(x_y = -2y\) and \(x_z = -2z\), giving \(dS = \sqrt{1 + 4y^2 + 4z^2}\, dA\). Use polar in the \(yz\)-plane (with \(y \ge 0\) restricting \(\theta \in [-\pi/2, \pi/2]\)): \[\text{SA} = \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\!\int_0^2 r\sqrt{1+4r^2}\, dr\, d\theta = \pi \cdot \frac{1}{12}(1+4r^2)^{3/2}\Big|_0^2 = \frac{\pi}{12}(17^{3/2} - 1).\]

problems.problem: Determine the surface area of the portion of \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 11\) with \(x \ge 0\), \(y \le 0\) and \(z \ge 0\).
problems.solution: The sphere of radius \(\sqrt{11}\) has total surface area \(4\pi(\sqrt{11})^2 = 44\pi\). The constraints \(x \ge 0,\, y \le 0,\, z \ge 0\) pick out one octant (one eighth of the sphere). \[\text{SA} = \frac{44\pi}{8} = \frac{11\pi}{2}.\]

problems.problem: Determine the surface area of the portion of the surface given by the following parametric equation that lies above the triangle in the \(uv\)-plane with vertices\(\left( {0,0} \right)\), \(\left( {10,2} \right)\) and \(\left( {0,2} \right)\). \(\vec r\left( {u,v} \right) = \left\langle {{v^2},3v,2u} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: Compute \(\vec r_u = \langle 0, 0, 2\rangle\) and \(\vec r_v = \langle 2v, 3, 0\rangle\), so \[\vec r_u \times \vec r_v = \langle -6,\, 4v,\, 0\rangle, \qquad |\vec r_u \times \vec r_v| = 2\sqrt{9 + 4v^2}.\]The triangle has vertices \((0,0),(10,2),(0,2)\); the line from \((0,0)\) to \((10,2)\) is \(u = 5v\). For \(0 \le v \le 2\), \(u\) runs \(0\) to \(5v\). \[\text{SA} = \int_0^2 \int_0^{5v} 2\sqrt{9 + 4v^2}\, du\, dv = \int_0^2 10v\sqrt{9 + 4v^2}\, dv = \frac{5}{6}(9 + 4v^2)^{3/2}\Big|_0^2 = \frac{5}{6}(125 - 27) = \frac{245}{3}.\]

problems.problem: Determine the surface area of the portion of the surface given by the following parametric equation that lies above the region in the \(uv\)-plane bounded by \(\displaystyle v = \frac{3}{2}{u^2}\), \(u = 2\) and the \(u\)-axis. \(\vec r\left( {u,v} \right) = \left\langle {uv,3uv,v} \right\rangle \)
problems.solution: With \(\vec r_u = \langle v, 3v, 0\rangle\) and \(\vec r_v = \langle u, 3u, 1\rangle\), \[\vec r_u \times \vec r_v = \langle 3v,\, -v,\, 0\rangle, \qquad |\vec r_u \times \vec r_v| = v\sqrt{10}\quad(v \ge 0).\]The region is \(0 \le u \le 2\), \(0 \le v \le \tfrac{3}{2}u^2\). \[\text{SA} = \sqrt{10}\int_0^2 \int_0^{3u^2/2} v\, dv\, du = \sqrt{10}\int_0^2 \tfrac{1}{2}\left(\tfrac{3u^2}{2}\right)^2 du = \frac{9\sqrt{10}}{8}\cdot\frac{32}{5} = \frac{36\sqrt{10}}{5}.\]

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The plane \(7x + 3y + 4z = 15\).
problems.solution: Solve for \(z\): \(z = (15 - 7x - 3y)/4\). Use \(x\) and \(y\) as parameters with no restriction. \[\vec r(x,y) = \left\langle x,\, y,\, \frac{15 - 7x - 3y}{4}\right\rangle, \quad (x,y) \in \mathbb{R}^2.\]

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The portion of the plane \(7x + 3y + 4z = 15\) that lies in the 1 st octant.
problems.solution: With \(z = (15 - 7x - 3y)/4\), the first-octant constraints \(x,y,z \ge 0\) reduce to \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\), and \(7x + 3y \le 15\). \[\vec r(x,y) = \left\langle x,\, y,\, \frac{15 - 7x - 3y}{4}\right\rangle, \quad x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0,\ 7x + 3y \le 15.\]

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The cylinder \({x^2} + {y^2} = 5\) for \( - 1 \le z \le 6\).
problems.solution: Cylinder of radius \(\sqrt{5}\) along the \(z\)-axis. \[\vec r(z,\theta) = \langle \sqrt{5}\cos\theta,\, \sqrt{5}\sin\theta,\, z\rangle, \quad -1 \le z \le 6,\ 0 \le \theta \le 2\pi.\]

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The portion of \(y = 4 - {x^2} - {z^2}\) that is in front of \(y = - 6\).
problems.solution: \"In front of \(y = -6\)\" means \(y \ge -6\), so \(4 - x^2 - z^2 \ge -6\), giving \(x^2 + z^2 \le 10\). Use polar in the \(xz\)-plane: \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(z = r\sin\theta\). \[\vec r(r,\theta) = \langle r\cos\theta,\, 4 - r^2,\, r\sin\theta\rangle, \quad 0 \le r \le \sqrt{10},\ 0 \le \theta \le 2\pi.\]

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The portion of the sphere of radius 6 with \(x \ge 0\).
problems.solution: Sphere of radius 6. \(x \ge 0\) requires \(\cos\theta \ge 0\), i.e. \(\theta \in [-\pi/2, \pi/2]\); \(\varphi\) ranges over the full \([0, \pi]\). \[\vec r(\varphi,\theta) = \langle 6\sin\varphi\cos\theta,\, 6\sin\varphi\sin\theta,\, 6\cos\varphi\rangle, \quad 0 \le \varphi \le \pi,\ -\tfrac{\pi}{2} \le \theta \le \tfrac{\pi}{2}.\]

problems.problem: Give a parametrization of the given surface. The tangent plane to the surface given by the following parametric equation at the point \(\left( {8,14,2} \right)\). \(\vec r\left( {u,v} \right) = \left( {{u^2} + 2u} \right)\vec i + \left( {3v - 2u} \right)\vec j + \left( {6v - 10} \right)\vec k\)
problems.solution: Solve for \((u,v)\): \(6v - 10 = 2 \Rightarrow v = 2\); \(3v - 2u = 14 \Rightarrow u = -4\); check \(u^2 + 2u = 16 - 8 = 8\) ✓. Then \(\vec r_u = \langle 2u+2, -2, 0\rangle = \langle -6, -2, 0\rangle\) and \(\vec r_v = \langle 0, 3, 6\rangle\). \[\vec r_u \times \vec r_v = \langle -12,\, 36,\, -18\rangle.\]The tangent plane: \(-12(x-8) + 36(y-14) - 18(z-2) = 0\), or \(2x - 6y + 3z = -62\).

problems.problem: Determine the surface area of the portion of \(2x + 3y + 6z = 9\) that is inside the cylinder \({x^2} + {y^2} = 7\).
problems.solution: From \(z = (9 - 2x - 3y)/6\), \(z_x = -1/3\) and \(z_y = -1/2\). \[dS = \sqrt{1 + \tfrac{1}{9} + \tfrac{1}{4}}\, dA = \sqrt{\tfrac{49}{36}}\, dA = \tfrac{7}{6}\, dA.\]The projection is the disk \(x^2 + y^2 \le 7\) with area \(7\pi\), so \(\text{SA} = (7/6)(7\pi) = 49\pi/6\).

problems.problem: Determine the surface area of the portion of \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 25\) with \(z \le 0\).
problems.solution: The full sphere of radius 5 has surface area \(4\pi(25) = 100\pi\). The lower hemisphere is half of that. \[\text{SA} = 50\pi.\]

problems.problem: Determine the surface area of the portion of \(z = 3 + 2y + \frac{1}{4}{x^4}\) that is above the region in the \(xy\)-plane bounded by \(y = {x^5}\), \(x = 1\) and the \(x\)-axis.
problems.solution: With \(z = 3 + 2y + \tfrac{1}{4}x^4\), \(z_x = x^3\) and \(z_y = 2\), so \(dS = \sqrt{1 + x^6 + 4}\, dA = \sqrt{5 + x^6}\, dA\). The region is \(0 \le x \le 1\), \(0 \le y \le x^5\). \[\text{SA} = \int_0^1 \int_0^{x^5} \sqrt{5 + x^6}\, dy\, dx = \int_0^1 x^5 \sqrt{5 + x^6}\, dx.\]Let \(u = 5 + x^6\); the integral becomes \(\tfrac{1}{6}\int_5^6 \sqrt{u}\, du = \tfrac{1}{9}(6^{3/2} - 5^{3/2})\).

17.3.title: Surface Integrals
17.3.unitTitle: Conservative Fields, Green's, Stokes' & Divergence Theorems

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{2x - 3y + z\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the portion of \(x + y + z = 2\) that is in the 1 st octant.
problems.solution: Solve \(z = 2 - x - y\); then \(z_x = z_y = -1\), so \(dS = \sqrt{3}\, dA\). The first-octant projection is the triangle \(x,y \ge 0,\, x + y \le 2\), and the integrand becomes \(2x - 3y + (2 - x - y) = x - 4y + 2\). \[I = \sqrt{3}\int_0^2 \int_0^{2-x}(x - 4y + 2)\, dy\, dx = \sqrt{3}\int_0^2 \big[(x+2)(2-x) - 2(2-x)^2\big]\, dx.\]Expanding gives \(-3x^2 + 8x - 4\); integrating from 0 to 2 yields \(-8 + 16 - 8 = 0\). So \(I = 0\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{x + {y^2} + {z^2}\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the portion of \(x = 4 - {y^2} - {z^2}\) that lies in front of \(x = - 2\).
problems.solution: Parametrize by \((y,z)\): \(\vec r = \langle 4 - y^2 - z^2,\, y,\, z\rangle\). Then \(\vec r_y \times \vec r_z = \langle 1, 2y, 2z\rangle\) and \(|\vec r_y \times \vec r_z| = \sqrt{1 + 4y^2 + 4z^2}\). On \(S\), the integrand simplifies: \(x + y^2 + z^2 = (4 - y^2 - z^2) + y^2 + z^2 = 4\). The region \(D\) is \(y^2 + z^2 \le 6\). \[I = 4\iint_D \sqrt{1+4y^2+4z^2}\, dA = 4\int_0^{2\pi}\!\int_0^{\sqrt 6} r\sqrt{1+4r^2}\, dr\, d\theta = 8\pi \cdot \frac{1}{12}(25^{3/2} - 1) = \frac{248\pi}{3}.\]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{6\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the portion of \(y = 4z + {x^3} + 6\) that lies over the region in the xz-plane with bounded by \(z = {x^3}\), \(x = 1\) and the \(x\)-axis.
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{xyz\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the portion of \({x^2} + {y^2} = 36\) between \(z = - 3\) and \(z = 1\).
problems.solution: Parametrize the cylinder by \(\vec r(\theta, z) = \langle 6\cos\theta, 6\sin\theta, z\rangle\) with \(\theta \in [0, 2\pi]\) and \(z \in [-3, 1]\). Then \(|\vec r_\theta \times \vec r_z| = 6\), so \(dS = 6\, d\theta\, dz\). The integrand is \(xyz = 36 z\sin\theta\cos\theta = 18 z\sin(2\theta)\). \[I = \int_{-3}^1 \int_0^{2\pi} 18 z\sin(2\theta)\cdot 6\, d\theta\, dz = 108\int_{-3}^1 z\, dz \int_0^{2\pi}\sin(2\theta)\, d\theta = 0,\]since \(\int_0^{2\pi}\sin(2\theta)\, d\theta = 0\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{{z^2} + x\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the portion of \({x^2} + {y^2} + {z^2} = 4\) with \(z \ge 0\).
problems.solution: Parametrize the upper hemisphere of radius 2 by \(\vec r(\varphi,\theta) = \langle 2\sin\varphi\cos\theta, 2\sin\varphi\sin\theta, 2\cos\varphi\rangle\) with \(\varphi \in [0, \pi/2]\), \(\theta \in [0, 2\pi]\); \(dS = 4\sin\varphi\, d\varphi\, d\theta\). The integrand is \(z^2 + x = 4\cos^2\varphi + 2\sin\varphi\cos\theta\). \[I = \int_0^{2\pi}\!\int_0^{\pi/2}\!(4\cos^2\varphi + 2\sin\varphi\cos\theta)\cdot 4\sin\varphi\, d\varphi\, d\theta.\]The \(\cos\theta\) piece integrates to 0 over \([0, 2\pi]\). The remaining piece is \(16 \cdot 2\pi \cdot \int_0^{\pi/2}\cos^2\varphi\sin\varphi\, d\varphi = 32\pi \cdot \tfrac{1}{3} = \tfrac{32\pi}{3}\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{4y\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the portion of \({x^2} + {z^2} = 9\) between \(y = 2\) and \(y = 10 - x\).
problems.solution: Parametrize the cylinder by \(\vec r(\theta, y) = \langle 3\cos\theta, y, 3\sin\theta\rangle\). Then \(|\vec r_\theta \times \vec r_y| = 3\), so \(dS = 3\, d\theta\, dy\), and on \(S\) the bounds are \(2 \le y \le 10 - 3\cos\theta\). \[I = \int_0^{2\pi}\!\int_2^{10 - 3\cos\theta} 4y\cdot 3\, dy\, d\theta = 6\int_0^{2\pi}\big[(10 - 3\cos\theta)^2 - 4\big]\, d\theta.\]Expanding gives \(96 - 60\cos\theta + 9\cos^2\theta\); integrating over \([0, 2\pi]\) gives \(192\pi + 0 + 9\pi = 201\pi\). So \(I = 6\cdot 201\pi = 1206\pi\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{z + 3\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the surface of the solid bounded by \(z = 2{x^2} + 2{y^2} - 3\) and \(z = 1\). Note that both surfaces of this solid are included in \(S\).
problems.solution: The surface has two pieces. The cap \(z = 1\) is a disk of radius \(\sqrt{2}\) (where \(2x^2 + 2y^2 - 3 = 1\)); the integrand is \(z + 3 = 4\), so the cap contributes \(4 \cdot 2\pi = 8\pi\). On the paraboloid, \(z_x = 4x\), \(z_y = 4y\), so \(dS = \sqrt{1 + 16(x^2+y^2)}\, dA\); using polar with \(\rho \in [0, \sqrt 2]\) and \(z + 3 = 2\rho^2\), \[I_{\text{par}} = 4\pi\int_0^{\sqrt 2} \rho^3\sqrt{1 + 16\rho^2}\, d\rho.\]With \(u = 1 + 16\rho^2\) this becomes \(\tfrac{\pi}{128}\int_1^{33}(u^{3/2} - u^{1/2})\, du = \tfrac{\pi}{64}\big(\tfrac{33^{5/2}}{5} - \tfrac{33^{3/2}}{3} + \tfrac{2}{15}\big)\). Adding gives the result.

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{z\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the surface of the solid bounded by \({y^2} + {z^2} = 4\), \(x = y - 3\), and \(x = 6 - z\). Note that all three surfaces of this solid are included in \(S\).
problems.solution: The solid is a cylinder \(y^2 + z^2 \le 4\) of finite length, capped by the planes \(x = y - 3\) and \(x = 6 - z\). On either plane, the disk is \(y^2 + z^2 \le 4\), which is symmetric in \(z\), so \(\iint z\, dS = 0\) on each cap. For the cylindrical side, parametrize by \(\vec r(\theta, x) = \langle x, 2\cos\theta, 2\sin\theta\rangle\) with \(2\cos\theta - 3 \le x \le 6 - 2\sin\theta\) and \(dS = 2\, dx\, d\theta\): \[I_{\text{side}} = \int_0^{2\pi}\!\int_{2\cos\theta-3}^{6-2\sin\theta} 2\sin\theta\cdot 2\, dx\, d\theta = 8\int_0^{2\pi}\sin\theta\,(9 - 2\sin\theta - 2\cos\theta)\, d\theta = 8(-2\pi) = -16\pi.\]So \(I = -16\pi\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{4 + z\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the portion of the sphere of radius 1 with \(z \ge 0\) and \(x \le 0\). Note that all three surfaces of this solid are included in \(S\).
problems.solution: Parametrize the unit sphere by \(\vec r(\varphi, \theta)\) with \(dS = \sin\varphi\, d\varphi\, d\theta\). \(z \ge 0\) gives \(\varphi \in [0, \pi/2]\); \(x \le 0\) gives \(\theta \in [\pi/2, 3\pi/2]\). On \(S\), \(z = \cos\varphi\). \[I = \int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}\!\int_0^{\pi/2}(4 + \cos\varphi)\sin\varphi\, d\varphi\, d\theta = \pi\left(4 + \tfrac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{9\pi}{2}.\]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{z + 3y - {x^2}\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the portion of \(z = 2 - 3y + {x^2}\) that lies over the triangle in the \(xy\)-plane with vertices \(\left( {0,0} \right)\), \(\left( {2,0} \right)\) and \(\left( {2, - 4} \right)\).
Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{40y\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the portion of \(y = 3{x^2} + 3{z^2}\) that lies behind \(y = 6\).
problems.solution: \"Behind \(y = 6\)\" gives \(3x^2 + 3z^2 \le 6\) i.e. \(x^2 + z^2 \le 2\). With \(y = 3x^2 + 3z^2\), \(dS = \sqrt{1 + 36(x^2 + z^2)}\, dA\). In polar (in the \(xz\)-plane), \(\rho \in [0, \sqrt 2]\) and \(40y = 120\rho^2\). \[I = \int_0^{2\pi}\!\int_0^{\sqrt 2} 120\rho^2\sqrt{1 + 36\rho^2}\cdot \rho\, d\rho\, d\theta = 240\pi \int_0^{\sqrt 2}\rho^3\sqrt{1 + 36\rho^2}\, d\rho.\]Substituting \(u = 1 + 36\rho^2\) yields \(\tfrac{5\pi}{27}\big(\tfrac{73^{5/2}}{5} - \tfrac{73^{3/2}}{3} + \tfrac{2}{15}\big)\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{2y\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the portion of \({y^2} + {z^2} = 4\) between \(x = 0\) and \(x = 3 - z\).
problems.solution: Parametrize the cylinder by \(\vec r(\theta, x) = \langle x, 2\cos\theta, 2\sin\theta\rangle\) with \(dS = 2\, dx\, d\theta\). The integrand is \(2y = 4\cos\theta\), and \(x \in [0, 3 - 2\sin\theta]\). \[I = \int_0^{2\pi}\!\int_0^{3 - 2\sin\theta} 4\cos\theta\cdot 2\, dx\, d\theta = 8\int_0^{2\pi}\cos\theta\,(3 - 2\sin\theta)\, d\theta = 0,\]since both \(\int\cos\theta\, d\theta\) and \(\int\sin\theta\cos\theta\, d\theta\) vanish over \([0, 2\pi]\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{xz\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the portion of the sphere of radius 3 with \(x \le 0\), \(y \ge 0\) and \(z \ge 0\).
problems.solution: With sphere \(\vec r = 3\langle \sin\varphi\cos\theta, \sin\varphi\sin\theta, \cos\varphi\rangle\), \(dS = 9\sin\varphi\, d\varphi\, d\theta\). The octant \(x\le 0, y\ge 0, z\ge 0\) gives \(\varphi \in [0,\pi/2]\), \(\theta \in [\pi/2, \pi]\). On \(S\), \(xz = 9\sin\varphi\cos\theta\cos\varphi = \tfrac{9}{2}\sin(2\varphi)\cos\theta\). \[I = \frac{81}{2}\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi}\cos\theta\, d\theta \int_0^{\pi/2}\sin(2\varphi)\sin\varphi\, d\varphi = \frac{81}{2}(-1)\cdot \frac{2}{3} = -27.\]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{yz + 4xy\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the surface of the solid bounded by \(4x + 2y + z = 8\), \(z = 0\), \(y = 0\) and \(x = 0\). Note that all four surfaces of this solid are included in \(S\).
problems.solution: The tetrahedron has four faces. With the integrand \(y(z + 4x)\): on \(y=0\) the integrand vanishes; on \(z = 0\), \(\iint_{T_1} 4xy\, dA = 32/3\) (where \(T_1\) is the triangle \(4x + 2y \le 8\) in the \(xy\)-plane); on \(x = 0\), \(\iint_{T_2} yz\, dA = 128/3\). On the slanted plane \(z = 8 - 4x - 2y\), \(dS = \sqrt{21}\, dA\) and the integrand becomes \(y(8 - 2y)\): \[\sqrt{21}\int_0^2\!\int_0^{4-2x}(8y - 2y^2)\, dy\, dx = \frac{64\sqrt{21}}{3}.\]Summing: \(I = \tfrac{32}{3} + 0 + \tfrac{128}{3} + \tfrac{64\sqrt{21}}{3} = \tfrac{160 + 64\sqrt{21}}{3}\).

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{x - z\,dS}}\) where \(S\) is the surface of the solid bounded by \({x^2} + {y^2} = 4\), \(z = x - 3\), and \(z = x + 2\). Note that all three surfaces of this solid are included in \(S\).
problems.solution: The solid is the cylinder \(x^2 + y^2 \le 4\) capped by the planes \(z = x - 3\) and \(z = x + 2\). On the cylinder side with \(x = 2\cos\theta\), \(y = 2\sin\theta\), \(z\) runs from \(2\cos\theta - 3\) to \(2\cos\theta + 2\); the \(z\)-integral of \(x - z\) over a length-5 interval centered (in average) at \(z\)-mean \(2\cos\theta - \tfrac{1}{2}\) gives \(5(2\cos\theta) - 5(2\cos\theta - \tfrac{1}{2}) = \tfrac{5}{2}\) per unit \(d\theta\). With \(dS = 2\, dz\, d\theta\), \(I_{\text{side}} = \int_0^{2\pi} 5\, d\theta = 10\pi\). \[I_{\text{cap}_{z=x-3}} = 3\cdot\sqrt 2\cdot 4\pi = 12\sqrt 2\,\pi,\qquad I_{\text{cap}_{z=x+2}} = -2\cdot\sqrt 2\cdot 4\pi = -8\sqrt 2\,\pi.\]Total \(I = 10\pi + 4\sqrt 2\,\pi = (10 + 4\sqrt 2)\pi\).

17.4.title: Surface Integrals of Vector Fields
17.4.unitTitle: Conservative Fields, Green's, Stokes' & Divergence Theorems

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{\vec F\centerdot \,d\vec S}}\) where \(\vec F = \left( {z - y} \right)\,\vec i + x\,\vec j + 4y\,\vec k\) and \(S\) is the portion of \(x + y + z = 2\) that is in the 1st octant oriented in the positive \(z\)-axis direction.
problems.solution: With \(z = 2 - x - y\), parametrize by \((x,y)\): \(\vec r_x \times \vec r_y = \langle 1, 1, 1\rangle\), which has positive \(z\)-component, matching the requested orientation. Then \[\vec F \cdot (\vec r_x \times \vec r_y) = (z - y) + x + 4y = x + 3y + z = 2y + 2.\]Over the triangle \(x, y \ge 0,\, x + y \le 2\), \[I = \int_0^2 \int_0^{2-x}(2y + 2)\, dy\, dx = \int_0^2 (2-x)(4-x)\, dx = \frac{20}{3}.\]

problems.problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \iint\limits_{S}{{\vec F\centerdot \,d\vec S}}\) where \(\vec F = \left( {x - 4} \right)\,\vec i + z\,\vec j - y\,\vec k\) and \(S\) is the portion of \(x = 4 - {y^2} - {z^2}\) that lies in front of \(x = - 2\) oriented in the negative \(x\)-axis direction.
